# Moss Inference

> Run optimized LLM inference alongside retrieval on the same host, delivering sub-200ms inference latency so your agent can start responding sooner.

**Sub-200ms time to first token, with retrieval built in.**

Moss Inference is a low-latency inference API built for real-time AI agents. It brings optimized model inference and context retrieval together, enabling agents to start responding in under 200ms on supported fast-lane workloads.

Run Moss's optimized inference model or access models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other providers through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Ground responses in your Moss indexes without building or managing a separate retrieval pipeline.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Private beta:** Moss Inference is currently in private beta. [Request access through the Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev/).

## Why Moss Inference?

Traditional AI applications retrieve context and generate responses through separate systems. Even after retrieving the right information, an agent still needs to send that context to an LLM and wait for generation to begin.

Moss Inference brings retrieval and generation closer together, reducing the overhead between finding relevant information and generating a response.

### Sub-200ms time to first token

Start generating responses in under 200ms with Moss's optimized inference model on supported workloads. Built for applications where response latency matters, including conversational AI, interactive agents, and real-time workflows.

### Retrieval and inference, colocated

Moss runs its optimized inference model alongside its retrieval runtime, allowing relevant context to be retrieved and used without a separate network round trip between the retrieval and generation systems.

Specify a Moss index in your inference request, and Moss retrieves relevant context to ground the model's response.

### One OpenAI-compatible API

Access Moss's optimized model and supported third-party models through a single endpoint.

Use the OpenAI-compatible Responses API, with an optional `indexes` parameter to enable context retrieval. You can use Moss for inference alone or combine it with your existing Moss indexes.

## How Moss Inference works

Moss Inference combines context retrieval and model execution into a single request.

1. **Send a request.** Your agent calls the Moss Inference API, specifying a model and optionally one or more Moss indexes.
2. **Retrieve relevant context.** When indexes are specified, Moss searches them and adds relevant information to the model's input.
3. **Generate a response.** The selected model generates a response, which can be streamed back to your application.

With Moss's optimized model, retrieval and inference run on colocated infrastructure. When using a third-party model, Moss provides access through the same API, with optional retrieval grounding.

**API endpoint**

`https://inference.moss.dev/v1`

## Available models

Moss Inference supports two ways to run inference.

| Model type | Description |
| - | - |
| Moss optimized model | Moss-hosted inference optimized for low-latency response generation, with colocated retrieval |
| Third-party models | Access supported models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other providers through the Moss endpoint |

Both options can use your Moss indexes to provide relevant context during inference. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists every id with its prompt limit and prices.

## How it fits

| You need | Moss Inference gives you |
| - | - |
| A model | `moss/fastlane-1` on Moss GPUs, or a vendor model, on one project key |
| Time to first token | Under 200 ms on `moss/fastlane-1`, grounded. A vendor model adds its own latency |
| Grounding | A search of the indexes a call names, hits added to the prompt |
| Tools | OpenAI function tools run by your code, MCP servers and the [`moss_search`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search) tool run by Moss |
| Streaming | OpenAI's Responses events or Chat Completions chunks |
| A client | Any OpenAI client with a new base URL, or a Moss SDK on seven platforms |
| Billing | Credits per token and per retrieval, or vendor-billed tokens on your own key |

## Make one call

Run this after the [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md), which creates the `faq` index it searches.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -N https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "stream": true,
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    response = await client.responses.create(
        model="moss/fastlane-1",
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
    )
    print(response.output_text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Moss searches the `faq` index for the question, adds what it finds to the prompt, and answers. The curl call streams the reply. The Python client installs with `pip install moss`; [SDKs](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks.md) lists the other six.

## What can you build?

**Real-time voice agents**

Reduce the delay before an agent starts responding while retrieving relevant information from conversation context and business knowledge.

**Browser and computer-use agents**

Support agents that interact with websites and applications, using retrieved instructions, task context, and relevant knowledge to inform their next actions.

**Long-running agents**

Give agents access to relevant information from previous steps and persistent indexes as they work through multi-step tasks.

**AI copilots and assistants**

Build responsive applications that answer questions using your own documents, product information, and business knowledge.

## Choose how to start

>
> Get a grounded, streamed reply in five minutes.

> [card] [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md)

> [card] [Use an OpenAI client](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/openai-compatibility.md)
>

> [card] [SDKs](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks.md)
>
> Inference clients for seven platforms.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning | Called elsewhere |
| - | - | - |
| Index | A searchable set of your documents, built with the Moss SDK or API. | Vector store, knowledge base |
| Retrieval | One search of your indexes: the search before the model answers, or one `moss_search` call. | RAG, grounding |
| Time to first token | The time from sending the request to the first streamed token, not to the whole reply. | TTFT, latency |
| Project id and key | The two portal credentials that together form the bearer token. | API key |
| Moss key | A vendor model called on Moss's vendor account and billed to your credits. | Hosted model |
| Your own key | A vendor model called on your vendor account, with the key sent in `X-Moss-Provider-Key`. | BYOK |
| Model id | `provider/model`, such as `moss/fastlane-1` or `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`. | Model string |
| Reply cache | A repeated request answered without a model call, free. | Response cache |
| Prefix cache | Prompt tokens `moss/fastlane-1` still holds from an earlier call, billed at the cached price. | Prompt caching |

# Quickstart

> Call the moss model, stream the reply, then ground it in your own index.

Six steps from a project key to a streamed reply that answers from your data. Run the steps in order, and every block runs as written once the two environment variables are set.

**1. Get your project id and key**

In the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev), copy the project id, then open API Keys and create a key. Inference bills from credits with no included allowance, so add credits on the Billing page first (see [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#credits)). Export the id and key:

```bash theme={null}
export MOSS_PROJECT_ID=your_project_id
export MOSS_PROJECT_KEY=your_project_key
```

**2. Install a client**

curl needs no install until step 5, which creates the index with the Python or JavaScript SDK.

```bash Python theme={null}
pip install "moss>=1.22.0"
```

```bash JavaScript theme={null}
npm install @moss-js/moss@^1.22.0
```

```bash OpenAI client theme={null}
pip install openai
```

**3. Get a response**

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    response = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    )
    print(response.output_text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

```python OpenAI client theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
)
response = client.responses.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
)
print(response.output_text)
```

The model is `moss/fastlane-1` unless you name another. The reply is an OpenAI [Response object](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#response), and the SDKs expose its text as `output_text`. On a new project nothing is grounded yet, so the answer is generic. Step 5 fixes that.

**4. Stream it**

Add `stream: true` and read `response.output_text.delta` events as they arrive.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -N https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "stream": true,
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    stream = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        stream=True,
    )
    async with stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
                print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const stream = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  stream: true,
})
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? '')
}
```

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event and shows the Chat Completions form.

**5. Ground it in your data**

Create an index named `faq` with four documents, then name it in the call. Pick another name if `faq` is taken.

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, MossInference

client = MossClient(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])
inference = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])

documents = [
    DocumentInfo(id="doc1", text="How do I track my order? You can track your order by logging into your account.", metadata={"category": "shipping"}),
    DocumentInfo(id="doc2", text="What is your return policy? We offer a 30-day return policy for most items.", metadata={"category": "returns"}),
    DocumentInfo(id="doc3", text="How can I change my shipping address? Contact our customer service team.", metadata={"category": "support"}),
    DocumentInfo(id="doc4", text="Do you ship to Canada? Yes, we ship to Canada and the US. Delivery takes 5 to 7 business days.", metadata={"category": "shipping"}),
]


async def main():
    await client.create_index("faq", documents, "moss-minilm")
    response = await inference.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
    )
    print(response.output_text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossClient, MossInference, type DocumentInfo } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossClient(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const inference = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)

const documents: DocumentInfo[] = [
  { id: 'doc1', text: 'How do I track my order? You can track your order by logging into your account.', metadata: { category: 'shipping' } },
  { id: 'doc2', text: 'What is your return policy? We offer a 30-day return policy for most items.', metadata: { category: 'returns' } },
  { id: 'doc3', text: 'How can I change my shipping address? Contact our customer service team.', metadata: { category: 'support' } },
  { id: 'doc4', text: 'Do you ship to Canada? Yes, we ship to Canada and the US. Delivery takes 5 to 7 business days.', metadata: { category: 'shipping' } },
]

await client.createIndex('faq', documents, { modelId: 'moss-minilm' })
const response = await inference.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

The reply should now mention delivery in 5 to 7 business days. With curl or an OpenAI client, send the header `X-Moss-Indexes: faq` instead of `indexes`. Without the header, Moss does not search before the model runs. [Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

**6. Pick a model**

Name any model from the [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) page in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same on all of them.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

inference = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    response = await inference.responses.create(
        model="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
    )
    print(response.output_text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const inference = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const response = await inference.responses.create({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5',
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

# Models

> Every model Moss Inference serves, with its prompt limit, prices, routes and the parameters it refuses.

Every model is one id in the `model` field. Retrieval from your indexes works the same on all of them, and `GET /v1/models` lists the ones served now.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For voice agents, use `moss/fastlane-1` when the prompt and the retrieved facts fit in 262,144 tokens. For a larger context, use `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` or `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. `google/gemini-3.8-flash` thinks before it answers, which delays the first token. Set `reasoning` to `{"effort": "none"}` to turn it off.

## Model table

Prices in USD per 1M tokens, as of 2026-11-05. A dash in Cache write means the model has no separate cache-write price.

Prompt limit is the most prompt tokens a request can send on the Moss key. With your own key, a vendor model takes prompts of up to 200,000 tokens. The other limits are on [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

### Moss

| Model | Prompt limit | Input | Cached input | Cache write | Output |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Fastlane 1 `moss/fastlane-1` | 262,144 (whole context) | \$0.25 | \$0.03 | - | \$1.75 |

`moss` still works as a deprecated alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. The reply shows `moss/fastlane-1`.

### OpenAI

| Model | Prompt limit | Input | Cached input | Cache write | Output |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| GPT-6 Luna `openai/gpt-6-luna` | 128,000 | \$0.10 | \$0.01 | \$0.125 | \$0.50 |
| GPT-6.1 Terra `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` | 128,000 | \$1.00 | \$0.05 | \$1.25 | \$5.00 |
| GPT-6.1 Sol `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | 128,000 | \$2.00 | \$0.10 | \$2.50 | \$10.00 |
| GPT-6 Astra `openai/gpt-6-astra` | 128,000 | \$10.00 | \$1.00 | \$12.50 | \$50.00 |

### Anthropic

| Model | Prompt limit | Input | Cached input | Cache write | Output |

## Routes

The model you send and whether you send your own key decide where a call runs and who bills it.

| You send | Runs on | Billed to |
| - | - | - |
| `moss/fastlane-1`, or no `model` | Moss GPUs | Your credits, at the [Moss model prices](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#the-moss-model) |
| A vendor id from the table, without your key | The vendor, on the Moss key | Your credits, at the table prices |
| Any vendor model, with your key | The vendor, on your key | Your vendor account |

Every route also bills a retrieval for each search of your indexes. See [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#retrievals). [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers the third route.

## The Moss model

`moss/fastlane-1` is the default model. It runs on Moss GPUs and bills your credits.

* It runs on the same machines as the search of your indexes, which is the fast lane in its name. A grounded call streams its first token in under 200 ms.
* Its window is 262,144 tokens, shared by the prompt, the retrieved facts and the reply.
* A prompt that does not fit the window returns `400` with `code` `context_length_exceeded`.
* It takes text only.
* It keeps a prefix cache. A repeated system prompt or the earlier turns of a conversation bill at the cached input price.

Use it for grounded answers, tool calls and structured output.

## Parameters refused on the Moss key

On the Moss key, Moss sends a vendor only the fields that model takes. A request that sets any other field returns `400 unsupported_parameter` before the vendor is called.

A null, `false` or empty value counts as unset. So does a penalty or `top_logprobs` of 0, and a `temperature` or `top_p` of 1.

| Vendor | Fields refused on the Moss key |
| - | - |
| OpenAI | `seed`, `logit_bias`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `stop`, `logprobs`, `top_logprobs` |
| Anthropic | `seed`, `logit_bias`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `logprobs`, `top_logprobs`, `temperature`, `top_p`, a `text.format` or `response_format` of type `json_object` (use `json_schema`); on `claude-sonnet-5.5`, `claude-opus-5.5` and `claude-fable-5.1`, a `tool_choice` of `required` or a named tool |
| Google | `seed`, `logit_bias`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `logprobs`, `top_logprobs` |
| Open models | None |

Google models on the Moss key also refuse message parts other than text and base64 data URL images. Open models refuse `file` parts.

With your own key, the request reaches the vendor as you send it. See [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md).

## List models

`GET /v1/models` returns the models served now, in OpenAI's list shape. An OpenAI client reads it with `client.models.list()`.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"
```

```python OpenAI client theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
)
for model in client.models.list():
    print(model.id)
```

```json Response theme={null}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {"id": "moss/fastlane-1", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "moss"},
    {"id": "openai/gpt-6-luna", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "moss"},
    {"id": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "moss"}
  ]
}
```

The [List models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/models.md) reference describes each field.

## Changes

New models and retirements appear in the [Changelog](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/changelog.md). A retired id returns `400 model_not_found`.

# Pricing

> How Moss Inference bills: credits, tokens, prompt caching, retrievals and your own vendor key.

Moss Inference bills tokens and retrievals from your credits. This page covers credits, the `moss/fastlane-1` prices, vendor models, your own key and caching.

## Credits

Inference bills from credits on every plan, with no included allowance.

* Buy credits on the Billing page of the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). The minimum purchase is \$5.
* Set auto-reload on the same page.
* Only organization owners can buy credits.

> [!WARNING]
>
> When your credits run out, requests return `429 usage_limit_exceeded` until you add credits.

## The Moss model

| Item | Price |
| - | - |
| Input tokens | \$0.25 / 1M tokens |
| Cached input tokens | \$0.03 / 1M tokens |
| Output tokens | \$1.75 / 1M tokens |
| Retrieval | \$0.50 / 1k retrievals |

Tokens are the `usage` counts of each reply. Input tokens include the retrieved facts.

## Vendor models on the Moss key

A vendor model called without your own key bills your credits per token. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#model-table) lists the input, cached input, cache write and output prices of each model.

Retrievals bill at the same price as on `moss/fastlane-1`.

## Your own key

With your own key in `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, the vendor bills the tokens to your vendor account. Moss bills only the retrievals. See [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md).

## Prompt caching

Prompt tokens a model already holds from an earlier call bill at the cached input price.

* On `moss/fastlane-1`, these are in the prefix cache, such as a repeated system prompt or the earlier turns of a conversation.
* The Chat Completions field `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` counts them, and Responses uses `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. The rest of the prompt bills at the input price.
* Where a model lists a cache-write price, prompt tokens written to the vendor's cache bill at that price.

The reply cache is separate. It answers a repeated request without a model call, and the reply reports 0 prompt tokens (`usage.prompt_tokens` on Chat Completions, `usage.input_tokens` on Responses). A reply-cache hit is free.

## Retrievals

A retrieval is one search of your indexes: the search that `X-Moss-Indexes` runs before the model, or one call of the [Moss search tool](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md) that an index answered. It bills the same on every model, your own key included.

* The price is \$0.50 / 1k retrievals.
* A call that names no index in `X-Moss-Indexes` and has no `moss_search` tool has no search and no retrieval charge.
* A reply-cache hit is not a retrieval.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers choosing indexes.

## Usage

Inference is not billed as session minutes. The Usage page in the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev) shows inference tokens per model and retrievals.

# OpenAI compatibility

> Call Moss Inference from any OpenAI client: base URL, key, endpoints, Moss headers and what differs from OpenAI.

Moss Inference speaks OpenAI's API, so any OpenAI client works once you change the base URL and the key. This page covers the endpoints, the Moss headers and what differs from OpenAI.

## Set the base URL and key

```text theme={null}
https://inference.moss.dev/v1
```

The key is your project id and project key from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev), joined by a colon. Send it as a bearer token:

```text theme={null}
Authorization: Bearer <project_id>:<project_key>
```

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| [`POST /v1/responses`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses) | OpenAI's Responses API. The Moss SDKs call it. |
| [`POST /v1/chat/completions`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/chat-completions) | OpenAI's Chat Completions API. |
| [`GET /v1/models`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/models) | The models served now, in OpenAI's list shape. |

## Point an OpenAI client at Moss

Change the base URL and the key. The `X-Moss-Indexes` header is optional and names the indexes to search. Install OpenAI's client with `pip install openai` or `npm install openai`. The Vercel AI SDK needs `npm install @ai-sdk/openai ai`.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
    default_headers={"X-Moss-Indexes": "faq"},
)
response = client.responses.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
)
print(response.output_text)
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: 'https://inference.moss.dev/v1',
  apiKey: `${process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID}:${process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY}`,
  defaultHeaders: { 'X-Moss-Indexes': 'faq' },
})
const response = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'moss/fastlane-1',
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

```typescript Vercel AI SDK theme={null}
import { createOpenAI } from '@ai-sdk/openai'
import { generateText } from 'ai'

const moss = createOpenAI({
  baseURL: 'https://inference.moss.dev/v1',
  apiKey: `${process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID}:${process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY}`,
  headers: { 'X-Moss-Indexes': 'faq' },
})
const { text } = await generateText({
  model: moss.chat('moss/fastlane-1'),
  system: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  prompt: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
})
console.log(text)
```

The Python and JavaScript tabs use OpenAI's own clients. The Vercel AI SDK tab calls Chat Completions through `.chat()`. For the Moss SDKs, see [SDKs](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks.md).

## Responses or Chat Completions

Both endpoints search the indexes a call names and take the same models, headers and limits.

| Use | Pick |
| - | - |
| New code | Responses |
| A Moss SDK | Responses. The Moss SDKs call it. |
| Existing code on Chat Completions | Chat Completions |
| The Vercel AI SDK | Chat Completions, through `.chat()` |

The same call on Chat Completions:

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "system", "content": "You are the support agent for Acme." },
      { "role": "user", "content": "Do you ship to Canada?" }
    ]
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
    default_headers={"X-Moss-Indexes": "faq"},
)
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are the support agent for Acme."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Do you ship to Canada?"},
    ],
)
print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: 'https://inference.moss.dev/v1',
  apiKey: `${process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID}:${process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY}`,
  defaultHeaders: { 'X-Moss-Indexes': 'faq' },
})
const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'moss/fastlane-1',
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'You are the support agent for Acme.' },
    { role: 'user', content: 'Do you ship to Canada?' },
  ],
})
console.log(completion.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Moss headers

Both endpoints read these request headers. The last column names the matching Moss SDK option.

| Header | Default | What it does | SDK option |
| - | - | - | - |
| `X-Moss-Indexes` | none | Comma-separated index names to search, such as `faq,policies`. Without it, Moss does not search before the model runs. A [`moss_search`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search) tool still searches. | `indexes` |
| `X-Moss-Retrieve` | `on` | `off` skips the search before the model runs, even when indexes are named. It does not turn off [`moss_search`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search). | `retrieve` |
| `X-Moss-Cache` | `on` | `off` skips the reply cache. | `cache` |
| `X-Moss-System-Prompt` | `on` | `off` skips the project's [system prompt](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/chat-completions.md#system-prompt). | none |
| `X-Moss-Provider-Key` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key. The call runs on it. | `api_key`, `apiKey` |
| `X-Request-Id` | none | Your own id for the call. Moss logs it and passes it to a vendor model. | none |

The rules for `X-Moss-Indexes` and `X-Moss-Retrieve` are in [Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md). Your own key is covered in [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md).

Every reply carries these headers:

| Header | What it holds |
| - | - |
| `X-Moss-Request-Id` | The request's id, a refused request included. Send it when you report a problem. |
| `X-Moss-Retrieve-Ms` | How long the search before the model took, in milliseconds. It leaves out `moss_search` calls. |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-*`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-*`, `x-ratelimit-reset-*` | How much of the project's limits is left. |

The `*` is `requests`, and on `moss/fastlane-1` also `tokens`. The limits themselves are in [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## What is different from OpenAI

On Responses, Moss differs from OpenAI in these ways:

* Moss stores no responses. `store` is ignored, and `previous_response_id` and `conversation` are refused. Send the whole conversation in `input` on every call. See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).
* Tools are `function`, `mcp` and the Moss [`moss_search`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search) tool only. OpenAI's built-in tools, such as `web_search`, `file_search`, `code_interpreter`, `image_generation`, computer use and shell, are refused. So are custom tools, and a `tool_choice` that names one.
* Content parts are `input_text`, `output_text`, and `input_image` with an `image_url`. Files (`input_file`), audio (`input_audio`) and images by `file_id` are refused. The `moss/fastlane-1` model reads text only.
* [Input items](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#input-items) other than those listed, such as `item_reference`, are refused.
* `background: true`, a non-empty `include`, `prompt`, and `truncation: "auto"` are refused.
* `reasoning` takes `effort` only. `text.verbosity` takes `medium` only.
* Any field missing from the [Responses request](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#request) table is refused, such as `max_tool_calls` or `top_logprobs`.

A refused field returns `400` with `type` `invalid_request_error` and `code` `unsupported_parameter`. The message names the field:

```json 400 - Bad Request theme={null}
{
  "error": {
    "message": "previous_response_id is not supported. Send the whole conversation in input.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "unsupported_parameter"
  }
}
```

On Chat Completions:

* A reply without `stream` has one choice and no `logprobs`.
* Chat Completions ends a stream with `data: [DONE]`. Responses sends none.
* The last chunk before `data: [DONE]` has empty `choices` and the whole reply's `usage`. See [Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md).

Vendor models on the Moss key also refuse some fields, such as `temperature` on an Anthropic model, with the same `400`. The list per vendor is in [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#parameters-refused-on-the-moss-key).

# Ground answers in your indexes

> Choose the indexes Moss searches, turn the search off, and see what it costs and how long it takes.

Name an index in the call and the model answers from it. This page covers choosing indexes, turning the search off, the cost and the timing header.

On each call that names an index, Moss:

1. searches those indexes for the user's question,
2. adds the hits to the prompt,
3. sends the prompt to the model, which answers.

A call that names no index is plain inference: no search and no retrieval fee.

The search reads only the text of user messages, never images. It works the same on every model.

## Choose indexes

Name the indexes to search in `indexes` in the Moss SDKs. With curl or an OpenAI client, send the `X-Moss-Indexes` header.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    response = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
    )
    print(response.output_text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

```python OpenAI client theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
)
response = client.responses.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    extra_headers={"X-Moss-Indexes": "faq"},
)
print(response.output_text)
```

Name several indexes as a list, or as a comma-separated header such as `X-Moss-Indexes: faq,policies`.

* One request searches at most 32 indexes. The names in `X-Moss-Indexes` and in a `moss_search` tool count together. More than 32 names returns `400`.
* An index outside this project returns `403`.

The full error list is in [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors).

## Turn it off

To skip the search, name no index and send no [`moss_search`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search) tool. The model then answers from `input` alone.

To skip it on a call that still names indexes, set `retrieve` to `False` in Python or `false` in JavaScript, or send `X-Moss-Retrieve: off`. This does not turn off the [Moss search tool](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md).

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -H "X-Moss-Retrieve: off" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    response = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
        retrieve=False,
    )
    print(response.output_text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
  retrieve: false,
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

```python OpenAI client theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
)
response = client.responses.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    extra_headers={"X-Moss-Indexes": "faq", "X-Moss-Retrieve": "off"},
)
print(response.output_text)
```

## Check what it costs

Each request that searches your indexes before the model runs is one retrieval, however many indexes it names. Each [Moss search tool](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md#billing) call that an index answered is one more retrieval. The price is \$0.50 / 1k retrievals.

* The fee is the same on every model, and with your own vendor key.
* A request that names no index, or has the search off, has no retrieval before the model. Its `moss_search` calls still count.
* A reply-cache hit is not a retrieval.

The retrieved facts also count as input tokens. `usage.input_tokens` on Responses and `usage.prompt_tokens` on Chat Completions include them. See [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#retrievals).

## See how long it took

The reply header `X-Moss-Retrieve-Ms` holds how long the search took, in milliseconds. This call prints it:

```bash theme={null}
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{"model": "moss/fastlane-1", "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.", "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"}' \
  | grep -i x-moss-retrieve-ms
```

## Get better answers

* Keep `instructions` short and on one job, such as "You are the support agent for Acme."
* Name only the indexes a use case needs. Hits from unrelated documents then stay out of the prompt.
* On `moss/fastlane-1`, the prompt, the retrieved facts and the reply share 262,144 tokens. Leave room for `max_output_tokens`. See [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#the-moss-model).
* Keep your indexes current. To create and update them, see [Indexing data](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/indexing-data.md).

# Streaming

> Stream replies as Responses events or Chat Completions chunks, stop early, and catch errors after the stream starts.

Set `stream` to `true` and the reply arrives as server-sent events while the model writes it. This page covers the events of each API, stopping early, errors after the stream starts and where usage arrives.

## Stream a response

Responses streams typed events. The text arrives in `response.output_text.delta` events.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -N https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "stream": true,
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    stream = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
        stream=True,
    )
    async with stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
                print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const stream = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
  stream: true,
})
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? '')
}
```

```python OpenAI client theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
    default_headers={"X-Moss-Indexes": "faq"},
)
stream = client.responses.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    stream=True,
)
for event in stream:
    if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
        print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
```

Moss sends only these event types, in OpenAI's [streaming event](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses-streaming) shapes:

| Part | Events |
| - | - |
| Start | `response.created`, `response.in_progress` |
| Output items | `response.output_item.added`, `response.output_item.done` |
| Content parts | `response.content_part.added`, `response.content_part.done` |
| Text | `response.output_text.delta`, `response.output_text.done` |
| Function calls | `response.function_call_arguments.delta`, `response.function_call_arguments.done` |
| MCP and `moss_search` calls | The `mcp_call` events in [MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) |

The stream ends with one event that carries the whole response:

* `response.completed`: the reply is done.
* `response.incomplete`: `max_output_tokens` or a content filter cut the reply short.
* `response.failed`: the call failed. See [Errors after the stream starts](#errors-after-the-stream-starts).

Responses sends no `data: [DONE]`. In the SDKs, `await stream.get_final_response()` in Python and `await stream.finalResponse()` in JavaScript read the rest and return that response.

## Stream Chat Completions

Chat Completions streams `chat.completion.chunk` objects and ends with `data: [DONE]`. The text arrives in `choices[0].delta.content`.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -N https://inference.moss.dev/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [
      { "role": "system", "content": "You are the support agent for Acme." },
      { "role": "user", "content": "Do you ship to Canada?" }
    ]
  }'
```

```python OpenAI client theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
    default_headers={"X-Moss-Indexes": "faq"},
)
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are the support agent for Acme."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Do you ship to Canada?"},
    ],
    stream=True,
)
for chunk in stream:
    if chunk.choices:
        print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content or "", end="", flush=True)
    elif chunk.usage:
        print(f"\n{chunk.usage.total_tokens} tokens")
```

On the wire, the stream looks like this:

```text theme={null}
data: {"id": "chatcmpl-1", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1761177600, "model": "moss/fastlane-1", "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Yes, we ship"}, "finish_reason": null}]}

data: {"id": "chatcmpl-1", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1761177600, "model": "moss/fastlane-1", "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"content": " to Canada."}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}

data: {"id": "chatcmpl-1", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1761177600, "model": "moss/fastlane-1", "choices": [], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 165, "completion_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 172, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 128}}}

data: [DONE]
```

The last chunk before `data: [DONE]` has empty `choices` and the whole reply's `usage`. Check `choices` before you read `choices[0]`.

## Stop early

In the Moss SDKs, leave the loop to stop. That closes the connection, which stops the model. This example stops after the first sentence:

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])


async def main():
    stream = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
        stream=True,
    )
    text = ""
    async with stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
                text += event.delta
                if "." in text:
                    break
    print(text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const stream = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
  stream: true,
})
let text = ''
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') text += event.delta ?? ''
  if (text.includes('.')) break
}
console.log(text)
```

In Python, `break` leaves the `async with stream:` block, which closes the connection. JavaScript can also stop with `stream.controller.abort()`. In JavaScript, neither way throws.

## Errors after the stream starts

Once the first event is sent, the status is already `200`. A failure after that arrives in the body:

* Responses ends the stream with `response.failed`. Its `response.error` has `type`, `code` and `message`. Its `response.output` holds the items so far.
* Chat Completions sends a final `data:` frame that carries `error` instead of `choices`, then `data: [DONE]`.

**Check the body of every stream for `error`: the status is already 200.**

The Moss SDKs check for you. They raise their [inference error](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#sdk-errors) from the loop, and a `response.failed` event raises it too. A stream that ends before its last event raises it with `type` `incomplete_stream`. The SDKs retry only before the response starts, so a failure mid-stream is not retried.

If the stream fails after an MCP call or a `moss_search` call ran, `error.code` is `failed_after_tool_call`. Do not replay that request: the tool may already have changed data. See [MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md). Every code is in [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors).

## Read usage on a stream

| API | Usage arrives in | To leave it out |
| - | - | - |
| Responses | The final event's `response.usage` | `stream_options` is ignored. |
| Chat Completions | The last chunk before `data: [DONE]`, with empty `choices` | `"stream_options": {"include_usage": false}` |

Both counts include the retrieved facts. On `moss/fastlane-1`, the Chat Completions field `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is the part of the prompt held in the prefix cache. See [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#prompt-caching).

<!-- Page: Tool calling · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md · local: pages/inference/tool-calling.md -->

# Tool calling

> Give the model function tools, run each call in your code, and send the results back.

The model asks for a tool, your code runs it, and you send the result back. This page shows that loop on Responses and on Chat Completions, then structured output. To have Moss run the tools for you, use [MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md). To let the model search your indexes, use the [Moss search tool](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md).

## The loop

Moss stores nothing between calls. Each round sends the whole conversation, and you repeat it until the reply has no tool calls.

**1. Send your tools**

Put function tools in `tools`. On Responses a function tool is flat: `name`, `description` and `parameters` sit next to `type`.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Where is order A1?",
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "name": "lookup_order",
      "description": "Look up an order by its id.",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]}
    }]
  }'
```

**2. Run each call**

The reply's `output` holds one `function_call` item per call, with a `call_id`, the tool's `name` and its `arguments`. `arguments` is a JSON string, such as `{"id": "A1"}`. Parse it and run the tool in your code.

**3. Send the results back**

Call again with the conversation so far. In order, send the earlier input, the `output` items, and one `function_call_output` per call with the same `call_id`. Send `instructions` again too.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Where is order A1?"},
      {"id": "fc_8fd7_0", "type": "function_call", "status": "completed", "call_id": "call_1",
       "name": "lookup_order", "arguments": "{\"id\": \"A1\"}"},
      {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": "Shipped on Oct 20."}
    ],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "name": "lookup_order",
      "description": "Look up an order by its id.",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]}
    }]
  }'
```

The reply is the answer, or more calls. Repeat until `output` has no `function_call` items.

**Send `tools` on every request.** Moss keeps no state, so the model sees only the tools in the request it is answering.

**Send `output` items back unchanged.** A `function_call` item can carry fields beyond OpenAI's, such as Gemini's `extra_content` and its thought signature. The model needs them on the next turn.

## Write the loop with an SDK

Each loop runs until the reply has no calls. `lookup_order` stands for your own code, and it returns text.

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import json
import os

from moss import MossInference
from moss.inference import ResponseFunctionToolCall

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])

tools = [{
    "type": "function",
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "description": "Look up an order by its id.",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]},
}]


def lookup_order(id):
    return "Shipped on Oct 20."


async def main():
    items = [{"role": "user", "content": "Where is order A1?"}]
    while True:
        response = await client.responses.create(
            instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
            input=items,
            tools=tools,
        )
        items += response.output
        calls = [i for i in response.output if isinstance(i, ResponseFunctionToolCall)]
        if not calls:
            print(response.output_text)
            break
        for call in calls:
            output = lookup_order(**json.loads(call.arguments))
            items.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call.call_id, "output": output})


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'
import type { FunctionTool, ResponseInputItem } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)

const tools: FunctionTool[] = [
  {
    type: 'function',
    name: 'lookup_order',
    description: 'Look up an order by its id.',
    parameters: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id'] },
  },
]

async function lookupOrder(id: string): Promise<string> {
  return 'Shipped on Oct 20.'
}

const input: ResponseInputItem[] = [{ role: 'user', content: 'Where is order A1?' }]

for (;;) {
  const stream = await client.responses.create({
    instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
    input,
    tools,
    stream: true,
  })
  for await (const event of stream) {
    if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? '')
  }
  const { output } = await stream.finalResponse()
  input.push(...output)
  const calls = output.filter((item) => item.type === 'function_call')
  if (calls.length === 0) break
  for (const call of calls) {
    const { id } = JSON.parse(call.arguments)
    input.push({ type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.call_id, output: await lookupOrder(id) })
  }
}
```

In Python, each call is a `ResponseFunctionToolCall` and goes back as its `raw` JSON, with every field the model sent. In JavaScript, the loop streams each round and reads the items from `stream.finalResponse()`. Without `stream: true`, `create` returns the response directly.

## Call tools on Chat Completions

Chat Completions takes OpenAI's Chat shape, where a tool nests `name` and `parameters` under `function`. A reply without `stream` has the calls in `choices[0].message.tool_calls`, with `finish_reason` `tool_calls`.

Send the assistant message back unchanged, then one `tool` message per call, and call again:

```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are the support agent for Acme."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Where is order A1?"},
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": null,
      "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function",
                      "function": {"name": "lookup_order", "arguments": "{\"id\": \"A1\"}"}}]
    },
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "Shipped on Oct 20."}
  ],
  "tools": [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "lookup_order",
      "description": "Look up an order by its id.",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]}
    }
  }]
}
```

The same two rules apply. Send `tools` every time, and keep every field of `tool_calls`, such as Gemini's `extra_content`. A `tools` value that is not a list of objects returns `400`.

## Choose how the model calls tools

`tool_choice` sets whether the model must call a tool. On Responses it takes these values:

| Value | The model |
| - | - |
| `auto` | Decides for itself. The default. |
| `none` | Answers without a tool. |
| `required` | Calls at least one tool. |
| `{"type": "function", "name": "lookup_order"}` | Calls that function. |
| `{"type": "mcp", "server_label": "crm", "name": "lookup_order"}` | Calls that tool of an [MCP server](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md). |

On Chat Completions, `tool_choice` takes OpenAI's Chat values. A named function there is `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_order"}}`.

On the Moss key, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` and `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` take only `auto` and `none`. A `tool_choice` of `required` or a named tool returns `400 unsupported_parameter`.

`parallel_tool_calls` is `true` by default, so the model can call more than one tool at once. Set it to `false` to allow one call at a time.

## Structured output

To get JSON that matches a schema, set `text.format` to type `json_schema` on Responses. Type `json_object` asks for any JSON object, and type `text` is plain text. Anthropic models on the Moss key refuse `json_object` with `400 unsupported_parameter`; send `json_schema` instead.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?",
    "text": {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "shipping_answer", "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"ships": {"type": "boolean"}, "answer": {"type": "string"}},
      "required": ["ships", "answer"],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }}}
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import json
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])

schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"ships": {"type": "boolean"}, "answer": {"type": "string"}},
    "required": ["ships", "answer"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}


async def main():
    response = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
        text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "shipping_answer", "schema": schema}},
    )
    print(json.loads(response.output_text))


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const schema = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: { ships: { type: 'boolean' }, answer: { type: 'string' } },
  required: ['ships', 'answer'],
  additionalProperties: false,
}
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
  text: { format: { type: 'json_schema', name: 'shipping_answer', schema } },
})
console.log(JSON.parse(response.output_text))
```

`output_text` is then the JSON object as a string. On Chat Completions, send the schema in `response_format` instead, in OpenAI's shape: `{"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "shipping_answer", "schema": ...}}`.

## Stream tool calls

On a Responses stream, each call starts with `response.output_item.added`. Its arguments arrive in pieces in `response.function_call_arguments.delta` events, then whole in `response.function_call_arguments.done`. `response.output_item.done` carries the finished `function_call` item.

On a Chat Completions stream, each call arrives in pieces in `delta.tool_calls`, with `index`, `id`, `function.name` and `function.arguments`. Join the pieces by `index`. A chunk with `finish_reason` `tool_calls` ends the round.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event and chunk.

---

<!-- Page: MCP servers · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md · local: pages/inference/mcp-servers.md -->

# MCP servers

> Name an MCP server in tools, and Moss runs its tools for the model during the response.

A `tools` entry of type `mcp` names an MCP server. Moss connects to it, offers its tools to the model, and runs each call the model makes. Your code sends no results for these tools.

## Add a server

```json theme={null}
{
  "type": "mcp",
  "server_label": "crm",
  "server_url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
  "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer CRM_TOKEN"},
  "allowed_tools": ["lookup_order"]
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `type` | yes | `mcp` |
| `server_label` | yes | A name for the server. Different for each server in the request. In a request that has the [Moss search tool](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md), `moss` is kept for that tool and returns `400`. |
| `server_url` | yes | A public `https` URL on port 443. Any other URL returns `400`. |
| `headers` | no | Sent to that server only, such as `Authorization`. They never reach the model. |
| `allowed_tools` | no | Tool names. The model sees only these tools of the server. |
| `transport` | no | `streamable_http`, the default, or `sse` for an older server. |
| `require_approval` | no | Only `never`. Moss never asks for approval. |

A public server, such as `https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp`, needs no `headers`. OpenAI's connectors (`connector_id`) and its `authorization` field are not supported, so send a token in `headers`. A response's `tools` field leaves out MCP `headers`.

One request can hold your own [function tools](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) and MCP servers together. When the model calls both in one round, only your function calls are returned, and the MCP calls are not run. A request with MCP servers can run for a few minutes.

## Run a request with a server

These examples stream the answer and print each MCP call when it ends. Replace the URL with your server's, and set `CRM_TOKEN` to its token.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -N https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "stream": true,
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Where is order A1?",
    "tools": [{
      "type": "mcp",
      "server_label": "crm",
      "server_url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer '"$CRM_TOKEN"'"}
    }]
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference
from moss.inference import McpCall, McpServer

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])

crm = McpServer(
    server_label="crm",
    server_url="https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CRM_TOKEN']}"},
)


async def main():
    stream = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Where is order A1?",
        tools=[crm],
        stream=True,
    )
    async with stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if event.type == "response.output_item.done" and isinstance(event.item, McpCall):
                print(event.item.name, event.item.output)
            elif event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
                print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'
import type { McpServer } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)

const crm: McpServer = {
  type: 'mcp',
  server_label: 'crm',
  server_url: 'https://mcp.example.com/mcp',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CRM_TOKEN}` },
}
const stream = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Where is order A1?',
  tools: [crm],
  stream: true,
})
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === 'response.output_item.done' && event.item?.type === 'mcp_call') {
    console.log(event.item.server_label, event.item.name, event.item.output)
  } else if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') {
    process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? '')
  }
}
```

Each call is an `mcp_call` item. It arrives in `response.output_item.added` when it starts and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `output`.

## Tool steps

### Read steps on Responses

Each MCP call streams as these events, in order:

1. `response.output_item.added`
2. `response.mcp_call.in_progress`
3. `response.mcp_call_arguments.done`
4. `response.mcp_call.completed`, or `response.mcp_call.failed`
5. `response.output_item.done`

The finished item holds the call and its result:

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "call_1",
  "type": "mcp_call",
  "status": "completed",
  "server_label": "crm",
  "name": "lookup_order",
  "arguments": "{\"id\": \"A1\"}",
  "output": "Shipped on Oct 20.",
  "error": null,
  "duration_ms": 41.2
}
```

A failed call has `status` `failed` and `output` null. Its `error` is `{"type": "mcp_tool_execution_error", "content": ...}`.

### Read steps on Chat Completions

A stream carries one extra chunk before each MCP call and one after it. Each has an empty `delta` and a `moss_tool_step`:

```text theme={null}
data: {"object": "chat.completion.chunk", "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": null}], "moss_tool_step": {"type": "call", "id": "call_1", "server_label": "crm", "name": "lookup_order", "arguments": "{\"id\": \"A1\"}"}}

data: {"object": "chat.completion.chunk", "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": null}], "moss_tool_step": {"type": "result", "id": "call_1", "server_label": "crm", "name": "lookup_order", "is_error": false, "duration_ms": 41.2, "output": "Shipped on Oct 20."}}
```

A `call` step comes before the tool runs and carries its `arguments`. A `result` step comes after, with `is_error`, `duration_ms` and `output`. Both have the same `id`, the `server_label` and the tool's `name`.

A reply without `stream` lists the steps in order in a top-level `moss_tool_steps` array. OpenAI clients ignore both fields.

Chat Completions does not add MCP calls to the message history. Keep what you need from the steps in your own messages.

## Send `mcp_call` items back

On Responses, put the `mcp_call` items back in `input` with the rest of `output`. The model sees their results and does not run the tools again.

An `mcp_call` with neither `output` nor `error` never finished, and its tool may have run. Sending it back returns `400`. Check whether the tool ran, and send the outcome as a message in its place.

## Errors

| Status | `type` | `code` | Cause | What to do |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | | A bad `tools` entry, a `server_label` or tool name used twice, or too many servers or tools. | Fix the `tools` list. |
| `400` | `mcp_error` | `mcp_server_error` | `server_url` is not a public `https` URL on port 443. | Use a public `https` URL on port 443. |
| `424` | `mcp_error` | `mcp_server_error` | The server did not connect, refused the credentials, or failed to list its tools. | Check the server and its `headers`. |
| `424` | | `failed_after_tool_call` | A call failed after a tool ran. | Do not replay. Read what ran. |
| `429` | `capacity` | `mcp_loops_busy` | Too many requests with MCP servers or `moss_search` at once. | Retry after `Retry-After`. |

A tool may already have changed data when a call fails after it, so Moss never retries that call:

* Without `stream`, the reply is `424` with `code` `failed_after_tool_call` and the header `x-should-retry: false`. Its body holds the `output` items so far on Responses, or the `moss_tool_steps` that ran on Chat Completions.
* On a Responses stream, `response.failed` has `error.code` `failed_after_tool_call`.
* On a Chat Completions stream, an `error` frame follows the last step.

**Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

Read the items or steps that ran to see what the tool did.

In the SDKs, every MCP failure is an `InferenceError`. It has `status`, `type`, `code` and `retry_after` in Python, and `status`, `type`, `errorCode` and `retryAfter` in JavaScript.

[Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every other error. Its [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits) section covers the request limits.

<!-- Page: Moss search tool · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md · local: pages/inference/moss-search.md -->

# Moss search tool

> Give the model a moss_search tool, and Moss searches your project's indexes each time the model asks.

A `tools` entry of type `moss_search` gives the model a `moss_search(query)` tool. Moss runs each search on your project's indexes and returns the passages to the model. Your code does not run it.

[Retrieval](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) with `X-Moss-Indexes` searches once, before the model runs, with the user's message as the query. `moss_search` searches when the model asks, with the model's query. You can use both.

## Add the tool

```json theme={null}
{
  "type": "moss_search",
  "indexes": ["docs", "faq"],
  "top_k": 5
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `type` | yes | `moss_search` |
| `indexes` | yes | 1 to 32 index names in your project. A name outside the project returns `403` before the model runs. |
| `top_k` | no | Passages for each search, 1 to 20. The default is 5. |
| `description` | no | The tool description the model reads, up to 1000 characters. Use it to say what the indexes hold. |

One `moss_search` entry per request. An unknown field returns `400`. So does a function tool of your own named `moss_search`.

## Run a request with the tool

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -N https://inference.moss.dev/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "moss/fastlane-1",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are the support agent for Acme."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "How much is the Pro plan, and does it work offline?"}
    ],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "moss_search",
      "indexes": ["docs"],
      "description": "Search the Acme product docs and pricing pages."
    }]
  }'
```

The same entry works in `tools` on [`/v1/responses`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses).

To make the model search first, set `tool_choice`. On Chat Completions, send `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "moss_search"}}`. On Responses, send `{"type": "function", "name": "moss_search"}` or `{"type": "mcp", "server_label": "moss", "name": "moss_search"}`.

`moss_search` does not need `X-Moss-Indexes`. `X-Moss-Retrieve: off` and `X-Moss-Retrieve-Ms` apply only to the search before the model. They do not turn off or time `moss_search`.

## What the model gets back

Each call searches every named index and returns the best passages, numbered, best first, marked as data, not instructions. A query is cut at 2000 characters.

A failed search, an empty query or a timeout goes back to the model as the tool result, and the request goes on.

## Tool steps

Each search is a tool step, the same as an MCP call, with `server_label` `moss` and `name` `moss_search`.

* On Chat Completions, a stream carries a `moss_tool_step` chunk before and after each search. A reply without `stream` lists the steps in `moss_tool_steps`. See [Read steps on Chat Completions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md#read-steps-on-chat-completions).
* On Responses, each search is an `mcp_call` output item, with the `response.mcp_call.*` events in [Read steps on Responses](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md#read-steps-on-responses). There is no `moss_tool_step` chunk.

On Responses, send the `mcp_call` items back in `input` unchanged. The model sees the earlier searches and does not run them again. Chat Completions does not add searches to the message history.

## Limits and errors

The tool loop and its errors are the same as for [MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md#errors), including `mcp_loops_busy` and `failed_after_tool_call`.

| Limit | Value |
| - | - |
| Tool rounds per request | 10 |
| Tool calls per round | 8. A ninth call does not run, and the model reads an error. |
| Time for one search | 30 s |
| Time for all tool rounds | 150 s |
| Time for the whole turn | 180 s |
| Text of one search result | up to 8,000 characters. Whole passages go in, best first. A last line says how many passages did not fit. |

Beside `moss_search`, an MCP server with `server_label` `moss` returns `400`.

A streamed reply has the header `x-should-retry: false`, so a client does not replay it. So does every reply on Responses. On Chat Completions, a reply without `stream` has it only when it fails after a tool step.

`moss_search`, MCP servers and your own [function tools](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) can share a request. When the model calls one of your functions, the loop ends and returns the call to your code. If the same round also calls `moss_search`, that search does not run.

## Billing

Each `moss_search` call that an index answered is one retrieval, however many indexes it names. A tool over `faq` and `policies` called twice is two retrievals. A failed search or an empty query is not billed. `X-Moss-Retrieve: off` does not change this. [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#retrievals) has the price of a retrieval.
