# Bring your own key

> Run vendor models on your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, with the same search of your indexes.

Send your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key with a call, and the call runs on your vendor account. Moss still searches your indexes and adds the hits to the prompt.

## Send your key

Put the key in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header. In the SDKs, pass it as `api_key` in Python or `apiKey` in JavaScript, and the SDK sends the header for you. These examples read an OpenAI key from `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

```bash curl theme={null}
curl https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOSS_PROJECT_ID:$MOSS_PROJECT_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Moss-Indexes: faq" \
  -H "X-Moss-Provider-Key: $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "instructions": "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    "input": "Do you ship to Canada?"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(
    os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"],
    os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"],
    api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"],
)


async def main():
    response = await client.responses.create(
        model="gpt-6-luna",
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input="Do you ship to Canada?",
        indexes=["faq"],
    )
    print(response.output_text)


asyncio.run(main())
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!, {
  apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
})
const response = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'gpt-6-luna',
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

```python OpenAI client theme={null}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.moss.dev/v1",
    api_key=f"{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_ID']}:{os.environ['MOSS_PROJECT_KEY']}",
    default_headers={"X-Moss-Indexes": "faq", "X-Moss-Provider-Key": os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]},
)
response = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
)
print(response.output_text)
```

A key on the client applies to every call. To use a key for one call, pass `api_key` to `responses.create` in Python. In JavaScript, pass `apiKey` in the second argument of `responses.create`. In JavaScript, a request field named `apiKey` or `api_key` throws, so keep the key out of the first argument.

Moss sends the key only to that vendor and never stores it. The SDKs send it as a header, never in the body. The reply's `model` is the name you sent.

## Which names work

With your key, `model` takes a listed id or the vendor's own model name.

| You send | Runs on |
| - | - |
| A listed OpenAI, Anthropic or Google id, such as `openai/gpt-6-luna` | That model, on your key |
| `gpt-*`, `chatgpt-*`, or `o1` to `o9` | OpenAI |
| `claude-*` | Anthropic |
| `gemini-*` | Google |

For example, `gpt-6-luna` goes to OpenAI and `claude-haiku-5-5` goes to Anthropic. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists the ids.

A vendor's own name works only with your key. Without the key, the call returns `400` with `code` `missing_provider_key`.

## Use the vendor's own fields

The request reaches the vendor as you sent it, so it takes that vendor's own fields. Moss does not hold it to the [parameters refused on the Moss key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#parameters-refused-on-the-moss-key). The vendor decides what it accepts.

On your key, a prompt can hold up to 200,000 tokens. [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits) has the other limits.

## Handle vendor errors

A wrong or refused key gets the vendor's own error and status. The error has `type` `model_error` and `code` `upstream_error`. Its message starts with `The model rejected the prompt`, followed by the vendor's message.

A bad key is `401` from OpenAI and Anthropic, and `400` from Google. Moss never retries the call on the Moss key, so fix the key and send the call again.

## Know who bills what

| Cost | Billed by |
| - | - |
| Tokens | Your vendor account |
| Retrievals | Moss, from your credits, at \$0.50 / 1k retrievals |

Moss bills one retrieval for each search of your indexes, on any model: the `X-Moss-Indexes` search before the model, and each `moss_search` call. A call that searches no index has no retrieval fee. [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#retrievals) has the details.

# SDKs

> The inference client in each Moss SDK, with its package and minimum version.

Each Moss SDK has an inference client for the Responses endpoint, separate from `MossClient`. Any OpenAI client also works with the base URL changed: see [OpenAI compatibility](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/openai-compatibility.md).

## Packages

| SDK | Package | Minimum version | Client |
| - | - | - | - |
| [Python](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/python.md) | `moss` | 1.22.0 | `MossInference` |
| [JavaScript](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/javascript.md) | `@moss-js/moss` | 1.22.0 | `MossInference` |
| [Browser](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/browser.md) | `@moss-dev/moss-web` | 1.8.0 | `MossInference` |
| [Swift](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/swift.md) | `Moss` Swift package | 0.13.0 | `MossInference` |
| [Android](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/android.md) | `moss-android` AAR | 0.29.0 | `dev.usemoss.moss.MossInference` |
| [Elixir](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/elixir.md) | `moss` | 1.11.0 | `Moss.Inference` |
| [C](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/c.md) | `libmoss` | 0.29.0 | `moss_inference_new`, `moss_inference_free` |

## Guides

> [card] [Python](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/python.md)
>
> An async client in the `moss` package.

> [card] [JavaScript](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/javascript.md)
>
> A drop-in for OpenAI's client, plus `indexes`.

> [card] [Browser](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/browser.md)
>
> Call from a page, with the project key kept on your server.

> [card] [Swift](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/swift.md)
>
> `responses.create`, and `createStreaming` for events.

> [card] [Android](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/android.md)
>
> A Kotlin client to call from `Dispatchers.IO`.

> [card] [Elixir](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/elixir.md)
>
> `Moss.Inference.Responses.create/3`, from any process.

> [card] [C](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/c.md)
>
> Requests and responses as JSON, with an event callback.

<!-- Page: Python · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/python.md · local: pages/inference/sdks/python.md -->

# Python

> The Python client for Moss Inference: OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes.

`MossInference` is the Python client for [Moss Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/overview.md). Its `responses.create` takes OpenAI's Responses arguments, searches your indexes, and returns OpenAI's field names.

## Install

```bash theme={null}
pip install "moss>=1.22.0"
```

`MossInference` needs `moss` 1.22.0 or later. Earlier versions have `chat.completions.create` instead. See the [changelog](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/changelog.md). For the rest of the SDK setup, see [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/api.md#install).

## Create a client

```python theme={null}
import os

from moss import MossInference

client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"])
```

Copy the project id and key from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). Build one client and reuse it for every call. To close its connections, call `await client.close()` or use `async with client:`.

The API is async only. The examples below use this `client` inside an `async` function. With `MOSS_PROJECT_ID` and `MOSS_PROJECT_KEY` set, `from moss import inference` gives you `inference.responses.create` with no client to build.

## Get a response

```python theme={null}
response = await client.responses.create(
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
)
print(response.output_text)
```

`response.output_text` joins the text of the response's messages. `response.output` holds its items.

`response.request_id` is the response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. A stream has the same `stream.request_id`. Include it when you report a problem. Both are `None` when the response has none.

Moss stores no response, so `input` holds the whole conversation. Pass a string, or a list of items such as `{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}` and the `output` items of earlier responses. See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).

## Stream a response

```python theme={null}
stream = await client.responses.create(
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    stream=True,
)
async with stream:
    async for event in stream:
        if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
            print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
```

Each event has OpenAI's `type`, such as `response.output_text.delta`, and the fields of that type. The stream ends after one of two events:

* `response.completed`, whose `event.response` is the whole response.
* `response.incomplete`, when `max_output_tokens` or a content filter cut the response short.

`await stream.get_final_response()` reads the rest of the stream and returns that response.

To stop early, `break` out of the loop. Leaving the `async with stream:` block closes the connection, which stops the model.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event.

## Ground it in your indexes

```python theme={null}
response = await client.responses.create(
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    indexes=["faq"],
)
```

Moss searches the `faq` index and adds what it finds to the prompt. The [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md) creates that index.

Without `indexes`, Moss does not search before the model runs. You can name at most 32.

`retrieve=False` skips the search on a call that names indexes.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

## Use a vendor model

Name a model from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same for every model. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists them all.

### On the Moss key

```python theme={null}
response = await client.responses.create(
    model="anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    indexes=["faq"],
)
```

Without your own key, a listed vendor model runs on the Moss key and bills your credits. [Routes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#routes) shows who bills each call.

A listed model that is not served right now raises `InferenceError` with `code` `"model_not_enabled"`. Send `moss/fastlane-1` or use your own key.

### With your own key

Pass your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key to a client as `api_key`:

```python theme={null}
own_client = MossInference(
    os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"],
    os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"],
    api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"],
)
response = await own_client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna",
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    indexes=["faq"],
)
```

The key goes in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header, never in the body. To use a key for one call only, pass `api_key` to `responses.create`.

The response's `model` is the name you sent. [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers model names and billing.

## Tool calls

Pass OpenAI function tools in `tools`. A function tool is flat, as in OpenAI's Responses API. Each call the model makes comes as a `ResponseFunctionToolCall` item of `output`.

Put the `output` items back into `input` as they are. Add one `function_call_output` item per call, and call again until the response has no calls:

```python theme={null}
import json

from moss.inference import ResponseFunctionToolCall


def lookup_order(order_id):
    return "Shipped on Oct 20."


tools = [{
    "type": "function",
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}},
}]
items = [{"role": "user", "content": "Where is order A1?"}]
while True:
    response = await client.responses.create(
        instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
        input=items,
        tools=tools,
    )
    items += response.output
    calls = [i for i in response.output if isinstance(i, ResponseFunctionToolCall)]
    if not calls:
        print(response.output_text)
        break
    for call in calls:
        output = lookup_order(json.loads(call.arguments)["id"])
        items.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call.call_id, "output": output})
```

`lookup_order` stands for your own code, and it returns text. Each item goes back as its `raw` JSON. It keeps every field the model sent, such as the thought signature Gemini needs in the next turn.

[Tool calling](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) covers `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` and structured output.

## MCP servers

An `McpServer` in `tools` names an MCP server. Moss Inference runs its tools for the model, so your code sends no `function_call_output` items for them.

```python theme={null}
from moss.inference import McpCall, McpServer

crm = McpServer(
    server_label="crm",
    server_url="https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer your-crm-token"},
)
stream = await client.responses.create(
    instructions="You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input="Where is order A1?",
    tools=[crm],
    stream=True,
)
async with stream:
    async for event in stream:
        if event.type == "response.output_item.done" and isinstance(event.item, McpCall):
            print(event.item.name, event.item.output)
        elif event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
            print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
```

Each call comes as an `McpCall` item. It arrives in `response.output_item.added` when it starts, and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `output`.

Send the items back in `input` with the rest of `output`. The model then sees the earlier tool results.

MCP failures raise `InferenceError` with `status`, `type`, `code` and `retry_after`. A call that fails after a tool ran has `code` `"failed_after_tool_call"`. The tool may already have changed data, so Moss Inference does not retry the call. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

[MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) covers the server fields and every MCP error.

## Errors

A failed call raises `moss.inference.InferenceError`. Once a stream has started, it raises from the `async for` loop. A `response.failed` event raises it too.

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `status` | The HTTP status of a refused request. |
| `type` | The kind of failure. |
| `message` | What went wrong. Also `str(error)`. |
| `code` | The error code Moss Inference sent, such as `"rate_limit_exceeded"`. |
| `request_id` | The response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. |
| `retry_after` | Seconds to wait, from a `Retry-After` header. |

A field the failure lacks is `None`.

The SDK sets these types itself, with `status` `None`:

| `type` | Cause |
| - | - |
| `invalid_request_error` | An argument rejected before sending, such as an empty key or an index name that is empty or holds a comma. |
| `connection_error` | Moss Inference unreachable, or the connection broke. |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out, such as `timeout` or `idle_timeout`. |
| `incomplete_stream` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. |
| `server_error` | A stream event over 1 MiB, or one that is not a JSON object. |

Every other error carries what Moss Inference sent. [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every code. For a `429`, see [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## Options

`MossInference(project_id, project_key, ...)`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `project_id`, `project_key` | required | Your project id and key. |
| `api_key` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, for a vendor `model`. Sent as `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, never in the body. An empty key raises `InferenceError`. |
| `timeout` | none | Seconds for a whole call, stream included. 0 or less turns it off. |
| `idle_timeout` | `120` | Seconds to wait for the response to start, and for each pause in it. 0 or less turns it off. `None` keeps 120. |
| `max_retries` | `2` | Retries before the response starts. `0` turns them off. |
| `default_headers` | none | Headers sent with every call. |

`responses.create(...)` takes keyword arguments only:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `model` | `"moss"` | `moss` is an alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. Or a listed vendor model on the Moss key, or any vendor model with your `api_key`. |
| `input` | required | A string, or a list of OpenAI input item dicts and earlier `output` items. |
| `instructions` | none | The system message, before `input`. |
| `stream` | `False` | `True` returns a `ResponseStream` of `ResponseStreamEvent`. Otherwise one `Response`. |
| `tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` | none | Flat function tools and `McpServer`s, and how the model may call them. |
| `max_output_tokens` | none | The most tokens the response may have. |
| `indexes` | none | Index names to search, at most 32. Without it, Moss does not search before the model runs. |
| `retrieve` | `True` | `False` skips the search even when indexes are named. |
| `cache` | `True` | `True` can answer an identical request from the reply cache. `False` always asks the model. |
| `api_key` | the client's | Your vendor key for this call. |
| `timeout`, `idle_timeout` | the client's | This call's limits. 0 or less turns one off. `None` keeps the client's. |
| `max_retries` | the client's | This call's retries. |
| `extra_headers` | none | Headers for this call, over `default_headers`. |
| `extra_body` | none | Extra body fields. |
| Other OpenAI arguments | none | `temperature`, `text` for structured output, `reasoning` and the rest. |

---

# JavaScript

> The JavaScript client for Moss Inference: OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes.

`MossInference` is the JavaScript client for [Moss Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/overview.md). Its `responses.create` takes OpenAI's Responses arguments plus `indexes`, searches those indexes, and returns OpenAI's shapes.

## Install

```bash theme={null}
npm install @moss-js/moss@^1.22.0
```

`MossInference` needs `@moss-js/moss` 1.22.0 or later. Earlier versions have `chat.completions.create` instead. See the [changelog](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/changelog.md). For the rest of the SDK setup, see [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/api.md#install).

## Create a client

```typescript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
```

Copy the project id and key from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). Build one client and reuse it for every call. It has nothing to close. The examples below use this `client`.

With `MOSS_PROJECT_ID` and `MOSS_PROJECT_KEY` set, `import { inference } from '@moss-js/moss'` gives you `inference.responses.create` with no client to build.

## Get a response

```typescript theme={null}
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
})
console.log(response.output_text)
```

`response.output_text` joins the text of the response's messages. `response.output` holds its items.

`response.requestId` is the response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. A stream has the same `stream.requestId`. Include it when you report a problem. Both are `undefined` when the response has none.

Moss stores no response, so `input` holds the whole conversation. Pass a string, or a list of items such as `{ role: 'user', content: 'Hi' }` and the `output` items of earlier responses. See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).

## Stream a response

```typescript theme={null}
const stream = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  stream: true,
})
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? '')
}
```

Each event is the JSON Moss Inference sent, with OpenAI's `type`, such as `response.output_text.delta`. The stream ends after one of two events:

* `response.completed`, whose `event.response` is the whole response.
* `response.incomplete`, when `max_output_tokens` or a content filter cut the response short.

`await stream.finalResponse()` reads the rest of the stream and returns that response.

To stop early, leave the loop or call `stream.controller.abort()`. Either one closes the connection, which stops the model, and neither throws.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event.

## Ground it in your indexes

```typescript theme={null}
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
})
```

Moss searches the `faq` index and adds what it finds to the prompt. The [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md) creates that index.

Without `indexes`, Moss does not search before the model runs. You can name at most 32.

`retrieve: false` skips the search on a call that names indexes.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

## Use a vendor model

Name a model from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same for every model. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists them all.

### On the Moss key

```typescript theme={null}
const response = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5',
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
})
```

Without your own key, a listed vendor model runs on the Moss key and bills your credits. [Routes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#routes) shows who bills each call.

A listed model that is not served right now throws `InferenceError` with `errorCode` `'model_not_enabled'`. Send `moss/fastlane-1` or use your own key.

### With your own key

Pass your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key to a client as `apiKey`:

```typescript theme={null}
const ownClient = new MossInference(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!, {
  apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
})
const response = await ownClient.responses.create({
  model: 'gpt-6-luna',
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Do you ship to Canada?',
  indexes: ['faq'],
})
```

The key goes in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header, never in the body. To use a key for one call only, pass `{ apiKey }` as the second argument of `responses.create`.

The response's `model` is the name you sent. [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers model names and billing.

## Tool calls

`tools`, `tool_choice` and `parallel_tool_calls` take OpenAI's Responses shapes, so a function tool is flat. Each call the model makes comes as a `function_call` item of `output`.

Push the `output` items onto `input` unchanged. Add one `function_call_output` item per call, and call again until the response has no calls:

```typescript theme={null}
import type { FunctionTool, ResponseInputItem } from '@moss-js/moss'

const lookupOrder = (id: string) => 'Shipped on Oct 20.'

const tools: FunctionTool[] = [
  {
    type: 'function',
    name: 'lookup_order',
    description: 'Look up an order by its id.',
    parameters: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id'] },
  },
]
const input: ResponseInputItem[] = [{ role: 'user', content: 'Where is order A1?' }]

for (;;) {
  const stream = await client.responses.create({
    instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
    input,
    tools,
    stream: true,
  })
  for await (const event of stream) {
    if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? '')
  }
  const { output } = await stream.finalResponse()
  input.push(...output)
  const calls = output.filter((item) => item.type === 'function_call')
  if (calls.length === 0) break
  for (const call of calls) {
    const { id } = JSON.parse(call.arguments)
    input.push({ type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.call_id, output: lookupOrder(id) })
  }
}
```

`lookupOrder` stands for your own code. Push the items unchanged to keep every field the model sent. Gemini, for one, needs its thought signature in the next turn.

`finalResponse()` also works without the `for await` loop. Without `stream: true`, `create` returns the response directly.

[Tool calling](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) covers `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` and structured output.

## MCP servers

An `McpServer` entry in `tools` names an MCP server. Moss Inference calls its tools for the model during the response, so your code sends no `function_call_output` items for them.

```typescript theme={null}
import type { McpServer } from '@moss-js/moss'

const crm: McpServer = {
  type: 'mcp',
  server_label: 'crm',
  server_url: 'https://mcp.example.com/mcp',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CRM_TOKEN}` },
}
const stream = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: 'You are the support agent for Acme.',
  input: 'Where is order A1?',
  tools: [crm],
  stream: true,
})
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === 'response.output_item.done' && event.item?.type === 'mcp_call') {
    console.log(event.item.server_label, event.item.name, event.item.output)
  } else if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') {
    process.stdout.write(event.delta ?? '')
  }
}
```

Each call comes as an `mcp_call` item. It arrives in `response.output_item.added` when it starts, and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `output`.

Send the items back in `input` with the rest of `output`. The model then sees the earlier tool results.

MCP failures throw `InferenceError` with `status`, `type`, `errorCode` and `retryAfter`. A call that fails after a tool ran has `errorCode` `'failed_after_tool_call'`. The tool may already have changed data, so Moss Inference does not retry the call. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

[MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) covers the server fields and every MCP error.

## Errors

Every failure other than an abort throws `InferenceError`. Once a stream has started, it throws from the `for await` loop. A `response.failed` event throws it too.

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `status` | The HTTP status of a refused request. |
| `type` | The kind of failure. |
| `message` | What went wrong. |
| `errorCode` | The error code Moss Inference sent, such as `"rate_limit_exceeded"`. |
| `requestId` | The response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. |
| `retryAfter` | Milliseconds to wait, from a `Retry-After` header. |

A field the failure lacks is `undefined`. The error also has a Moss `code`, so [`isMossError`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/functions/isMossError) accepts it.

The SDK sets these types itself, with `status` `undefined`:

| `type` | Cause |
| - | - |
| `invalid_request_error` | An argument rejected before sending, such as an empty key, an index name that is empty or holds a comma, or an unset `MOSS_PROJECT_ID` for `inference`. |
| `connection_error` | Moss Inference unreachable, or the connection broke. |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out, such as `timeout` or `idleTimeout`. |
| `incomplete_stream` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. |
| `server_error` | A stream event over 1 MiB, or one that is not a JSON object. |

Every other error carries what Moss Inference sent. [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every code. For a `429`, see [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## Options

`new MossInference(projectId, projectKey, options?)`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `apiKey` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, for a vendor `model`. Sent as `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, never in the body. An empty key throws `InferenceError`. |
| `timeout` | none | Milliseconds for a whole call, stream included. `null` turns it off. |
| `idleTimeout` | `120_000` | Milliseconds to wait for the response to start, and for each pause in it. `null` turns it off. |
| `maxRetries` | `2` | Retries before the response starts. `0` turns them off. |
| `headers` | none | Headers sent with every call. |

`responses.create(params, options?)` takes OpenAI's fields and the Moss fields in `params`. Settings for this call only go in `options`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `model` | `"moss"` | `moss` is an alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. Or a listed vendor model on the Moss key, or any vendor model with your `apiKey`. |
| `input` | required | A string, or a list of messages, `function_call_output` items and earlier `output` items. |
| `instructions` | none | The system message, before `input`. |
| `stream` | `false` | `true` resolves to a `ResponseStream` of events. Otherwise to one `Response`. |
| `tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` | none | Flat function tools and `McpServer` entries, and how the model may call them. |
| `max_output_tokens` | none | The most tokens the response may have. |
| `indexes` | none | Index names to search, at most 32. Without it, Moss does not search before the model runs. |
| `cache` | `true` | `true` can answer an identical request from the reply cache. `false` always asks the model. |
| `retrieve` | `true` | `false` skips the search even when indexes are named. |
| Other OpenAI fields | none | `temperature`, `text` for structured output, `reasoning` and the rest. An `apiKey` or `api_key` field throws. |
| `options.apiKey` | the client's | Your vendor key for this call. |
| `options.timeout`, `options.idleTimeout` | the client's | This call's limits. `null` turns one off. |
| `options.maxRetries` | the client's | This call's retries. |
| `options.headers` | none | Headers for this call. They add to the client's, or replace them by name. |
| `options.signal` | none | An `AbortSignal` that cancels the call. |

# Browser

> The browser client for Moss Inference: OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes.

`MossInference` is the browser client for [Moss Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/overview.md). Its `responses.create` takes OpenAI's Responses arguments plus `indexes`, and returns OpenAI's shapes.

Moss Inference searches your indexes in the cloud, so the page loads no index. The client works like the [JavaScript client](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/javascript.md). This page covers what differs in the browser.

## Install

```bash theme={null}
npm install @moss-dev/moss-web@^1.8.0
```

`MossInference` needs `@moss-dev/moss-web` 1.8.0 or later. For the rest of the SDK setup, see [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/browser/api.md#install).

## Create a client

```typescript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from "@moss-dev/moss-web";

const client = new MossInference("your_project_id", "your_project_key");
```

Copy the project id and key from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). CORS is open, so the page can call Moss Inference directly.

> [!WARNING]
>
> A project key in page code is visible to every visitor. It can also create and delete your indexes. Keep direct calls to prototypes, local demos and internal tools.

On a public page, pass `null` for both and a `baseURL` path served by a route of yours that adds them:

```typescript theme={null}
import { MossInference } from "@moss-dev/moss-web";

const client = new MossInference(null, null, { baseURL: "/moss/v1" });
```

[Keep the project key on your server](#keep-the-project-key-on-your-server) shows that route.

Build one client and reuse it for every call. It has nothing to close. The examples below use the first `client`, which calls Moss Inference directly.

## Get a response

```typescript theme={null}
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
});
document.querySelector("#answer")!.textContent = response.output_text;
```

`response.output_text` joins the text of the response's messages. `response.output` holds its items.

`response.requestId` is the response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. A stream has the same `stream.requestId`. Include it when you report a problem. Both are `undefined` when the response has none.

Moss stores no response, so `input` holds the whole conversation. Pass a string, or a list of items such as `{ role: "user", content: "Hi" }` and the `output` items of earlier responses. See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).

## Stream a response

```typescript theme={null}
const answer = document.querySelector("#answer")!;

const stream = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  stream: true,
});
document.querySelector("#stop")!.addEventListener("click", () => stream.controller.abort());
for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === "response.output_text.delta") answer.textContent += event.delta ?? "";
}
```

Each event has OpenAI's `type`, such as `response.output_text.delta`. The stream ends after one of two events:

* `response.completed`, whose `event.response` is the whole response.
* `response.incomplete`, when `max_output_tokens` or a content filter cut the response short.

`await stream.finalResponse()` reads the rest of the stream and returns that response.

To stop early, leave the loop or call `stream.controller.abort()`, as the stop button does. Either one closes the connection, which stops the model, and neither throws.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event.

## Ground it in your indexes

```typescript theme={null}
const response = await client.responses.create({
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  indexes: ["faq"],
});
```

Moss searches the `faq` index and adds what it finds to the prompt. The [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md) creates that index.

Without `indexes`, Moss does not search before the model runs. You can name at most 32.

`retrieve: false` skips the search on a call that names indexes. Through a [server route](#keep-the-project-key-on-your-server), the route picks the indexes instead.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

## Use a vendor model

Name a model from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same for every model. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists them all.

### On the Moss key

```typescript theme={null}
const response = await client.responses.create({
  model: "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  indexes: ["faq"],
});
```

Without your own key, a listed vendor model runs on the Moss key and bills your credits. [Routes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#routes) shows who bills each call.

A listed model that is not served right now throws `InferenceError` with `errorCode` `"model_not_enabled"`. Send `moss/fastlane-1` or use your own key.

### With your own key

Pass your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key to a client as `apiKey`:

```typescript theme={null}
const ownClient = new MossInference("your_project_id", "your_project_key", {
  apiKey: "your_openai_api_key",
});
const response = await ownClient.responses.create({
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  indexes: ["faq"],
});
```

The key goes in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header, never in the body. To use a key for one call only, pass `{ apiKey }` as the second argument of `responses.create`.

Every visitor can read a key in page code, like a project key. On a public page, your server route sets `X-Moss-Provider-Key` itself.

[Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers model names and billing.

## Tool calls

`tools`, `tool_choice` and `parallel_tool_calls` take OpenAI's Responses shapes, so a function tool is flat. Each call the model makes comes as a `function_call` item of `output`, and your code runs it.

Push the `output` items onto `input` unchanged. Add one `function_call_output` item per call, and call again until the response has no calls:

```typescript theme={null}
import type { FunctionTool, ResponseInputItem } from "@moss-dev/moss-web";

const lookupOrder = (id: string) => "Shipped on Oct 20.";

const answer = document.querySelector("#answer")!;
const tools: FunctionTool[] = [
  {
    type: "function",
    name: "lookup_order",
    parameters: { type: "object", properties: { id: { type: "string" } }, required: ["id"] },
  },
];
const input: ResponseInputItem[] = [{ role: "user", content: "Where is order A1?" }];

for (;;) {
  const stream = await client.responses.create({
    instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    input,
    tools,
    stream: true,
  });
  for await (const event of stream) {
    if (event.type === "response.output_text.delta") answer.textContent += event.delta ?? "";
  }
  const { output } = await stream.finalResponse();
  input.push(...output);
  const calls = output.filter((item) => item.type === "function_call");
  if (calls.length === 0) break;
  for (const call of calls) {
    const { id } = JSON.parse(call.arguments);
    input.push({ type: "function_call_output", call_id: call.call_id, output: lookupOrder(id) });
  }
}
```

`lookupOrder` stands for your own code, and it returns text. Push the items unchanged to keep every field the model sent.

`finalResponse()` also works without the `for await` loop. A second call returns the same response. It rejects with what the loop would throw, or with the signal's reason after an abort. Without `stream: true`, `create` returns the response directly.

[Tool calling](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) covers `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` and structured output.

## MCP servers

Add MCP entries in your [server route](#keep-the-project-key-on-your-server), never in page code. Moss Inference calls the server's tools for the model during the response, so your code sends no `function_call_output` items for them.

Each call comes as an `mcp_call` item. It arrives in `response.output_item.added` when it starts, and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `output`.

Send the items back in `input` with the rest of `output`. The model then sees the earlier tool results.

MCP failures throw `InferenceError` with `status`, `type`, `errorCode` and `retryAfter`. A call that fails after a tool ran has `errorCode` `"failed_after_tool_call"`. The tool may already have changed data, so Moss Inference does not retry the call. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

[MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) covers the server fields and every MCP error.

## Errors

Every failure other than an abort throws `InferenceError`. Once a stream has started, it throws from the `for await` loop.

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `status` | The HTTP status of a refused request. |
| `type` | The kind of failure. |
| `message` | What went wrong. |
| `errorCode` | The error code Moss Inference sent, such as `"rate_limit_exceeded"`. |
| `requestId` | The response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. |
| `retryAfter` | Milliseconds to wait, from a `Retry-After` header. |

A field the failure lacks is `undefined`. A call without `baseURL` gets no `retryAfter`, because Moss Inference does not expose `Retry-After` to the page.

The SDK sets these types itself, with `status` `undefined`:

| `type` | Cause |
| - | - |
| `invalid_request_error` | An argument rejected before sending, such as an empty key, an index name that is empty or holds a comma, `null` credentials without `baseURL`, or a `baseURL` that is not a path on the page's origin. |
| `connection_error` | Your route or Moss Inference unreachable, a call the browser blocked, such as over CORS, or a broken connection. |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out, such as `timeout` or `idleTimeout`. |
| `incomplete_stream` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. |
| `server_error` | A stream event over 1 MiB, or one that is not a JSON object. |

Every other error carries what Moss Inference sent. [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every code. For a `429`, see [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## Options

`new MossInference(projectId, projectKey, options?)`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `baseURL` | none | A path on the page's origin, such as `/moss/v1`, with no query or fragment. Required when the id and key are `null`. Without it, calls go to `https://inference.moss.dev/v1`. |
| `apiKey` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, for a vendor `model`. Sent as `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, never in the body. Every visitor can read it in page code. An empty key throws `InferenceError`. |
| `timeout` | none | Milliseconds for a whole call, stream included. `null` turns it off. |
| `idleTimeout` | `120_000` | Milliseconds to wait for the response to start, and for each pause in it. `null` turns it off. |
| `maxRetries` | `2` | Retries before the response starts. `0` turns them off. |
| `headers` | none | Headers sent with every call. |

Each call resolves `baseURL` against the page, so a client built during server rendering works in the browser.

`responses.create(params, options?)` takes OpenAI's fields and the Moss fields in `params`. Settings for this call only go in `options`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `model` | `"moss"` | `moss` is an alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. Or a listed vendor model on the Moss key, or any vendor model with your `apiKey`. |
| `input` | required | A string, or a list of messages, `function_call_output` items and earlier `output` items. |
| `instructions` | none | The system message, before `input`. |
| `stream` | `false` | `true` resolves to a `ResponseStream` of events. Otherwise to one `Response`. |
| `tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` | none | Flat function tools and MCP entries, and how the model may call them. |
| `max_output_tokens` | none | The most tokens the response may have. |
| `indexes` | none | Index names to search, at most 32. Without it, Moss does not search, except through a server route. |
| `cache` | `true` | `true` can answer an identical request from the reply cache. `false` always asks the model. |
| `retrieve` | `true` | `false` skips the search even when indexes are named. |
| Other OpenAI fields | none | `temperature`, `text` for structured output, `reasoning` and the rest. An `apiKey` or `api_key` field throws. |
| `options.apiKey` | the client's | Your vendor key for this call. |
| `options.timeout`, `options.idleTimeout` | the client's | This call's limits. `null` turns one off. |
| `options.maxRetries` | the client's | This call's retries. |
| `options.headers` | none | Headers for this call. They add to the client's, or replace them by name. |
| `options.signal` | none | An `AbortSignal` that cancels the call. |

## Keep the project key on your server

A public page calls Moss Inference through a route of yours. The route adds the project id and key on your server, so the key never reaches the page. This one serves `POST /moss/v1/responses`:

```typescript theme={null}
import { isSignedIn } from "./session";

const ENDPOINT = "https://inference.moss.dev/v1/responses";
const INDEXES = ["faq"];
const FORWARD = ["content-type", "accept"];
const REPLY = ["content-type", "retry-after", "x-moss-request-id"];

export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  if (!(await isSignedIn(request))) {
    return Response.json({ detail: "Sign in first." }, { status: 401 });
  }
  const { MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY } = process.env;
  const indexes = request.headers.get("x-moss-indexes")?.split(",") ?? INDEXES;
  if (!indexes.every((name) => INDEXES.includes(name))) {
    return Response.json({ detail: "This page cannot search that index." }, { status: 403 });
  }
  const headers = new Headers();
  for (const name of FORWARD) {
    const value = request.headers.get(name);
    if (value !== null) headers.set(name, value);
  }
  headers.set("X-Moss-Indexes", indexes.join(","));
  headers.set("Authorization", `Bearer ${MOSS_PROJECT_ID}:${MOSS_PROJECT_KEY}`);
  const reply = await fetch(ENDPOINT, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: await request.text(),
    signal: request.signal,
    redirect: "manual",
  });
  const replyHeaders = [...reply.headers].filter(([name]) => REPLY.includes(name));
  return new Response(reply.body, { status: reply.status, headers: replyHeaders });
}
```

Every call spends your credits, so the route answers only a visitor your own session check accepts.

Every visitor can set any header, so the route forwards only the headers it names. It refuses an index outside its list with `403`. It always sends `X-Moss-Indexes`, because a call without it does no search.

As a result, `retrieve`, `cache`, an empty `indexes` list and `apiKey` in page code do not reach Moss Inference. A route that wants them sets `X-Moss-Retrieve`, `X-Moss-Cache` or `X-Moss-Provider-Key` itself.

With `null` credentials, the client sends no `Authorization` header. A header you pass in `headers`, such as the visitor's session token, then reaches the route.

---

<!-- Page: Swift · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/swift.md · local: pages/inference/sdks/swift.md -->

# Swift

> The Swift client for Moss Inference: OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes.

`MossInference` is the Swift client for [Moss Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/overview.md). It searches your indexes in the cloud and answers in the shape of OpenAI's Responses API. `responses.create` returns the whole response, and `createStreaming` streams its events.

## Install

```swift theme={null}
dependencies: [
  .package(url: "https://github.com/usemoss/moss", from: "0.15.0"),
],
targets: [
  .target(name: "YourTarget", dependencies: [
    .product(name: "Moss", package: "moss"),
  ]),
]
```

`MossInference` needs the `Moss` Swift package 0.13.0 or later. For Xcode and the rest of the SDK setup, see [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/swift/api.md#install).

## Create a client

```swift theme={null}
import Foundation
import Moss

let client = try MossInference(
  projectId: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"]!,
  projectKey: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"]!
)
```

Copy the project id and key from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). Build one client and reuse it for every call. The initializer throws [`InferenceError`](#errors) for an argument it refuses.

The examples below use this `client`. Every call is `async` and throws, so each one takes `try await`.

## Get a response

```swift theme={null}
let response = try await client.responses.create(
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme."
)
print(response.outputText)
```

`response.outputText` joins the text of the response's messages. `response.output` holds its `OutputItem`s: `.message`, `.functionCall`, `.mcpCall`, or `.other` for any other type. Each one has its JSON in `raw`.

`response.requestId` is the response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. A stream has the same `stream.requestId`. Include it when you report a problem. Both are `nil` when the response has none.

Moss stores no response, so `input` holds the whole conversation. Pass a string, or an array of `InputItem`s:

* `.system`, `.developer`, `.user` and `.assistant` take the text of a message, such as `.user("Hi")`.
* `.functionCallOutput(callId:output:)` takes a tool's result.
* `InputItem(item)` sends back an `output` item of an earlier response.
* `.raw` takes any other item as a JSON object.

See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).

## Stream a response

```swift theme={null}
let stream = try await client.responses.createStreaming(
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme."
)
for try await event in stream where event.type == "response.output_text.delta" {
  print(event.delta ?? "", terminator: "")
}
```

`createStreaming` takes the same arguments as `create`. Each `ResponseStreamEvent` has OpenAI's `type`, such as `response.output_text.delta`, and the fields of that type. The stream ends after one of two events:

* `response.completed`, whose `event.response` is the whole response.
* `response.incomplete`, when `maxOutputTokens` or a content filter cut the response short.

To stop early, call `stream.cancel()`. It closes the connection, which stops the model, and ends the loop without an error.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event.

## Ground it in your indexes

```swift theme={null}
let response = try await client.responses.create(
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  indexes: ["faq"]
)
```

Moss searches the `faq` index and adds what it finds to the prompt. The [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md) creates that index.

Without `indexes`, Moss does not search before the model runs. You can name at most 32.

`retrieve: false` skips the search on a call that names indexes.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

## Use a vendor model

Name a model from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same for every model. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists them all.

### On the Moss key

```swift theme={null}
let response = try await client.responses.create(
  model: "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  indexes: ["faq"]
)
```

Without your own key, a listed vendor model runs on the Moss key and bills your credits. [Routes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#routes) shows who bills each call.

A listed model that is not served right now throws `InferenceError` with `code` `"model_not_enabled"`. Send `moss/fastlane-1` or use your own key.

### With your own key

Pass your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key to a client as `apiKey`:

```swift theme={null}
let ownClient = try MossInference(
  projectId: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"]!,
  projectKey: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"]!,
  apiKey: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["OPENAI_API_KEY"]!
)
let response = try await ownClient.responses.create(
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  indexes: ["faq"]
)
```

The key goes in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header, never in the body. To use a key for one call only, pass `apiKey` to `create` or `createStreaming`.

[Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers model names and billing.

## Tool calls

Pass your functions in `tools`, as the flat function tools of OpenAI's Responses API. Each call the model makes comes as a `.functionCall` item of `output`.

Put the `output` items back into `input` with `InputItem(item)`. Add one `.functionCallOutput(callId:output:)` per call, and call again until the response has no calls:

```swift theme={null}
func lookupOrder(_ arguments: String) -> String {
  "Shipped on Oct 20."
}

let tools: [Tool] = [
  .function(
    name: "lookup_order",
    description: "Find an order by its id.",
    parameters: ["type": "object", "properties": ["id": ["type": "string"]], "required": ["id"]]
  )
]
var input: [InputItem] = [.user("Where is order A1?")]
while true {
  let response = try await client.responses.create(
    input: .items(input),
    instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    tools: tools
  )
  input += response.output.map(InputItem.init)
  var called = false
  for case .functionCall(let call) in response.output {
    input.append(.functionCallOutput(callId: call.callId, output: lookupOrder(call.arguments)))
    called = true
  }
  if !called {
    print(response.outputText)
    break
  }
}
```

`lookupOrder` stands for your own code, and it returns a `String`. `InputItem(item)` sends the item's `raw` JSON. It keeps every field the model sent, such as the thought signature Gemini needs in the next turn.

[Tool calling](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) covers tool choice, parallel calls and structured output.

## MCP servers

An `McpServer` in `tools` names an MCP server. Moss Inference runs its tools for the model, so your code sends no `.functionCallOutput` items for them.

```swift theme={null}
let crm = McpServer(
  serverLabel: "crm",
  serverURL: "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
  headers: ["Authorization": "Bearer your-crm-token"]
)
let stream = try await client.responses.createStreaming(
  input: "Where is order A1?",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  tools: [.mcp(crm)]
)
for try await event in stream {
  switch (event.type, event.item) {
  case ("response.output_item.done", .mcpCall(let call)?): print(call.name, call.output ?? "")
  case ("response.output_text.delta", _): print(event.delta ?? "", terminator: "")
  default: break
  }
}
```

`McpServer` also takes `allowedTools`, and `transport` as `.streamableHTTP` or `.sse`.

Each call comes as an `.mcpCall` item. It arrives in `response.output_item.added` when it starts, and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `output`.

An `McpCall` has the call's `serverLabel`, `name` and `arguments`. Once the call has ended, it also has its `status`, `output` or `error`, and `durationMs`.

Send the items back in `input` with the rest of `output`. The model then sees the earlier tool results.

MCP failures throw `InferenceError` with `status`, `type`, `code` and `retryAfter`. A call that fails after a tool ran has `code` `"failed_after_tool_call"`. The tool may already have changed data, so Moss Inference does not retry the call. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

[MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) covers the server fields and every MCP error.

## Errors

A failed call throws `InferenceError`. Once a stream has started, it throws from the `for try await` loop. A `response.failed` event throws it too.

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `status` | The HTTP status of a refused request. |
| `type` | The kind of failure. |
| `message` | What went wrong. |
| `code` | The error code Moss Inference sent, such as `"rate_limit_exceeded"`. |
| `requestId` | The response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. |
| `retryAfter` | Seconds to wait, from a `Retry-After` header. |

A field the failure lacks is `nil`.

The SDK sets these types itself, with `status` `nil`:

| `type` | Cause |
| - | - |
| `invalid_request_error` | An argument rejected before sending, such as an empty key or an index name that is empty or holds a comma. |
| `connection_error` | Moss Inference unreachable, or the connection broke. |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out, such as `timeout` or `idleTimeout`. |
| `incomplete_stream` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. |
| `server_error` | A stream event over 1 MiB, or one that is not a JSON object. |

Every other error carries what Moss Inference sent. [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every code. For a `429`, see [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## Options

`MossInference(...)`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `projectId`, `projectKey` | required | Your project id and key. |
| `apiKey` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, for a vendor `model`. Sent as `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, never in the body. An empty key throws `InferenceError`. |
| `timeout` | none | Seconds for a whole call, stream included. `nil` or `.infinity` turns it off. |
| `idleTimeout` | `120` | Seconds to wait for the response to start, and for each pause in it. `nil` or `.infinity` turns it off. |
| `maxRetries` | `2` | Retries before the response starts. `0` turns them off. |

`create` and `createStreaming` take the same labeled arguments, in this order:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `model` | `"moss"` | `moss` is an alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. Or a listed vendor model on the Moss key, or any vendor model with your `apiKey`. |
| `input` | required | A string literal or `.text(string)`, or an array literal or `.items(array)` of `InputItem`. |
| `instructions` | `nil` | The system message, before `input`. |
| `tools` | `[]` | `[Tool]`: `.function(name:description:parameters:strict:)` for your function, `.mcp(server)` for an MCP server, `.raw(object)` for any other entry. |
| `toolChoice` | `nil` | `.auto`, `.required`, `.function(name)`, `.never` (sent as `none`), or `.raw(object)` for any other object. |
| `parallelToolCalls` | `nil` | Whether the model may call several tools at once. |
| `maxOutputTokens` | `nil` | The most tokens the response may have. |
| `indexes` | none | Index names to search, at most 32. Without it, Moss does not search before the model runs. |
| `retrieve` | `true` | `false` skips the search even when indexes are named. |
| `cache` | `true` | `true` can answer an identical request from the reply cache. `false` always asks the model. |
| `apiKey` | the client's | Your vendor key for this call. |
| `timeout`, `idleTimeout` | the client's | This call's limits. `.infinity` turns one off. `nil` keeps the client's. |
| `maxRetries` | the client's | This call's retries. |
| `extra` | `[:]` | Other OpenAI body fields as `[String: JSONValue]`, such as `["temperature": 0.2]` or `["text": ["format": ...]]`. The typed arguments win over the same keys. `stream` is always `true`. |

---

<!-- Page: Android · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/android.md · local: pages/inference/sdks/android.md -->

# Android

> The Android client for Moss Inference: OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes.

`MossInference` is the Kotlin client for [Moss Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/overview.md) on Android. It searches your indexes and answers in the shape of OpenAI's Responses API, with camelCase fields. `responses.create` returns the whole response, and `createStreaming` streams its events.

## Install

```bash theme={null}
VERSION=0.31.0
mkdir -p app/libs
curl -fL -o app/libs/moss-android.aar \
  "https://github.com/usemoss/moss/releases/download/android-sdk-v${VERSION}/moss-android-${VERSION}.aar"
```

Then add the AAR in `app/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin theme={null}
dependencies {
    implementation(files("libs/moss-android.aar"))
}
```

`MossInference` needs the `moss-android` AAR 0.29.0 or later. For the rest of the SDK setup, see [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/android/getting-started.md#install).

## Create a client

```kotlin theme={null}
import dev.usemoss.moss.MossInference

val inference = MossInference(projectId = projectId, projectKey = projectKey)
```

`projectId` and `projectKey` are your project id and key. Copy them from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). Build one client and reuse it for every call, from any thread.

Calls and stream reads block. On the main thread they throw `MossException`, so run them from `Dispatchers.IO`. The examples below use this `inference` client inside a coroutine.

## Get a response

```kotlin theme={null}
import dev.usemoss.moss.InputItem
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

val input = listOf(InputItem.user("Do you ship to Canada?"))

val response = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    inference.responses.create(
        input = input,
        instructions = "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    )
}
println(response.outputText)
```

`response.outputText` joins the text of the response's messages. `response.output` holds its items: `OutputItem.Message`, `FunctionCall`, `McpCall`, or `Other` for any other type. Each item has its JSON in `raw`.

`response.requestId` is the response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. A stream has the same `stream.requestId`. Include it when you report a problem. Both are `null` when the response has none.

Moss stores no response, so `input` holds the whole conversation. Build messages with `InputItem.user`, `system`, `developer` and `assistant`. Add the `output` items of earlier responses with `InputItem.of(item)`. See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).

## Stream a response

```kotlin theme={null}
import kotlinx.coroutines.ensureActive

withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    inference.responses.createStreaming(
        input = input,
        instructions = "You are the support agent for Acme.",
    ).use { stream ->
        for (event in stream) {
            ensureActive()
            if (event.type == "response.output_text.delta") print(event.delta)
        }
    }
}
```

Each `ResponseStreamEvent` has OpenAI's `type`, such as `response.output_text.delta`, and the fields of that type. The stream ends after one of two events:

* `response.completed`, whose `event.response` is the whole response.
* `response.incomplete`, when `maxOutputTokens` or a content filter cut the response short.

To stop early, leave `use` with a `break` or `return`. That closes the connection, which stops the model. Cancelling the coroutine alone does not. So the loop calls `ensureActive()`, whose throw leaves `use` the same way.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event.

## Ground it in your indexes

```kotlin theme={null}
val response = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    inference.responses.create(
        input = input,
        instructions = "You are the support agent for Acme.",
        indexes = listOf("faq"),
    )
}
```

Moss searches the `faq` index and adds what it finds to the prompt. The [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md) creates that index.

Without `indexes`, Moss does not search before the model runs. You can name at most 32.

`retrieve = false` skips the search on a call that names indexes.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

## Use a vendor model

Name a model from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same for every model. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists them all.

### On the Moss key

```kotlin theme={null}
val response = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    inference.responses.create(
        input = input,
        model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
        instructions = "You are the support agent for Acme.",
        indexes = listOf("faq"),
    )
}
```

Without your own key, a listed vendor model runs on the Moss key and bills your credits. [Routes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#routes) shows who bills each call.

A listed model that is not served right now throws `InferenceError` with `code` `"model_not_enabled"`. Send `moss/fastlane-1` or use your own key.

### With your own key

Pass your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key to a client as `apiKey`:

```kotlin theme={null}
val ownClient = MossInference(
    projectId = projectId,
    projectKey = projectKey,
    apiKey = openaiKey,
)

val response = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    ownClient.responses.create(
        input = input,
        model = "gpt-6-luna",
        instructions = "You are the support agent for Acme.",
        indexes = listOf("faq"),
    )
}
```

`openaiKey` is your OpenAI key. It goes in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header, never in the body. To use a key for one call only, pass `apiKey` to `responses.create` or `createStreaming`.

[Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers model names and billing.

## Tool calls

Pass `tools` as the flat function tools of OpenAI's Responses API. Each call the model makes comes as an `OutputItem.FunctionCall` item of `output`.

Append every `output` item with `InputItem.of(item)`, which sends it back unchanged. Add one `InputItem.functionCallOutput(callId, output)` per call, and call again until the response has no calls:

```kotlin theme={null}
import dev.usemoss.moss.OutputItem
import dev.usemoss.moss.Tool

fun lookupOrder(arguments: String): String = "Shipped on Oct 20."

val tools = listOf(
    Tool.function(
        name = "lookup_order",
        description = "Finds an order by its id.",
        parameters = """{"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]}""",
    ),
)

val answer = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    val items = mutableListOf<InputItem>(InputItem.user("Where is order A1?"))
    val instructions = "You are the support agent for Acme."
    var response = inference.responses.create(items, instructions = instructions, tools = tools)
    while (true) {
        items += response.output.map { InputItem.of(it) }
        val calls = response.output.filterIsInstance<OutputItem.FunctionCall>()
        if (calls.isEmpty()) break
        for (call in calls) {
            items += InputItem.functionCallOutput(call.callId, lookupOrder(call.arguments))
        }
        response = inference.responses.create(items, instructions = instructions, tools = tools)
    }
    response.outputText
}
println(answer)
```

`lookupOrder` stands for your own code. It takes the call's JSON arguments and returns the result as text. `InputItem.of(item)` keeps every field the model sent, such as the signature Gemini needs back in the next turn.

[Tool calling](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) covers `toolChoice`, `parallelToolCalls` and structured output.

## MCP servers

A `Tool.mcp` entry in `tools` names an MCP server. Moss Inference runs its tools for the model during the same call, so your code sends no `functionCallOutput` for them.

```kotlin theme={null}
import dev.usemoss.moss.McpServer

val crm = McpServer(
    serverLabel = "crm",
    serverUrl = "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
    headers = mapOf("Authorization" to "Bearer $crmToken"),
)

withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    inference.responses.createStreaming(
        listOf(InputItem.user("Where is order A1?")),
        instructions = "You are the support agent for Acme.",
        tools = listOf(Tool.mcp(crm)),
    ).use { stream ->
        for (event in stream) {
            ensureActive()
            val call = event.item as? OutputItem.McpCall
            if (call != null && event.type == "response.output_item.done") println("${call.name}: ${call.output}")
            if (event.type == "response.output_text.delta") print(event.delta)
        }
    }
}
```

`crmToken` is your CRM token. `McpServer` also takes `allowedTools` and `transport`, which is `McpServer.Transport.STREAMABLE_HTTP` or `SSE`.

Each call comes as an `OutputItem.McpCall`. It arrives in `response.output_item.added` when it starts, and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `output`.

An `McpCall` has the `serverLabel`, `name` and `arguments` of the call. Once the call ends, it also has its `status`, `output` or `error`, and `durationMs`.

Send the items back in `input` with the rest of `output`. The model then sees the earlier tool results.

MCP failures throw `InferenceError` with `status`, `type`, `code` and `retryAfterMs`. A call that fails after a tool ran has `code` `"failed_after_tool_call"`. The tool may already have changed data, so Moss Inference does not retry the call. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

[MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) covers the server fields and every MCP error.

## Errors

A failed call throws `InferenceError`. Once a stream has started, it throws from the `for` loop. A `response.failed` event throws it too.

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `status` | The HTTP status of a refused request. |
| `type` | The kind of failure. |
| `message` | What went wrong. |
| `code` | The error code Moss Inference sent, such as `"rate_limit_exceeded"`. |
| `requestId` | The response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. |
| `retryAfterMs` | Milliseconds to wait, from a `Retry-After` header. |

A field the failure lacks is `null`.

The SDK raises these errors itself. All but the first are an `InferenceError` with that `type` and `status` `null`:

| Error | Cause |
| - | - |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | An argument rejected before sending, such as a blank key or an index name that is blank or holds a comma. |
| `connection_error` | Moss Inference unreachable, or the connection broke. |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out, such as `timeoutMs` or `idleTimeoutMs`. |
| `incomplete_stream` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. |
| `server_error` | A stream event over 1 MiB, or one that is not a JSON object. |

Every other error carries what Moss Inference sent. [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every code. For a `429`, see [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## Options

`MossInference(...)`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `projectId`, `projectKey` | required | Your project id and key. |
| `apiKey` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, for a vendor `model`. Sent as `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, never in the body. A blank key throws `IllegalArgumentException`. |
| `timeoutMs` | none | Milliseconds for a whole call, stream included. `null` turns it off. |
| `idleTimeoutMs` | `120_000` | Milliseconds to wait for the response to start, and for each pause in it. `null` turns it off. |
| `maxRetries` | `2` | Retries before the response starts. `0` turns them off. |

`responses.create` and `createStreaming` take the same parameters, `input` first:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `input` | required | A `List<InputItem>`, built with `InputItem.user`, `system`, `developer`, `assistant`, `of(item)` and `functionCallOutput(callId, output)`. `InputItem.raw` takes any other item as the text of a JSON object. |
| `model` | `"moss"` | `moss` is an alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. Or a listed vendor model on the Moss key, or any vendor model with your `apiKey`. |
| `instructions` | none | The system message, before `input`. |
| `tools` | none | A `List<Tool>`: `Tool.function` for your function, `Tool.mcp` for an MCP server, `Tool.raw` for any other tool object. |
| `toolChoice` | none | `ToolChoice.AUTO`, `NONE`, `REQUIRED`, `ToolChoice.function(name)`, or `ToolChoice.raw(json)` for any other JSON object. |
| `parallelToolCalls` | none | Whether the model may call several tools at once. |
| `maxOutputTokens` | none | The most tokens the response may have. |
| `indexes` | none | Index names to search, at most 32. Without it, Moss does not search before the model runs. |
| `retrieve` | `true` | `false` skips the search even when indexes are named. |
| `cache` | `true` | `true` can answer an identical request from the reply cache. `false` always asks the model. |
| `apiKey` | the client's | Your vendor key for this call. |
| `extra` | none | Other OpenAI fields as JSON values, such as `temperature`, `text` for structured output or `reasoning`. Typed parameters win over `extra`. `stream` is always `true`. |
| `timeoutMs`, `idleTimeoutMs` | the client's | This call's limits. `null` turns one off. |
| `maxRetries` | the client's | This call's retries. |

---
