# Elixir

> The Elixir client for Moss Inference: OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes.

`Moss.Inference` is the Elixir client for [Moss Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/overview.md). Its `Responses.create/3` takes OpenAI's Responses body as a map and searches your indexes. It answers with OpenAI's field names as string keys.

## Install

```elixir theme={null}
# mix.exs
defp deps do
  [{:moss, "~> 1.11"}]
end
```

Then run `mix deps.get`. `Moss.Inference` needs `moss` 1.11.0 or later. For the rest of the SDK setup, see [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/elixir/api.md#install).

## Create a client

```elixir theme={null}
alias Moss.Inference.Responses

project_id = System.fetch_env!("MOSS_PROJECT_ID")
project_key = System.fetch_env!("MOSS_PROJECT_KEY")

client = Moss.Inference.new(project_id, project_key)
```

Copy the project id and key from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). Build one client and reuse it for every call, from any process. It is plain data with nothing to close.

The examples below use this `client` and the `Responses` alias.

## Get a response

```elixir theme={null}
params = %{instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.", input: "Do you ship to Canada?"}
{:ok, response} = Responses.create(client, params)

IO.puts(response["output_text"])
```

`params` is OpenAI's Responses body, with atom or string keys. `create/3` returns `{:ok, response}`.

`response["output_text"]` joins the text of the response's messages. `response["output"]` holds its items.

`response["request_id"]` is the response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. A stream has the same `stream.request_id`. Include it when you report a problem. Both are `nil` when the response has none.

Moss stores no response, so `input` holds the whole conversation. Pass a string, or a list of items such as `%{role: "user", content: "Hi"}` and the `"output"` items of earlier responses. See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).

## Stream a response

```elixir theme={null}
params = %{
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?",
  stream: true
}

{:ok, stream} = Responses.create(client, params)

for %{"type" => "response.output_text.delta", "delta" => delta} <- stream do
  IO.write(delta)
end
```

With `stream: true`, `create/3` returns `{:ok, stream}` once the response starts. Each event is a map with OpenAI's `"type"`, such as `response.output_text.delta`, and the fields of that type. The stream ends after one of two events:

* `response.completed`, when the response is done.
* `response.incomplete`, when `max_output_tokens` or a content filter cut the response short.

The `"response"` map of that last event holds `"output"` and `"usage"`. It has no `"output_text"` or `"request_id"`. Join the text from the `response.output_text.delta` events or from `"output"`. Read the request id from `stream.request_id`.

Read the stream once, in the process that called `create/3`.

To stop early, halt the stream, for example with `Enum.take/2`. You can also call `Moss.Inference.ResponseStream.close(stream)` from any process. Either one closes the connection, which stops the model.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event.

## Ground it in your indexes

```elixir theme={null}
params = %{instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.", input: "Do you ship to Canada?"}
{:ok, response} = Responses.create(client, params, indexes: ["faq"])
```

Moss searches the `faq` index and adds what it finds to the prompt. The [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md) creates that index.

`:indexes` goes in `opts`, the third argument, not in `params`. Code written for OpenAI keeps its body and adds `:indexes`.

Without `:indexes`, Moss does not search before the model runs. You can name at most 32.

`retrieve: false` skips the search on a call that names indexes.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

## Use a vendor model

Name a model from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same for every model. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists them all.

### On the Moss key

```elixir theme={null}
params = %{
  model: "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?"
}

{:ok, response} = Responses.create(client, params, indexes: ["faq"])
```

Without your own key, a listed vendor model runs on the Moss key and bills your credits. [Routes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#routes) shows who bills each call.

A listed model that is not served right now returns `{:error, error}` with `code` `"model_not_enabled"`. Send `moss/fastlane-1` or use your own key.

### With your own key

Pass your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key to a client as `:api_key`:

```elixir theme={null}
own_client =
  Moss.Inference.new(project_id, project_key, api_key: System.fetch_env!("OPENAI_API_KEY"))

params = %{
  model: "gpt-6-luna",
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Do you ship to Canada?"
}

{:ok, response} = Responses.create(own_client, params, indexes: ["faq"])
```

The key goes in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header, never in the body. To use a key for one call only, pass `:api_key` in the `opts` of `create/3`.

`response["model"]` is the name you sent. [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers model names and billing.

## Tool calls

Pass OpenAI function tools in `tools`, inside `params`. A function tool is flat, as in OpenAI's Responses API. Your code runs the tools. Each call the model makes comes as a `"function_call"` item of `"output"`.

Put the `"output"` items back into `input` as they are. Add one `"function_call_output"` item per call, and call again until the response has no calls:

```elixir theme={null}
defmodule Orders do
  alias Moss.Inference.Responses

  @lookup %{
    type: "function",
    name: "lookup_order",
    parameters: %{type: "object", properties: %{id: %{type: "string"}}}
  }

  def answer(client, input) do
    params = %{
      instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
      input: input,
      tools: [@lookup]
    }

    {:ok, response} = Responses.create(client, params)

    results =
      for %{"type" => "function_call"} = call <- response["output"] do
        output = lookup_order(call["arguments"])
        %{type: "function_call_output", call_id: call["call_id"], output: output}
      end

    if results == [],
      do: response["output_text"],
      else: answer(client, input ++ response["output"] ++ results)
  end

  defp lookup_order(_arguments), do: "Shipped on Oct 20."
end

IO.puts(Orders.answer(client, [%{role: "user", content: "Where is order A1?"}]))
```

`lookup_order/1` stands for your own code. It gets the arguments as a JSON string and returns the result as a string.

Each item goes back unchanged. It keeps every field the model sent, such as Gemini's `extra_content`.

[Tool calling](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) covers `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` and structured output.

## MCP servers

A `Moss.Inference.McpServer` struct in `tools` names an MCP server. Moss Inference runs its tools for the model during the response. Your code sends no `"function_call_output"` items for them.

```elixir theme={null}
crm = %Moss.Inference.McpServer{
  server_label: "crm",
  server_url: "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
  headers: %{"Authorization" => "Bearer " <> System.fetch_env!("CRM_TOKEN")}
}

params = %{
  instructions: "You are the support agent for Acme.",
  input: "Where is order A1?",
  tools: [crm],
  stream: true
}

{:ok, stream} = Responses.create(client, params)

for %{"type" => "response.output_item.done", "item" => %{"type" => "mcp_call"} = call} <- stream do
  IO.puts("#{call["server_label"]}.#{call["name"]}: #{call["output"]}")
end
```

Each call comes as an `"mcp_call"` item. It arrives in `response.output_item.added` when it starts, and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `"output"`.

Send the items back in `input` with the rest of `"output"`. The model then sees the earlier tool results.

MCP failures give a `Moss.Inference.Error` with `status`, `type`, `code` and `retry_after`. A call that fails after a tool ran has `code` `"failed_after_tool_call"`. The tool may already have changed data, so Moss Inference does not retry the call. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

[MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) covers the server fields and every MCP error.

## Errors

A failed call gives a `Moss.Inference.Error`. `new/3` raises it, and `create/3` returns it as `{:error, error}`. Once a stream has started, reading it raises the error. A `response.failed` event raises it too.

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `status` | The HTTP status of a refused request. |
| `type` | The kind of failure. |
| `message` | What went wrong. |
| `code` | The error code Moss Inference sent, such as `"rate_limit_exceeded"`. |
| `request_id` | The response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. |
| `retry_after` | Milliseconds to wait, from a `Retry-After` header. |

A field the failure lacks is `nil`.

The SDK sets these types itself, with `status` `nil`:

| `type` | Cause |
| - | - |
| `invalid_request_error` | An argument rejected before sending, such as an empty key, an index name that is empty or holds a comma, or an option like `:api_key` or `apiKey` inside `params`. |
| `connection_error` | Moss Inference unreachable, or the connection broke. |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out, such as `:timeout` or `:idle_timeout`. |
| `incomplete_stream` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. |
| `server_error` | A stream event over 1 MiB, or one that is not a JSON object. |

Every other error carries what Moss Inference sent. [Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every code. For a `429`, see [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## Options

`Moss.Inference.new(project_id, project_key, opts)`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `:api_key` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, for a vendor `model`. Sent as `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, never in the body. An empty key raises `Moss.Inference.Error`. |
| `:timeout` | none | Milliseconds for a whole call, stream included. `:infinity` turns it off. |
| `:idle_timeout` | `120_000` | Milliseconds to wait for the response to start, and for each pause in it. `:infinity` turns it off. |
| `:max_retries` | `2` | Retries before the response starts. `0` turns them off. |

`Moss.Inference.Responses.create(client, params, opts)` takes OpenAI's Responses body in `params`. The Moss options go in `opts`:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `params` | required | OpenAI's Responses body as a map, with atom or string keys. |
| `model` in `params` | `"moss"` | `moss` is an alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. Or a listed vendor model on the Moss key, or any vendor model with your `:api_key`. |
| `input` in `params` | required | A string, or a list of input item maps and earlier `"output"` items. |
| `instructions` in `params` | none | The system message, before `input`. |
| `stream` in `params` | `false` | `true` returns `{:ok, stream}`, an `Enumerable` of event maps, once the response starts. Otherwise `{:ok, response}`, one response map. |
| `tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` in `params` | none | Flat function tools and `Moss.Inference.McpServer` structs, and how the model may call them. |
| `max_output_tokens` in `params` | none | The most tokens the response may have. |
| `:indexes` | none | Index names to search, at most 32. Without it, Moss does not search before the model runs. |
| `:retrieve` | `true` | `false` skips the search even when indexes are named. |
| `:cache` | `true` | `true` can answer an identical request from the reply cache. `false` always asks the model. |
| `:api_key` | the client's | Your vendor key for this call. |
| `:timeout`, `:idle_timeout` | the client's | This call's limits. `:infinity` turns one off. |
| `:max_retries` | the client's | This call's retries. |

# C

> The C client for Moss Inference: OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes.

`MossInference` is the C client for [Moss Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/overview.md). `moss_inference_responses_create` takes an OpenAI Responses request as JSON, searches your indexes, and returns OpenAI's JSON.

## Install

```bash theme={null}
VERSION=0.31.0
TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin
curl -L -o libmoss.tar.gz \
  "https://github.com/usemoss/moss/releases/download/c-sdk-v${VERSION}/libmoss-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz"
mkdir -p libmoss && tar -xzf libmoss.tar.gz -C libmoss --strip-components=1
```

`MossInference` needs `libmoss` 0.29.0 or later. Set `TARGET` for your platform. The tarball holds the header, `include/libmoss.h`. A `libmoss.h` with these functions defines `MOSS_INFERENCE_API_VERSION` `3` or later. For the other platforms and how to link the library, see [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/c/getting-started.md#install).

## Create a client

```c theme={null}
#include "libmoss.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

char options[512];
snprintf(options, sizeof(options),
         "{\"project_id\": \"%s\", \"project_key\": \"%s\"}",
         getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_ID"), getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"));

MossInference *client = NULL;
if (moss_inference_new(options, &client) != OK) {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
    return 1;
}
```

Copy the project id and key from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). Build one client and reuse it for every call, from any thread. Free it with `moss_inference_free` once no call on it is running.

The examples below use this `client`.

## Get a response

```c theme={null}
const char *request =
    "{\"instructions\": \"You are the support agent for Acme.\","
    " \"input\": \"Do you ship to Canada?\"}";
char *response = NULL;
if (moss_inference_responses_create(client, request, NULL, NULL, NULL,
                                    &response) == OK) {
    printf("%s\n", response);
    moss_free_string(response);
} else {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
}
```

With `NULL` for the callback, `out_json` gets the response as the JSON of one OpenAI Response. Free it with `moss_free_string`.

The text is in the `output_text` parts of the `message` items of `output`.

The response's `request_id` is its `X-Moss-Request-Id`. Include it when you report a problem. It is left out when the response has none.

Moss stores no response, so `input` holds the whole conversation. Pass a string, or a list of items such as `{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}` and the `output` items of earlier responses. See [Conversations](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md#conversations).

## Stream a response

```c theme={null}
static int32_t print_event(const char *event_json, void *user_data) {
    (void)user_data;
    printf("%s\n", event_json);
    return 0; // any other value stops the stream
}

const char *request =
    "{\"instructions\": \"You are the support agent for Acme.\","
    " \"input\": \"Do you ship to Canada?\"}";
if (moss_inference_responses_create(client, request, NULL, print_event, NULL,
                                    NULL) != OK) {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
}
```

The call blocks until the response ends. It hands the callback each event as the JSON text of one OpenAI Responses event, such as `response.output_text.delta`. That event carries the new text in `delta`. The stream ends after one of two events:

* `response.completed`, when the response is done.
* `response.incomplete`, when `max_output_tokens` or a content filter cut the response short.

A streaming call can pass `out_json` too. It then gets the response of the last event.

To stop early, return a value other than `0` from the callback. The call then closes the connection, which stops the model, and returns `OK`.

[Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event.

## Ground it in your indexes

```c theme={null}
const char *request =
    "{\"instructions\": \"You are the support agent for Acme.\","
    " \"input\": \"Do you ship to Canada?\","
    " \"indexes\": [\"faq\"]}";
char *response = NULL;
if (moss_inference_responses_create(client, request, NULL, NULL, NULL,
                                    &response) == OK) {
    printf("%s\n", response);
    moss_free_string(response);
} else {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
}
```

Moss searches the `faq` index and adds what it finds to the prompt. The [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/quickstart.md) creates that index.

Without `indexes`, Moss does not search before the model runs. You can name at most 32.

`"retrieve": false` skips the search on a call that names indexes.

[Ground answers in your indexes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) covers the options and the cost.

## Use a vendor model

Name a model from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in `model`. The search of your indexes works the same for every model. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists them all.

### On the Moss key

```c theme={null}
const char *request =
    "{\"model\": \"anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5\","
    " \"instructions\": \"You are the support agent for Acme.\","
    " \"input\": \"Do you ship to Canada?\","
    " \"indexes\": [\"faq\"]}";
char *response = NULL;
if (moss_inference_responses_create(client, request, NULL, NULL, NULL,
                                    &response) == OK) {
    printf("%s\n", response);
    moss_free_string(response);
} else {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
}
```

Without your own key, a listed vendor model runs on the Moss key and bills your credits. [Routes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#routes) shows who bills each call.

A listed model that is not served right now fails with `code` `"model_not_enabled"` in `moss_last_error_detail()`. Send `moss/fastlane-1` or use your own key.

### With your own key

Pass your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key to a client as `api_key` in `options_json`:

```c theme={null}
char own_options[1024];
snprintf(own_options, sizeof(own_options),
         "{\"project_id\": \"%s\", \"project_key\": \"%s\", \"api_key\": \"%s\"}",
         getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_ID"), getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"),
         getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"));

MossInference *own_client = NULL;
if (moss_inference_new(own_options, &own_client) != OK) {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
    return 1;
}

const char *request =
    "{\"model\": \"gpt-6-luna\","
    " \"instructions\": \"You are the support agent for Acme.\","
    " \"input\": \"Do you ship to Canada?\","
    " \"indexes\": [\"faq\"]}";
char *response = NULL;
if (moss_inference_responses_create(own_client, request, NULL, NULL, NULL,
                                    &response) == OK) {
    printf("%s\n", response);
    moss_free_string(response);
} else {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
}
```

The key goes in the `X-Moss-Provider-Key` header, never in the body. To use a key for one call only, put `api_key` in `call_options_json`.

The response's `model` is the name you sent. [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md) covers model names and billing.

## Tool calls

Pass OpenAI function tools in `tools` of the request JSON. A function tool is flat, as in OpenAI's Responses API. Your code runs the tools.

```c theme={null}
const char *request =
    "{\"instructions\": \"You are the support agent for Acme.\","
    " \"input\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Where is order A1?\"}],"
    " \"tools\": [{\"type\": \"function\", \"name\": \"lookup_order\","
    " \"parameters\": {\"type\": \"object\","
    " \"properties\": {\"id\": {\"type\": \"string\"}}}}]}";
char *response = NULL;
if (moss_inference_responses_create(client, request, NULL, NULL, NULL,
                                    &response) == OK) {
    // With your JSON library, run lookup_order for each function_call item of output.
    moss_free_string(response);
} else {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
}
```

Each call the model makes comes as a `function_call` item of `output`, with its `call_id`, `name` and `arguments`.

Put the `output` items back into `input` as they are. Add one item per call, such as `{"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "...", "output": "Shipped on Oct 20."}`. Call again with the same `tools` until the response has no calls.

Each item keeps every field the model sent, such as the thought signature Gemini needs in the next turn.

[Tool calling](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) covers `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` and structured output.

## MCP servers

A `tools` entry of type `"mcp"` names an MCP server. Moss Inference runs its tools for the model within the same call, so your code sends no `function_call_output` items for them.

```c theme={null}
const char *request =
    "{\"instructions\": \"You are the support agent for Acme.\","
    " \"input\": \"Where is order A1?\","
    " \"tools\": [{\"type\": \"mcp\", \"server_label\": \"crm\","
    " \"server_url\": \"https://mcp.example.com/mcp\","
    " \"headers\": {\"Authorization\": \"Bearer your-crm-token\"}}]}";
char *response = NULL;
if (moss_inference_responses_create(client, request, NULL, print_event, NULL,
                                    &response) == OK) {
    printf("%s\n", response);
    moss_free_string(response);
} else {
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", moss_last_error());
}
```

`print_event` is the callback from [Stream a response](#stream-a-response).

Each call comes as an `mcp_call` item. It arrives in a `response.output_item.added` event when it starts, and in `response.output_item.done` when it ends. The same items are in the response's `output`.

Send the items back in `input` with the rest of `output`. The model then sees the earlier tool results.

MCP failures return a negative `MossResult`, with `status`, `type`, `code` and `retry_after_ms` in `moss_last_error_detail()`. A call that fails after a tool ran has `code` `"failed_after_tool_call"`. The tool may already have changed data, so Moss Inference does not retry the call. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.**

[MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md) covers the server fields and every MCP error.

## Errors

A failed call returns a negative `MossResult`. A streaming call returns it after the events the callback already got. A `response.failed` event fails the call too.

Right after the failed call, on the same thread, `moss_last_error()` holds the message. `moss_last_error_detail()` holds a JSON object with these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `status` | The HTTP status of a refused request. |
| `type` | The kind of failure. |
| `code` | The error code Moss Inference sent, such as `"rate_limit_exceeded"`. |
| `request_id` | The response's `X-Moss-Request-Id`. |
| `retry_after_ms` | Milliseconds to wait, from a `Retry-After` header. |

A field the failure lacks is `null`.

The SDK sets these types itself:

| `type` | Returns | Cause |
| - | - | - |
| none, the detail is `NULL` | `ERR_NULL_POINTER`, `ERR_INVALID_ARG` | An argument rejected before sending, such as an empty key, an index name that is empty or holds a comma, a `NULL` client or request, or no callback and no `out_json`. |
| `connection_error` | `ERR_CLOUD` | Moss Inference unreachable, or the connection broke. |
| `timeout` | `ERR_CLOUD` | A time limit ran out, such as `timeout_ms` or `idle_timeout_ms`. |
| `incomplete_stream` | `ERR_CLOUD` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. |
| `server_error` | `ERR_CLOUD`, `ERR_DESERIALIZATION` | A stream event over 1 MiB (`ERR_CLOUD`), or one that is not a JSON object (`ERR_DESERIALIZATION`). |

Every other error carries what Moss Inference sent. The call returns:

* `ERR_UNAUTHORIZED` for `authentication_error` and `permission_error`.
* `ERR_INVALID_ARG` for `invalid_request_error`.
* `ERR_CLOUD` for the rest.

[Errors and limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#errors) lists every code. For a `429`, see [Limits](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/errors-and-limits.md#limits).

## Options

```c theme={null}
typedef int32_t (*MossInferenceEventFn)(const char *event_json, void *user_data);
MossResult moss_inference_new(const char *options_json, MossInference **out);
void moss_inference_free(MossInference *client);
MossResult moss_inference_responses_create(
    const MossInference *client, const char *request_json, const char *call_options_json,
    MossInferenceEventFn on_event, void *user_data, char **out_json);
```

`options_json` of `moss_inference_new`:

| Key | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `project_id`, `project_key` | required | Your project id and key. |
| `api_key` | none | Your OpenAI, Anthropic or Google key, for a vendor `model`. Sent as `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, never in the body. An empty key returns `ERR_INVALID_ARG`. |
| `timeout_ms` | none | Milliseconds for a whole call, stream included. `0` turns it off. |
| `idle_timeout_ms` | `120000` | Milliseconds to wait for the response to start, and for each pause in it. `0` turns it off. |
| `max_retries` | `2` | Retries before the response starts. `0` turns them off. |

`request_json` of `moss_inference_responses_create`:

| Key | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `model` | `"moss"` | `moss` is an alias of `moss/fastlane-1`. Or a listed vendor model on the Moss key, or any vendor model with your `api_key`. |
| `input` | required | A string, or a list of messages, `function_call_output` items and earlier `output` items. |
| `instructions` | none | The system message, before `input`. |
| `tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls` | none | OpenAI's Responses tool fields. A `tools` entry of type `"mcp"` names an MCP server. |
| `indexes` | none | Index names to search, at most 32. Without it, Moss does not search before the model runs. |
| `retrieve` | `true` | `false` skips the search even when indexes are named. |
| `cache` | `true` | `true` can answer an identical request from the reply cache. `false` always asks the model. |
| Other OpenAI fields | none | `max_output_tokens`, `temperature`, `text` for structured output, `reasoning` and the rest. `stream` is always `true`. |

`call_options_json` of `moss_inference_responses_create`, which may be `NULL`:

| Key | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `api_key` | the client's | Your vendor key for this call. |
| `timeout_ms`, `idle_timeout_ms` | the client's | This call's limits. `0` turns one off. |
| `max_retries` | the client's | This call's retries. |

## Memory and the event callback

| Pointer | Owner | Release |
| - | - | - |
| `MossInference *` from `moss_inference_new` | You | `moss_inference_free`, once no call on it is running. `NULL` is a no-op. |
| `*out_json` from `moss_inference_responses_create` | You | `moss_free_string`. Set only when the call returns `OK`. `NULL` when the callback stopped the stream first. |
| `event_json` in the callback | `libmoss` | Nothing. Valid until the callback returns, so copy it to keep it. |
| `moss_last_error()`, `moss_last_error_detail()` | `libmoss` | Nothing. Valid until the next `libmoss` call on the same thread. |
| `options_json`, `request_json`, `call_options_json` | You | Your own. They only need to live until the call returns. |

* The callback runs on the thread that made the call, once per event. It never runs after the call returns.
* `libmoss` never reads or frees `user_data`.
* The next event is read only after the callback returns. A slow callback holds up the stream, and its time counts toward `timeout_ms`.

# Errors and limits

> Rate and size limits, every error status and code, and when to retry.

Every limit, error status and error code of Moss Inference, with what to do about each. Responses and Chat Completions share them.

## Limits

Limits apply per project.

| Limit | `moss/fastlane-1` | Vendor model |
| - | - | - |
| Requests per minute (sustained / burst) | 120 / 10 | 300 / 50 |
| Input tokens per minute | 600,000 | None |
| Prompt tokens per request | 262,144 | 128,000 on the Moss key, 200,000 on your key |
| Indexes per request | 32 | 32 |
| Request body | 4 MB | 4 MB |

On `moss/fastlane-1`, the 262,144 tokens are the whole context. The prompt, the retrieved facts and the reply share them.

On the Moss key, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` takes up to 64,000 prompt tokens. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md) lists the prompt limit of every model.

One request searches at most 32 indexes, named in `X-Moss-Indexes` and in a [`moss_search`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search) tool together.

MCP servers and the [`moss_search`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search) tool add limits of their own. A request with too many servers or tools returns `400`. Too many requests with these tools at once return `429` with `code` `mcp_loops_busy`. A request with these tools can run for a few minutes.

To raise a limit for your project, ask through [Support](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/start/support).

### Rate limit headers

These headers show how much of the project's limits is left.

| Header | Value |
| - | - |
| `x-ratelimit-limit-requests`, `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens` | The limit |
| `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` | What is left of it |
| `x-ratelimit-reset-requests`, `x-ratelimit-reset-tokens` | When it resets |

The `tokens` headers come on `moss/fastlane-1` only.

## Errors

Every error has OpenAI's shape: an `error` object with `message`, `type` and `code`.

```json 429 Too Many Requests theme={null}
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Rate limit reached for project 1a2b3c: too many requests per minute. Please try again in 1s.",
    "type": "requests",
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded"
  }
}
```

| Status | `type` | `code` | Cause | What to do |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | | A malformed body, more than 32 index names, or a bad `tools` entry | Fix the request. |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | `context_length_exceeded` | A prompt over the model's [limit](#limits) | Shorten the prompt. On `moss/fastlane-1`, leave room for the reply. |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | `model_not_enabled` | A listed model, on the Moss key, that is not served right now | Send `moss/fastlane-1`, or the model on your own key. |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | `missing_provider_key` | A vendor's own model name, such as `gpt-6-luna`, without your key | Send your key. See [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md). |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | `model_not_found` | A model name Moss does not serve | Pick an id from [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md). |
| `400` | `invalid_request_error` | `unsupported_parameter` | A field or message part the model does not take on the Moss key | Remove it, or use your own key. See [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#parameters-refused-on-the-moss-key). |
| `400` | `model_error` | | The model rejected the prompt | Change the prompt. |
| `400` | `mcp_error` | `mcp_server_error` | `server_url` is not a public `https` URL on port 443 | Use a public `https` URL on port 443. |
| `401` | `authentication_error` | | A missing or wrong `Authorization` token | Send `Authorization: Bearer <project_id>:<project_key>`. |
| `403` | `permission_error` | | `X-Moss-Indexes` or a `moss_search` entry names an index outside this project | Name only this project's indexes. |
| `413` | `invalid_request_error` | | A body over 4 MB | Send a smaller body. |
| `424` | `mcp_error` | `mcp_server_error` | The MCP server did not connect, refused the credentials, or failed to list its tools | Check `server_url` and `headers`. |
| `424` | | `failed_after_tool_call` | A failure after an MCP tool or `moss_search` ran. An MCP tool may have changed data | Do not replay it. See [MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md#errors). |
| `429` | `requests`, `tokens` | `rate_limit_exceeded` | Over a per-minute [limit](#limits) | Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry. |
| `429` | `usage_limit` | `usage_limit_exceeded` | Your credits ran out, so usage is paused | Add credits. See [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#credits). |
| `429` | `capacity` | `mcp_loops_busy` | Too many requests with MCP servers or `moss_search` at once | Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry. |
| Vendor `4xx` | `model_error` | `upstream_error` | The vendor refused a call on your own key, with its own status | Read the vendor's message, which follows `The model rejected the prompt`. |
| `502` | `model_error` | | The model failed, or a vendor returned `5xx` | Retry with backoff. |
| `503` | `server_error` | | Moss could not check the project | Retry with backoff. |
| `503` | `server_error` | `project_settings_unavailable` | Moss could not read the project's [system prompt](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/chat-completions.md#system-prompt), so it did not answer without it | Wait the 2 seconds of `Retry-After`, then retry. |
| `503` | `server_error` | `billing_unavailable` | Moss cannot meter a call on the Moss key right now | Wait the 5 seconds of `Retry-After`, or send `moss/fastlane-1`. |
| `503` | `capacity` | `server_overloaded` | Moss is at capacity, or the vendor rate limited the Moss key | Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry. |
| `503` | `capacity` | `vendor_unavailable` | The vendor refused or could not serve a call on the Moss key, such as on Anthropic's `529` overload | Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry. |

On your own key, a bad key returns the vendor's status: `401` from OpenAI and Anthropic, `400` from Google.

### Errors after a stream starts

A failure after a stream starts arrives as a stream event. On Responses, the stream ends with `response.failed`, whose `response.error` has `type`, `code` and `message`. On Chat Completions, a last `data:` frame carries `error` in place of `choices`, then `data: [DONE]` follows. Without `stream`, the same failure returns `502`, or `424` once an MCP call or a `moss_search` call ran. [Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md#errors-after-the-stream-starts) shows both stream forms.

## Retry rules

The Moss SDKs retry on their own, 2 times by default. They retry a connection failure, or a `408`, `409`, `429` or `5xx`, before the response starts. Each retry waits for `Retry-After` when it is 60 seconds or less, and backs off otherwise. In the Moss SDKs, `x-should-retry: false` stops a retry, and `x-should-retry: true` forces one. They never retry a stream that has started. The OpenAI SDKs retry on their own as well. If you call the endpoint directly, follow the same rules.

Fix a `400`, `401`, `403` or `413` before you send the request again.

**Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.** An MCP tool or `moss_search` already ran, and an MCP tool may have changed data. The `424` carries `x-should-retry: false`, so the SDKs do not retry it either.

Every response carries `X-Moss-Request-Id`, a refused one included. Include it when you report a problem. Each SDK exposes it as the request id of the response and of the error.

## SDK errors

Each Moss SDK has one error for a failed call.

| SDK | Error |
| - | - |
| [Python](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/python.md#errors) | `moss.inference.InferenceError` |
| [JavaScript](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/javascript.md#errors) | `InferenceError` |
| [Browser](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/browser.md#errors) | `InferenceError` |
| [Swift](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/swift.md#errors) | `InferenceError` |
| [Android](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/android.md#errors) | `InferenceError` |
| [Elixir](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/elixir.md#errors) | `Moss.Inference.Error` |
| [C](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/c.md#errors) | A negative `MossResult`, with the fields in `moss_last_error_detail()` |

The error holds the `status`, `type` and `code` from the [Errors](#errors) table. It also holds the request id and the `Retry-After` wait. JavaScript and the browser name the code `errorCode`.

The SDK sets five types itself, with no `status`:

| `type` | Cause |
| - | - |
| `invalid_request_error` | An argument the SDK rejects before sending, such as an empty key or an index name with a comma |
| `connection_error` | Moss Inference could not be reached, or the connection broke |
| `timeout` | A time limit ran out, such as the call's timeout or idle timeout |
| `incomplete_stream` | The stream ended before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete` |
| `server_error` | The stream sent an event over 1 MiB, or one that is not a JSON object |

Android throws `IllegalArgumentException` in place of `invalid_request_error`. In C, a rejected argument returns `ERR_NULL_POINTER` or `ERR_INVALID_ARG`, with a `NULL` detail.

<!-- Page: What is Moss? · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/start/what-is-moss.md · local: pages/start/what-is-moss.md -->

# What is Moss?

> Real-time semantic search that runs where your agent lives

Moss is the runtime for real-time semantic search in conversational apps. It delivers sub-10 ms lookups and instant index updates without extra infrastructure. It runs in the browser, on-device, or in the cloud - wherever your agent lives - so search feels native. Connect your data once; Moss packages, distributes, and keeps indexes fresh. Because the index lives next to your agent, retrieval is a function you call, not a service you query.

* Sub-10 ms lookups with instant updates
* Real-time sessions (Python, JavaScript, Swift, Elixir, C): index and query locally during a conversation, then sync to the cloud
* No infra to run; local-first with optional sync
* Browser, device, or cloud - same API

## Use cases

* Sub-10 ms answers for docs, FAQ, and in-app search
* Grounding agents with your data without centralizing user info
* Local or hybrid embeddings with minimal infrastructure

## Capabilities

> [card] [Real-Time Local Indexing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/real-time-local-indexing.md)
>
> Index and query on-device in milliseconds, with no network round trip.

> [card] [Live-Call Context](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/live-call-context.md)
>
> Short-term session context plus long-term knowledge, during a call.

> [card] [Data Hydration & Sync](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/data-hydration-sync.md)
>
> Hydrate from the cloud and stay fresh with zero-downtime hot-swaps.

> [card] [Cross-Agent Handoff](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/cross-agent-handoff.md)
>
> Carry full context across agents, channels, and devices.

## SDKs

One model across every surface: JavaScript (Node), Python, Swift (iOS), Android, Elixir, C, and an in-browser/WASM build.

## Using Moss Portal

* Sign up at Moss, confirm email, and sign in
* From the portal, copy your **Project ID**, then open **API Keys** and create a key
* Join our Discord to get onboarded: [Moss Discord](https://discord.gg/eMXExuafBR)

![Moss Portal walkthrough](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3db9d2d-0df5-4cec-99fd-7d49d0a30844)

## Samples

* View samples repo: [moss on GitHub](https://github.com/usemoss/moss)
* JavaScript: `javascript/comprehensive_sample.ts`, `javascript/load_and_query_sample.ts`
* Python: `python/comprehensive_sample.py`, `python/load_and_query_sample.py`
* Adapt by swapping the FAQ data with your own, or plug Moss calls into your app

## How it works (at a glance)

* **Index:** Convert your data into an efficient local index
* **Embeddings:** Generate vectors on-device (`moss-minilm`, `moss-mediumlm`) or supply your own
* **Sessions:** Index and query locally in real time during a live interaction, then sync to the cloud
* **Retrieval:** Load the index, then query in-memory with semantic or hybrid search
* **Storage:** Persist indexes locally and optionally sync to cloud

# SDK Quickstart

> Install, authenticate, create an index, and query it (JS/Python tabs)

Follow one path to a visible result. Choose your language tab.

## Prerequisites:

* Node.js 20.4+ or Python 3.10+
* Valid Moss project credentials (`MOSS_PROJECT_ID`, `MOSS_PROJECT_KEY`)
* JS: `@moss-js/moss`; Python: `moss`

**1. Install**

```bash JavaScript theme={null}
npm install @moss-js/moss
```

```bash Python theme={null}
pip install moss
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Versions below 1.9.0 will stop loading models when the legacy download path is retired. Upgrade to 1.9.0+ before then.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Moss for Node moved from `@moss-dev/moss` to `@moss-js/moss` with 1.8.0. `@moss-dev/moss` is a frozen 1.7.1 package. Versions below 1.9.0 will stop loading models when the legacy download path is retired. Upgrade to `@moss-js/moss` 1.9.0+ before then. The date will be announced in the changelog. `@moss-dev/moss-web` is the browser SDK and is not this package.

**2. Configure credentials**

From the Moss portal, copy your Project ID and create a key on the **API Keys** page. Set them as env vars:

```bash theme={null}
export MOSS_PROJECT_ID="your_project_id"
export MOSS_PROJECT_KEY="your_project_key"
```

**3. Create and query an index**

Save the JavaScript as `quickstart.mts` and run `npx tsx quickstart.mts` (the `.mts` extension lets it use top-level `await`), or save the Python as `quickstart.py` and run `python quickstart.py`:

```ts JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossClient, DocumentInfo } from '@moss-js/moss'
const client = new MossClient(process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!, process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!)
const documents: DocumentInfo[] = [
  { id: 'doc1', text: 'How do I track my order? You can track your order by logging into your account.', metadata: { category: 'shipping' } },
  { id: 'doc2', text: 'What is your return policy? We offer a 30-day return policy for most items.', metadata: { category: 'returns' } },
  { id: 'doc3', text: 'How can I change my shipping address? Contact our customer service team.', metadata: { category: 'support' } },
]
const indexName = 'faqs'
await client.createIndex(indexName, documents, { modelId: 'moss-minilm' }) // default; use 'moss-mediumlm' for higher accuracy
await client.loadIndex(indexName)
const results = await client.query(indexName, 'How do I return a damaged product?', { topK: 3 })
console.log(results.docs[0])
```

```python Python theme={null}
import os
import asyncio
from moss import MossClient, DocumentInfo, QueryOptions
client = MossClient(os.getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_ID"), os.getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"))
index_name = "faqs"
documents = [
    DocumentInfo(id="doc1", text="How do I track my order? You can track your order by logging into your account.", metadata={"category": "shipping"}),
    DocumentInfo(id="doc2", text="What is your return policy? We offer a 30-day return policy for most items.", metadata={"category": "returns"}),
    DocumentInfo(id="doc3", text="How can I change my shipping address? Contact our customer service team.", metadata={"category": "support"}),
]
async def main():
    await client.create_index(index_name, documents, "moss-minilm")  # default; use "moss-mediumlm" for higher accuracy
    await client.load_index(index_name)
    results = await client.query(index_name, "How do I return a damaged product?", QueryOptions(top_k=3, alpha=0.6))
    print(f"  ID: {results.docs[0].id}")
    print(f"  Text: {results.docs[0].text}")
    print(f"  Score: {results.docs[0].score}")
asyncio.run(main())
```

## Example output

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "doc2",
  "score": 0.82,
  "text": "What is your return policy? We offer a 30-day return policy for most items."
}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> `score` is each result's relevance to the query, from 0 to 1 (the value here is illustrative). See
> [Score semantics](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/retrieval.md#score-semantics) for what it means and the SDK version it needs.

> [!TIP]
>
> Need keyword-heavy results? Set `alpha` to `0.0` for pure keyword, `1.0` for pure semantic, or a blend in between (see [Hybrid Search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/hybrid-search.md) for details).

## Next steps

You just created a cloud index and queried it. Moss does much more:

>

> [card] [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md)
>
> Local-first, real-time indexing during a live interaction.

> [card] [Hybrid search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/hybrid-search.md)
>
> Blend semantic and keyword scoring with `alpha`.

> [card] [Metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/metadata-filtering.md)
>
> Narrow results with `$eq`, `$in`, `$near`, and more.

> [card] [Custom embeddings](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/custom-embeddings.md)
>
> Bring your own vectors instead of the built-in model.

> [card] [Multi-index search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/multi-index-search.md)
>
> Query several indexes at once for a global top-K.

> [card] [Data hydration & sync](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/data-hydration-sync.md)
>
> Hydrate on-device indexes and keep them fresh.

> [card] [SDK Overview](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/sdk.md)
>

<!-- Page: Core Concepts · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/start/core-concepts.md · local: pages/start/core-concepts.md -->

# Core Concepts

> Indexes, embeddings, retrieval, sessions, sync, and the rest of the Moss model.

This page defines the concepts you'll use across Moss. Most link to a How-it-works guide
where they go deeper.

## Index

A structure that powers fast, local search. You add documents and Moss builds an efficient
index for sub-10 ms queries. A project can hold many indexes.

### Document schema

* `id` (string), `text` (string), `metadata` (optional string map)
* Upserts replace matching `id`s; keep ids stable for updates

## Embeddings

Semantic vector representations of text. Moss embeds **on-device** with a built-in model, or
you can [bring your own vectors](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/custom-embeddings.md) using a `custom` model
(you then supply an `embedding` for every document and every query).

### Models

* `moss-minilm` (default): fast, lightweight, good for edge/offline
* `moss-mediumlm`: higher accuracy with reasonable performance
* `moss-litelm`: the on-device default on iOS
* `custom`: bring your own embedding vectors

### Chunking

* Uploaded files and web sources are chunked automatically; for your own documents, see [Chunking tips](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/indexing-data.md#chunking-tips)
* Smaller chunks improve recall; overlap preserves context continuity

## Loading

Querying always runs against an index held in memory. Load the index (or open a
[session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md)) before you query - there is no cloud-query-without-loading
path. You can also [load several indexes at once](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/multi-index-search.md)
for a single query, then unload them when done.

## Retrieval

How results are fetched, all over one query call:

* **Vector** (semantic) - matches on meaning
* **Keyword** (BM25) - matches on exact terms
* **[Hybrid](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/hybrid-search.md)** - blends both, tuned with `alpha` (1.0 semantic, 0.0 keyword, default 0.8)

### Retrieval knobs

* Result count: how many results to return
* `alpha`: the semantic/keyword blend
* `filter`: [metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/metadata-filtering.md) with `$eq`, `$in`, `$near`, `$and`/`$or`, and more

Each result carries a relevance `score` from 0 to 1, and it is not the sort key: results stay in hybrid
order. See [Score semantics](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/retrieval.md#score-semantics) for how it behaves and the SDK
version it needs.

## Multi-index search

Query several loaded indexes at once and get a single global top-K, each result tagged by its
source index. Useful when the answer is spread across separate corpora you keep as distinct
indexes. See [Multi-index search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/multi-index-search.md).

## Sessions

A local-first index you read and write in real time, with no cloud round trip on any
operation. The workflow is create-resume-query-push: open a session by name, index documents
locally as they arrive, query in-memory, and optionally push the result to the cloud. Ideal
for indexing during a live interaction. See [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md).

## Storage, sync, and freshness

Indexes persist locally on the device; the cloud copy is the source of truth. Loading pulls a
local snapshot, and [hydration and auto-refresh](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/data-hydration-sync.md) keep a loaded
index current by polling for newer versions and hot-swapping with no query downtime. Pushing
uploads local changes back to the cloud.

## Cross-agent handoff

Because a session is just a named cloud index, one agent can push a conversation and another
can resume it by opening a session with the same name - across agents, channels, and devices.
See [Cross-agent handoff](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/cross-agent-handoff.md).

## Cross-platform compatibility

Indexes are portable across SDKs: an index built or pushed from one language (Python,
JavaScript, Swift, Elixir, C) can be loaded and queried from another.

## Authentication

SDKs authenticate with project credentials (`MOSS_PROJECT_ID`, `MOSS_PROJECT_KEY`). For
browsers and other untrusted clients, mint short-lived tokens with a
[custom authenticator](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/custom-authenticator.md) instead of shipping the
project key. See [Authentication](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/authentication.md).

## Jobs

Cloud index builds (create, add, push) run as async jobs. The mutation returns a job id;
poll the job-status method to track progress through to completion.

## Performance expectations

* Sub-10 ms local queries (hardware-dependent)
* Sync is optional; compute stays on-device

# Vibecoding with Moss

> Starter prompts, LLM-friendly docs, and MCP setup for building Moss-powered apps with AI coding tools.

Every page in these docs has a **Copy page** button paste any page directly into Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or your preferred AI coding tool to give it full context.

We publish an [`llms.txt`](https://llmstxt.org) file a compact, machine-readable index of all Moss documentation that AI tools can fetch at the start of a session.

> [card] [llms.txt](https://docs.moss.dev/llms.txt)
>
> Full index of Moss documentation in a format AI tools can parse

## MCP Server

The Moss MCP server lets any MCP compatible client Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code call Moss tools directly. No SDK code needed: your AI assistant can create indexes, add documents, and run semantic search queries from within the conversation.

```json theme={null}
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "moss": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@moss-tools/mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "MOSS_PROJECT_ID": "your-project-id",
        "MOSS_PROJECT_KEY": "your-project-key"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Add this to your client's config file - `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` for Claude Desktop, or `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor. Get your Project ID and create a key on the API Keys page in the [Moss Portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev).

> [card] [MCP Server setup](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrations/mcp-server.md)
>
> Full setup guide with client-specific instructions and available tools

## Starter Prompt for Vibecoding

Paste this into your AI coding tool before starting a Moss project.

```
You are helping me build an application that uses Moss for real-time semantic search.

## About Moss
Moss is a semantic search runtime for conversational AI with sub-10ms local queries, instant index
updates, same SDK for browser, on-device, and cloud. No separate search infrastructure needed.

## Documentation
- Quickstart:    https://docs.moss.dev/docs/start/quickstart
- Core concepts: https://docs.moss.dev/docs/start/core-concepts
- SDK reference: https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/sdk
- API reference: https://docs.moss.dev/api-reference/v1
- MCP server:    https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrations/mcp-server
- Full doc index (LLM-friendly): https://docs.moss.dev/llms.txt

## Setup
- JS package: @moss-js/moss 1.9.0+  |  Python package: moss 1.9.0+
- Credentials: MOSS_PROJECT_ID from the project page and MOSS_PROJECT_KEY from the API Keys page at https://portal.usemoss.dev

## Key concepts
- createIndex / loadIndex / query is the core flow - see the quickstart for full examples
- Hybrid search: pass alpha (0.0 = keyword, 1.0 = semantic, default 0.8) to query()
- Mutations (createIndex, addDocs, deleteDocs) are async jobs; SDK polls until completion
- Embedding models: moss-minilm (fast, default), moss-mediumlm (higher accuracy), custom (bring your own vectors)
- Metadata filtering on local indexes: $eq, $ne, $in, $gt, $lt, $and, $or operators

## Common errors
- Unauthorized: missing or wrong MOSS_PROJECT_ID / MOSS_PROJECT_KEY
- Index not found: call createIndex() before loading or querying
- Index not loaded: call loadIndex() before query() - query() throws if the index isn't loaded locally
- Missing embeddings runtime: use moss-minilm or moss-mediumlm unless supplying custom vectors
```

# Real-Time Local Indexing

> Index and query in-process with a local session - no per-operation network call.

A **session** is an in-process index. You open it with `client.session(name)`, then add,
query, and delete documents locally; embedding and search run on-device, with no network
call per operation. When you are done, `push_index()` persists the index to the cloud.

A session is represented by a [`SessionIndex`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/classes/SessionIndex).

## Operations

![Session operations run on device, with add\_docs and query in process before optional push\_index to cloud](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/real-time-local-indexing-light.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=b8d71193d5c75cdb622b08faa0d70f84)

![Session operations run on device, with add\_docs and query in process before optional push\_index to cloud](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/real-time-local-indexing-dark.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=e25c731910af3f6cbdb56237653b98e0)

* **`add_docs(docs, options?)`** - embeds and indexes documents locally; returns `(added, updated)`.
* **`query(text, options?)`** - semantic or hybrid search over the in-memory index; returns a `SearchResult`.
* **`get_docs(options?)` / `delete_docs(ids)`** - read and remove documents locally.
* **`push_index()`** - uploads the session to the cloud, creating or replacing the cloud index of the same name. For a built-in model the service re-embeds the text with that model; a custom-model session keeps its own embeddings.

In Python and Elixir, and by default in Swift and C, `session(name)` is **create-or-resume**:
if a cloud index with that name already exists it is loaded into the session (no
re-embedding); otherwise the session starts empty. A JavaScript session always starts empty;
call `session.loadIndex(name)` to resume the cloud index. The rest of the API is the same
either way.

## Example

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, QueryOptions

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    # Open a session: new local index, or load an existing cloud index by name.
    session = await client.session(index_name="notes")

    # Add documents (embedded and indexed locally).
    added, updated = await session.add_docs([
        DocumentInfo(id="1", text="Ship the on-device SDK by Friday."),
        DocumentInfo(id="2", text="Follow up with the LiveKit team about latency."),
    ])
    print(f"{added} added, {updated} updated, {session.doc_count} total")

    # Query the in-memory index.
    results = await session.query("what's due this week", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
    for doc in results.docs:
        print(f"{doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Performance characteristics

* Operations run in-process: no network round trip, TLS, or serialization on the query path.
* Query text is embedded by a local model; with `model_id="custom"` you supply the query vector via `QueryOptions.embedding` instead.
* Local queries typically complete in single-digit milliseconds, which suits short, frequent queries against a per-session or per-user working set.

## Session vs. loaded cloud index

| Use a **session** when | Use a **loaded cloud index** when |
| - | - |
| You are indexing data created at runtime (a live call, a chat, a working set) | You are querying a large, stable corpus built ahead of time |
| You need writes and reads against the same in-memory index | Reads dominate and the data changes infrequently |
| The data is per-conversation or per-user and short-lived | The index is shared across many sessions |

The two compose: load a persistent index and open a session in the same client. See
[Live-call context](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/live-call-context.md).

>
> The full session lifecycle and API.

> [card] [SessionIndex reference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/classes/SessionIndex.md)
>

<!-- Page: Live-Call Context · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/live-call-context.md · local: pages/build/live-call-context.md -->

# Live-Call Context

> Query a persistent cloud index and a live session together during a conversation.

During a live interaction you typically query two indexes:

* **Long-term context** - a persistent cloud index of durable knowledge and account facts
  (FAQs, policies, profile). You load it once at the start of the call with `load_index()`.
* **Short-term context** - a [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md) holding the current
  conversation, which you build up with `add_docs()` as turns arrive.

Both run locally once loaded, so each turn can query the knowledge index and the session
without a network round trip, then pass the combined results to the model.

## A single agent turn

![A caller turn reaches an agent, which updates a short-term session, queries recent context and long-term cloud knowledge, then responds](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/live-call-context-light.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=d89ade0d0c3fc7d372706c25049088c7)

![A caller turn reaches an agent, which updates a short-term session, queries recent context and long-term cloud knowledge, then responds](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/live-call-context-dark.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=aab230eec0ffcd50cc3313256ab1d65d)

## How it works

**1. Load the long-term index**

`load_index("support-faqs")` loads the persistent knowledge index into memory for querying.

**2. Open a session for the call**

`client.session(call_id)` returns a local [`SessionIndex`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/classes/SessionIndex).
If an index with that name already exists in the cloud it is loaded; otherwise the session starts empty.

**3. Index transcript turns**

Call `add_docs` as turns arrive; documents are embedded and indexed locally.

**4. Query both indexes per turn**

Query the loaded knowledge index and the session, and pass both result sets to the model.

**5. Persist the session**

`session.push_index()` writes the session to the cloud so a later interaction can resume it.

## Example

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, QueryOptions

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    # Long-term context: load a persistent knowledge index.
    await client.load_index("support-faqs")

    # Short-term context: open a session for this call.
    call_id = f"call-{datetime.now():%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}"
    session = await client.session(index_name=call_id)

    # Index transcript turns into the session.
    await session.add_docs([
        DocumentInfo(id="turn-1", text="Customer was billed twice for the same renewal."),
        DocumentInfo(id="turn-2", text="Customer requested a refund for the duplicate $49.99 charge."),
    ])

    # Query both indexes and combine the results for the model.
    knowledge = await client.query("support-faqs", "duplicate charge refund policy", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
    recent = await session.query("refund request", QueryOptions(top_k=3))

    for doc in recent.docs:
        print(f"[session] {doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")
    for doc in knowledge.docs:
        print(f"[faqs]    {doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")

    # Persist the session at call end.
    result = await session.push_index()
    print(f"Pushed {result.doc_count} docs to cloud index {result.index_name!r}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Two kinds of context

| | Short-term context | Long-term context |
| - | - | - |
| **What** | The current conversation: working notes, live transcript | Durable knowledge and account facts: FAQs, policies, profile, history |
| **Where** | A local [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md), built turn by turn | A persistent cloud index, loaded once |
| **Lifetime** | The current interaction (optionally persisted at the end) | Across interactions |

## Data hydration and sync

At call start the long-term index and the session are loaded from the cloud (no
re-embedding); during the call the long-term index can stay current with `auto_refresh`; and
`session.push_index()` writes the session back. See
[Data hydration & sync](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/data-hydration-sync.md) for the load/refresh model and
refresh-interval tuning.

>

> [card] [Real-time local indexing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/real-time-local-indexing.md)
>

# Data Hydration & Sync

> Hydrate on-device indexes from the cloud and keep them fresh with zero-downtime hot-swaps.

Moss keeps an on-device index in sync with the cloud in two directions: **hydration**
(loading existing data into memory when you open an index or session) and **refresh**
(picking up cloud updates without reloading the service).

![A cloud index hydrates a loaded index or session on device, auto-refreshes it, and receives push\_index updates](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/data-hydration-sync-light.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=b95d0114e919a8efa91ab34c9b913427)

![A cloud index hydrates a loaded index or session on device, auto-refreshes it, and receives push\_index updates](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/data-hydration-sync-dark.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=c21699cc3fce026e80d35a139fd20e6f)

## Hydration: cloud to device

When you open a [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md) or load an index, Moss downloads the
index binary and deserializes it into memory, so the agent starts warm instead of empty. No
re-embedding happens; the prebuilt vectors are loaded directly.

```python theme={null}
from moss import MossClient

client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

# Hydrate a loaded index for querying...
await client.load_index("support-faqs")

# ...or hydrate a session by name (auto-loads the cloud index if it exists).
session = await client.session(index_name="call-123")
```

## Two layers of freshness

Once an index is live, freshness has two independent handles - one for getting changes into
the index, and one for propagating those changes to running agents.

### Layer 1: mutations

`add_docs` and `delete_docs` are the write API. They are asynchronous: you submit the
change, and Moss rebuilds the index server-side without touching your live service. A
mutation moves through statuses (`pending_upload`, `uploading`, `building`, `completed`);
while building, it reports finer-grained phases such as `generating_embeddings` and
`building_index`. Once `completed`, the new version is available in the cloud.

```python theme={null}
from moss import DocumentInfo, MutationOptions

await client.add_docs(
    "product-catalog",
    [DocumentInfo(id="item-9182", text="Wireless headphones, midnight blue, 40-hour battery.",
                  metadata={"category": "audio", "in_stock": "true"})],
    MutationOptions(upsert=True),
)
```

### Layer 2: runtime hot-swap

Load an index with `auto_refresh` and Moss keeps the in-memory copy current automatically:

```python theme={null}
await client.load_index("product-catalog", auto_refresh=True, polling_interval_in_seconds=120)
```

Periodically, Moss checks the cloud for a newer version. If one exists, it downloads in the
background while the current version keeps serving queries; when the download finishes, the
index is hot-swapped atomically. In-flight queries finish against the old version, new
queries immediately see the updated one. No restart, no dropped requests, no coordination.

The refresh path is:

1. Content changes land through `add_docs` or `delete_docs`.
2. Moss builds a new cloud version server-side.
3. `auto_refresh` detects the new version, downloads it in the background, and atomically hot-swaps the loaded index.
4. In-flight queries finish on the old version; new queries use the update.

## Tuning the refresh interval

`polling_interval_in_seconds` controls how often Moss checks for a new version - not how
fast a build completes. Match it to how quickly your data changes:

| Data change frequency | Suggested interval | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| Near-real-time (live inventory, pricing) | 30-60 s | Frequent polls; size your build time accordingly |
| Regular updates (daily policy changes) | 300-600 s | The default of 600 s fits here |
| Infrequent (quarterly docs, stable FAQs) | 1800 s+ | Low overhead; practically always fresh |

To force an immediate update after a known critical change, reload the index explicitly.
This is a blocking call that downloads and installs the latest version:

```python theme={null}
# Force an immediate refresh after a known critical update.
await client.load_index("compliance-rules")
```

## Independent per-index refresh

Each index manages its own refresh lifecycle on its own timer, so you can tune staleness
tolerance per knowledge domain. A slow rebuild on one index never blocks queries or
refreshes on another.

```python theme={null}
await client.load_index("live-inventory",  auto_refresh=True, polling_interval_in_seconds=30)
await client.load_index("support-policies", auto_refresh=True, polling_interval_in_seconds=600)
await client.load_index("legal-archive",    auto_refresh=True, polling_interval_in_seconds=3600)
```

## Persist: device to cloud

A [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md) accumulates context locally during an interaction.
`push_index()` syncs it back to the cloud - at the end, or at checkpoints - so it survives
the session and any agent can resume it (see [Cross-agent context & omni-channel handoff](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/cross-agent-handoff.md)).

```python theme={null}
await session.push_index()
```

## Convergence

With `auto_refresh` enabled, a loaded index converges to the latest version within at most
one polling interval after the build completes. The hot-swap is atomic: in-flight queries
complete against the previous version, and subsequent queries use the new one.

## Related

> [card] [Live-call context](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/live-call-context.md)
>
> Short-term + long-term context during a call.

> [card] [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md)
>
> The session lifecycle in depth.

<!-- Page: Cross-Agent Context & Omni-Channel Handoff · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/cross-agent-handoff.md · local: pages/build/cross-agent-handoff.md -->

# Cross-Agent Context & Omni-Channel Handoff

> Hand a conversation off across agents, channels, and devices with full context intact.

A session is identified by its **index name**. Any process that calls `client.session(name)`
loads the most recent version of that index pushed to the cloud. Multiple agents, channels,
or services can share one evolving index by using the same name: one process calls
`push_index()` to write, another calls `session(name)` to read the result.

## How it works

![Agent A pushes conversation context to a cloud index, then Agent B loads the latest version and continues the session](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/cross-agent-handoff-light.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=fd935baea3accdb912d277fe331f7a6d)

![Agent A pushes conversation context to a cloud index, then Agent B loads the latest version and continues the session](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/cross-agent-handoff-dark.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=20cacdaaad3202afe334107594b1fbce)

* **`session(name)`** loads the cloud index with that name into a local session (no re-embedding).
* **`push_index()`** writes the session back to the cloud, creating or replacing that index.

## Example

**Agent A** accumulates context, then pushes:

```python theme={null}
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient

client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

session = await client.session(index_name="conv-123")
await session.add_docs([
    DocumentInfo(id="turn-1", text="Customer reported a duplicate $49.99 charge."),
    DocumentInfo(id="turn-2", text="Agent confirmed a refund in 3-5 business days."),
])
await session.push_index()
```

**Agent B** (another process or device) opens the same name and resumes:

```python theme={null}
session = await client.session(index_name="conv-123")
print(f"{session.doc_count} documents loaded")

results = await session.query("status of the refund", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
for doc in results.docs:
    print(f"{doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")

await session.add_docs([
    DocumentInfo(id="turn-3", text="Customer confirmed the refund posted to their statement."),
])
await session.push_index()
```

## Semantics

* `push_index()` creates or replaces the cloud index of that name. Readers see the most recent completed push.
* `session(name)` loads the stored index directly; documents keep their pushed embeddings, with no re-embedding.
* All participants must use the same embedding model. Passing a `model_id` that differs from the stored index raises an error.

## Use cases

* **Omni-channel** - voice, chat, and email handlers share one index keyed by conversation or customer ID.
* **Agent escalation** - a frontline agent pushes; a specialist or human agent opens the same index with the full history.
* **Multi-device** - a session continues when the user moves from one device to another.
* **Multi-agent pipelines** - specialized agents (router, retrieval, reasoning, review) pass state through one named index; each read and write is a local in-memory operation rather than a network call.

## Related

> [card] [Sessions guide](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md)
>
> Create, resume, and persist sessions.

> [card] [Data hydration & sync](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/data-hydration-sync.md)
>
> Loading and refreshing indexes.

<!-- Page: Sub-10ms Knowledge Retrieval · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/offline-first-search.md · local: pages/build/offline-first-search.md -->

# Sub-10ms Knowledge Retrieval

> Load an index into memory and run semantic queries in-process.

Moss loads an index into memory and runs embedding and search in-process, so a query is a
local call with no network round trip per operation. The pattern is the same in every SDK:
load the index once, then query it.

```ts theme={null}
await client.loadIndex(indexName)
const results = await client.query(indexName, 'How do I return a damaged product?', { topK: 3 })
```

Queries run against the in-memory index and embed the query text with a local model.

## The query pipeline

![Query text is embedded locally, retrieved from an in-process loaded index, optionally reranked, and returned as results](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/offline-first-search-light.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=30c2869bae1001203721436fc245f3dc)

![Query text is embedded locally, retrieved from an in-process loaded index, optionally reranked, and returned as results](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/offline-first-search-dark.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=71b4a8ef2747d363022821e8dc8c2e1e)

* Load the index once, then query it in-process.
* Optional background sync to the cloud.
* Query pipeline: text -> embed -> retrieve -> rerank (optional).

## Prerequisites

* Node.js 18+ or Python 3.10+
* Moss credentials: `MOSS_PROJECT_ID`, `MOSS_PROJECT_KEY`
* An index to query (create `faqs` via the [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/start/quickstart.md) if you don't have one yet)

## Steps

**1. Export credentials (and index if different)**

```bash theme={null}
export MOSS_PROJECT_ID=your_project_id
export MOSS_PROJECT_KEY=your_project_key
export MOSS_INDEX_NAME=faqs   # or your index
```

**2. Ensure the index exists**

Ensure the index exists (see [Quickstart](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/start/quickstart.md) to create `faqs`).

**3. Run one of the snippets below**

Run one of the snippets below.

## Run the sample (JavaScript or Python)

```ts JavaScript theme={null}
import { MossClient } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossClient(
  process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_ID!,
  process.env.MOSS_PROJECT_KEY!
)

const indexName = process.env.MOSS_INDEX_NAME || 'faqs' // ensure this exists (see Quickstart)

async function main() {
  await client.loadIndex(indexName)
  const results = await client.query(indexName, 'How do I return a damaged product?', { topK: 3 })

  console.log(`Found ${results.docs.length} docs in ${results.timeTakenInMs}ms`)
  results.docs.forEach((doc, i) => {
    console.log(`${i + 1}. [${doc.id}] ${doc.text} (score: ${doc.score.toFixed(3)})`)
  })
}

main().catch(console.error)
```

```python Python theme={null}
import os
import asyncio
from moss import MossClient, QueryOptions

project_id = os.getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_ID")
project_key = os.getenv("MOSS_PROJECT_KEY")
index_name = os.getenv("MOSS_INDEX_NAME", "faqs")  # ensure this exists (see Quickstart)

async def main():
    client = MossClient(project_id, project_key)
    await client.load_index(index_name)
    results = await client.query(index_name, "How do I return a damaged product?", QueryOptions(top_k=3))

    print(f"Found {len(results.docs)} docs")
    for i, doc in enumerate(results.docs, 1):
        print(f"{i}. [{doc.id}] {doc.text} (score: {doc.score:.3f})")

asyncio.run(main())
```

The sample loads your index into memory and returns the top matches. An index must be loaded
with `loadIndex` / `load_index` (or opened as a session) before you can query it.

<!-- Page: Voice Agent (LiveKit) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/voice-agent-livekit.md · local: pages/build/voice-agent-livekit.md -->

# Voice Agent (LiveKit)

> Ground a LiveKit voice agent in your Moss index for real-time retrieval.

LiveKit provides the real-time audio pipeline (speech-to-text, LLM, text-to-speech); Moss
supplies retrieval. The agent loads a Moss index (and optionally opens a session for the live
conversation), then queries it in-process to ground its answers - each lookup is a local call,
not a network request.

## Pipeline

![Voice agent pipeline from mic to speech-to-text, Moss retrieval, LLM, and speaker](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/voice-agent-livekit-light.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=6b53d2e180b30870c6a709180c1d7f83)

![Voice agent pipeline from mic to speech-to-text, Moss retrieval, LLM, and speaker](https://mintcdn.com/moss-afcfb0b6/qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK/images/diagrams/voice-agent-livekit-dark.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=qKHE-zU1VqxhLNDK\&q=85\&s=8858b7b6e293775c3d94081e05a91a39)

## Two ways to build it

> [card] [LiveKit integration (DIY)](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrations/livekit.md)
>
> Add Moss to your own LiveKit agent: load a knowledge index, open a per-call session, and
> expose search as function tools. Full, copy-pasteable recipe.

> [card] [Managed Voice Agents](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/voice-agents/voice-agents.md)
>
> Let Moss host the agent: the Agent SDK, backend token minting, and the deploy CLI.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Prefer to start from a working app? Clone the
> [LiveKit voice agent sample](https://github.com/usemoss/moss/tree/main/apps/livekit-moss-vercel/livekit-voice-agent/livekit-moss-agent)
> and add your own keys.

## How retrieval fits

* Load a Moss index into memory at start; retrieval then runs in-process (single-digit ms).
* For live conversation memory, open a [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/sessions.md) and index transcript
  turns as they arrive - see [Live-call context](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/live-call-context.md).
* Expose retrieval to the LLM as a function tool so it searches only when it needs to. This keeps the
  chat context stable at the turn boundary, so retrieval composes with LiveKit preemptive generation -
  see [Retrieval and preemptive generation](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrations/livekit.md#retrieval-and-preemptive-generation).

## Related

> [card] [Live-call context](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/live-call-context.md)
>
> Short-term session context plus long-term knowledge during a call.

> [card] [Sub-10ms knowledge retrieval](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/build/offline-first-search.md)
>
> The load-then-query retrieval pipeline.
