<!-- Page: Errors & Troubleshooting · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/errors.md · local: pages/reference/errors.md -->

# Errors & Troubleshooting

> Reference for common Moss SDK errors and how to fix them

## Error codes

Every failure the native core reports carries a stable code. Branch on the code, not on the
message: a core failure's message is fixed text for each kind of failure, such as
`Index not found.`, with no URLs, file paths or index names. An argument the SDK rejects
itself keeps a message that describes it. *(Python moss 1.15.0+, @moss-js/moss 1.16.0+,
@moss-dev/moss-web 1.4.0+, Elixir moss 1.5.0+, Swift SDK 0.8.0+)*

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | The caller passed a value the operation cannot accept. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | The index or other named resource does not exist or is not loaded. |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | The credentials, token or plan do not permit the operation. |
| `NETWORK` | The Moss service could not be reached or did not answer in time. |
| `DESERIALIZATION` | Index data, a snapshot or a service response could not be decoded. |
| `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` | The embedding model could not be downloaded, verified or loaded. |
| `INTERNAL` | A failure inside the SDK that the caller cannot correct. |

Each SDK exposes the code in its own form:

| SDK | Error | Code |
| - | - | - |
| Python | [`MossError`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/interfaces/MossError), a `RuntimeError`. [`InvalidArgumentError`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/interfaces/InvalidArgumentError) is its `INVALID_ARGUMENT` subclass and also a `ValueError`. | `error.code`, a string such as `"NOT_FOUND"` |
| JavaScript | An `Error` that [`isMossError`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/functions/isMossError) accepts, typed [`MossError`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/interfaces/MossError) | `error.code`, a [`MossErrorCode`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/type-aliases/MossErrorCode) |
| Browser | An `Error` with a `code` property. See [Errors](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/browser/api.md#errors). | `error.code`, a string such as `"NOT_FOUND"` |
| Elixir | [`%Moss.Error{}`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/elixir/types#error), the `reason` in `{:error, reason}` | `reason.code`, an atom such as `:not_found` |
| Swift | [`MossError`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/swift/types#mosserror) | `error.code`, an `Int32` to compare with a constant such as `MossError.notFound` |

Some errors an SDK raises before it calls the core carry no code. In Python a closed
`MossClient` raises `RuntimeError` and some argument checks raise `ValueError` or `TypeError`;
in JavaScript a closed client or session and `createIndex` with no documents throw a plain
`Error`; in the browser `queryMultiIndex([])` throws a plain `Error`. The Python and
JavaScript web source methods raise `ManageApiError`. Elixir and Swift report their own
argument checks as a `%Moss.Error{}` and a `MossError` too.

`detail` holds the core error text: diagnostic text for logs and support, at most 512 bytes,
and not a stable contract. It names the operation or host instead of a request URL, and the
file instead of an absolute path. A failed response contributes only its HTTP status and the
error code its body names, such as `HTTP 403 Forbidden: AccessDenied`.

A bulk load reports the code of each index it could not load next to the message:
`LoadIndexesResult.failed_codes` in [Python](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/interfaces/LoadIndexesResult.md)
and [Elixir](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/elixir/types.md#loadindexesresult), and `failedCodes` in
[JavaScript](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/interfaces/LoadIndexesResult.md),
[the browser](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/browser/classes/MossClient.md#loadindexes) and
[Swift](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/swift/types.md#loadindexesresult).

***

## Error reference

| Error | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| `Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid credentials | Set `MOSS_PROJECT_ID` and `MOSS_PROJECT_KEY` in your environment |
| `Cannot find native binding` | `@moss-js/moss` was installed without optional dependencies, so the native binary for your platform is missing | Reinstall with optional dependencies. See [Install](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/api.md#install) |
| `Index not found` | Querying or loading an index that doesn't exist | Call `createIndex()` first; verify the name matches exactly (case-sensitive) |
| `Index not loaded` | Calling `query()` before `loadIndex()` | Call `loadIndex(name)` before `query()`. `query()` throws if the index isn't loaded locally |
| `Index already exists` | Calling `createIndex()` on an existing index name | Use `addDocs()` with `upsert: true` to update documents, or delete the index first |
| `Missing embeddings runtime` | Invalid or unrecognised `modelId` | Use `moss-minilm`, `moss-mediumlm`, or `custom` |
| `Embedding required` | Using `modelId: 'custom'` without providing `embedding` | Supply an `embedding` array on every document and every `query()` call |
| `Job failed` | Async mutation error | Inspect `JobStatusResponse.error` via `getJobStatus(jobId)` |
| `Validation error: index name must not be blank, "." or "..", must not contain "/" or control characters, and must be at most 256 bytes` | An index name that is blank, `.` or `..`, contains `/` or a control character, or is longer than 256 bytes. The SDK rejects it before sending any request | Use a name within these rules. Pass the raw name: the SDK percent-encodes it, so an already encoded name addresses a different index. *(Python moss 1.14.0+, @moss-js/moss 1.15.0+, @moss-dev/moss-web 1.3.0+, Elixir moss 1.4.0+, Swift SDK 0.7.0+)* |
| `Unsupported chunk_size 100. Supported: 200 to 2000` (also `chunk_overlap`, `markdown_header_depth` and `mode`) | Python `Chunking(...)` got a value out of range. It raises `InvalidArgumentError` | Use `chunk_size` 200 to 2000, `chunk_overlap` 0 to half of `chunk_size`, `markdown_header_depth` 1 to 6, and `mode` `"pages"` or `"sentences"`. See [`Chunking`](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/interfaces/Chunking). *(Python moss 1.18.0+)* |
| `chunk 1 of document "faq" has 2001 characters; chunks may have at most 2000 (about 512 tokens of English, the embedding model's input limit)` | A Python `chunker` returned a chunk of more than 2,000 characters. It raises `InvalidArgumentError` | Return chunks of at most 2,000 characters from `chunker`. *(Python moss 1.18.0+)* |
| `pass chunker or chunking, not both` | Python `create_index` or `add_docs` got both `chunker=` and `chunking=`. It raises `TypeError` | Pass one of them. *(Python moss 1.18.0+)* |
| `chunker and chunking cannot be used with model_id='custom': chunks have no embeddings` | Python `create_index` with `model_id="custom"`, or `SessionIndex.add_docs` on a custom-model session, got `chunker=` or `chunking=`. It raises `ValueError` | Chunk and embed the text yourself, then pass the chunks as documents with their `embedding`, without `chunker` or `chunking`. *(Python moss 1.18.0+)* |
| `no text to index in: a.md` | A Python file or document had no text left to index after chunking, such as a markdown file with only headings. It raises `InvalidArgumentError` | Add text to the listed files or documents, or leave them out. *(Python moss 1.18.0+)* |
| `cannot chunk document "faq" because it has an embedding` | A Python document with an `embedding` was passed with `chunker=` or `chunking=`. It raises `InvalidArgumentError` | Remove `embedding` and let the model embed each chunk, or chunk the text yourself and pass the chunks with their embeddings. *(Python moss 1.18.0+)* |

***

## Common scenarios

### Search results are irrelevant

* **Try hybrid search**: lower `alpha` for more keyword matching (default is `0.8`):
  ```ts theme={null}
  await client.query('my-index', 'query text', { topK: 5, alpha: 0.5 })
  ```
* **Check document chunking**: very long documents dilute embedding signal. Keep chunks under about 1200 characters, cut at sentence boundaries - see [Chunking tips](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/indexing-data.md#chunking-tips).
* **Switch models**: try `moss-mediumlm` for higher accuracy.

***

## SDK error behaviour

* Most methods throw if the target index does not exist.
* `createIndex()` throws if the index already exists.
* `loadIndex()` throws if the index does not exist in cloud storage or loading fails. With a `cachePath` (`cache_path` in Python) and a snapshot already on disk, it serves that snapshot instead when the cloud is unreachable or answers with a temporary error, while a 401, 403 or 404 still throws. *(Python moss 1.14.0+, @moss-js/moss 1.15.0+)*

If a job reaches `"failed"`, its `JobStatusResponse.error` will be non-null. The job's `currentPhase` (see [JobPhase](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/type-aliases/JobPhase.md)) can hint at where it failed - a job stuck on `downloading` usually means a network issue.

***

## Still stuck?

* Join the [Moss Discord](https://discord.gg/eMXExuafBR) for community help
* Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/usemoss/moss)

<!-- Page: Telemetry · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/telemetry.md · local: pages/reference/telemetry.md -->

# Telemetry

> What the Moss SDKs send to Moss, when they send it, and what never leaves your device.

Every Moss SDK sends usage telemetry to the Moss service: counts, timings, versions and
identifiers that show how Moss is used. Telemetry never contains your queries or your
documents. This page lists what is sent, when, and where, and the other data that leaves the
device when you use cloud features.

Telemetry is always on.

## What is sent

Every report from an SDK client or session carries:

* Your project id.
* The kind of operation it reports, such as an index load or a batch of queries.
* A random id for the client or session that sent it, so its reports can be grouped. A
  session opened from a client may carry the client's id.
* The device id, and the user id when you set one. See [Device id and user id](#device-id-and-user-id).
* The version of the SDK and of its native core and, outside the browser, the layout version
  of the on-disk model cache.

Depending on the operation, a report may also include:

* The name of the index or session it concerns, or the names of every index in a
  multi-index query.
* The embedding model id and its exact version. Swift and C sessions also send which version
  of the session options API opened them.
* Counts: queries run, documents in an index or session, documents added, and an estimate of
  the tokens in the added documents. The estimate is computed from the length of the text,
  and the text itself is not sent.
* How long each query took, in milliseconds.
* How an index was loaded: whether a cache directory was set, whether the index came from the
  disk cache while the Moss service was unreachable, the auto-refresh setting and interval,
  whether a refresh changed the index, when the cloud copy was last updated, and whether an
  old session snapshot was rebuilt and saved again.
* The name of the on-disk cache snapshot in use, a generated name of the form
  `generation-<timestamp>-<random id>`. Never its path.

Voice agents built with `moss-agent` (Python) send the same fields without a device id. They
also send, for each [LiveKit](https://livekit.com/) call, the LiveKit room name and job id,
a random call id, and the start time, end time and duration of the call. The agent's `client_id` option sets its random
id, which then stays the same across runs.

The browser SDK (`@moss-dev/moss-web`) sends less: the project id, a random id per client, the
device id, versions, and query counts. It sends no index names, timings or model details.
Releases before `@moss-dev/moss-web` 1.4.0, or with `@moss-dev/moss-wasm` 0.16.0, send none.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Index names, session names and LiveKit room names are sent exactly as you chose them. Keep
> personal data out of them.

## What is never sent

A report's body **never** contains:

* Query text.
* Document text, metadata, payloads or embeddings.
* File paths or file contents.
* Your operating system, device model, hardware serial numbers, MAC addresses or location.

The SDKs include no third-party analytics library, and telemetry goes only to the Moss
service. Like any request, each report reaches Moss from your IP address. In the browser it
also carries the headers the browser adds to every request, such as `User-Agent`, which names
the browser and operating system.

## When it is sent

* **When an operation happens.** Loading or unloading an index, an auto-refresh, and loading,
  changing or pushing a session each send one report in the background. If it fails, it is
  not sent again, and it never fails the call that caused it.
* **While you query.** Queries are counted and reported together every few seconds while
  there is activity. A client or session with nothing new to report sends nothing.
* **When you close.** Closing a client or session sends a final report and waits until it
  arrives or 2 seconds pass. See [Releasing resources](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/releasing-resources.md).
* **While a voice agent runs.** `moss-agent` sends a heartbeat every few seconds, even when
  idle.

When the Moss service can't be reached, usage and query reports stay in memory for a limited
time and are sent again with later reports. Telemetry is never written to disk; the only thing
it stores is the device id described below.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The 2-second wait on close and the resending of usage and query reports need
> `@moss-js/moss` >= **1.16.0**, `moss` >= **1.15.0** (Python), Elixir `moss` >= **1.5.0**, the Swift
> SDK >= **0.8.0** or the C SDK >= **0.24.0**. Earlier releases drop a report that fails.

The browser SDK reports every few seconds after queries run, and once more when the page is
unloaded or navigated away from, or when you call `dispose()`. It does not resend a report
that fails.

## Where it goes

Telemetry is sent over HTTPS to `https://service.usemoss.dev/index/telemetry`, authenticated
with your project's access token. When you point the SDK at another index service, with
`MOSS_INDEX_URL` or a base URL option such as the browser SDK's `baseUrl`, telemetry goes to
`/telemetry` under that URL along with the rest of the index traffic. Changing the URL moves
telemetry; it does not stop it.

## Device id and user id

The device id identifies the device or app installation that runs the SDK. Every id Moss
creates is a random UUID. Moss never reads hardware serial numbers or MAC addresses.

| Where the SDK runs | Device id |
| - | - |
| Node.js, Python, Elixir, C | A random UUID in `.moss/.moss-device-id` in the user's home directory, created on first use |
| iOS (Swift) | The app's `identifierForVendor` from iOS, or a random UUID kept in the Keychain on this device only when iOS doesn't provide one |
| Android (Kotlin) | `Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID`, or a random UUID kept in the app's `filesDir/moss-device-id` when Android returns none |
| Browser | A random UUID in `localStorage` under `moss-device-id`, one per origin |

**Home directory.** The home directory is `$HOME`, else `%USERPROFILE%`, else the system's
home directory. The file survives restarts and SDK upgrades or reinstalls, because it lives in
the home directory and not in the package. Deleting it gives the device a new id. When the
home directory can't be found or written, each process uses a new random id.

**Cache directory.** A JavaScript, Python or Elixir client given a cache directory, as a
client option or on a load (`cachePath`, or `cache_path` in Python and Elixir), reports the id
in `.moss-device-id` inside that directory, and creates the file when it is missing. That id
lasts as long as the directory does. In C, a load given a cache directory reports the id from
that file when it is already there, but doesn't create it. The client still
creates the home-directory file, but doesn't report its id while a cache-directory id is in use.

**iOS.** iOS issues and resets `identifierForVendor` under its own rules. The Swift SDK also
sends Moss's own random id alongside it.

**Android.** Android scopes `ANDROID_ID` to the app's signing key, the user and the device, and resets it on a factory reset. Declare it under Device or other IDs in Play's Data safety form.

**Browser.** The id survives page reloads on the same origin and is cleared with the site's
data. When `localStorage` is missing or blocked, each page uses a new id, and telemetry is
still sent.

**Your own device id.** You can supply the device id yourself: `identity.deviceId` in the
JavaScript client options, or `moss_client_new_with_device_id` in C. Moss still sends its own
random id alongside yours. The Python, Swift, Android, Elixir and browser SDKs have no such option.

```typescript theme={null}
import { MossClient } from '@moss-js/moss'

const client = new MossClient(projectId, projectKey, {
  identity: { deviceId: installationId, userId: accountId },
})
```

**User id.** Only the JavaScript SDK (`@moss-js/moss`) has one: `identity.userId`, sent only
when you set it. Moss never creates a user id.

## Other data that leaves the device

Telemetry is not the only traffic. These operations send data to the Moss service because they
work with cloud indexes:

| When you | What is sent |
| - | - |
| Use a project key | The project id and key, exchanged for a short-lived access token at first use and again before it expires. With a custom authenticator, your authenticator supplies the token instead |
| Create an index, or add documents to a cloud index | Document ids, text, metadata, payloads and any embeddings you supply |
| Delete or fetch documents in a cloud index | Document ids |
| Create an index from files | The file contents and file names |
| Push a session | Every document in the session, with its id, text, metadata, payload and embedding |
| Load or refresh an index | The index name and project id. The index is downloaded to the device |
| Open a session | In Python and Elixir, and by default in Swift and C, the session name and project id, to load the cloud index with that name; when it exists, it is downloaded into the session. Opening a JavaScript session requests no index: its name goes only into usage telemetry, and the first index request is `session.loadIndex()` or `pushIndex()` |
| Load a built-in embedding model, cached or not | The model id and a one-time public key, sent to the Moss service for a short-lived key to the model. When the model isn't cached, it is also downloaded from `models.moss.link`. Loading fails while the Moss service can't be reached |
| Add a web source (JavaScript and Python) | The URL to crawl and the index name |

While idle, the browser SDK checks its access token every 30 seconds, and requests a new
one, from the project key or through your authenticator, only when it is about to expire.

**Queries never leave the device.** Every query runs on an index loaded into memory or on a
session, and its text is embedded on the device, in the browser too. There is no cloud query.
The native SDKs load a built-in model when they load an index that uses it. The browser SDK
loads it at the first text query, which then contacts the Moss service as the table above
describes.

## Related

>
> How Moss handles personal data.

> [card] [Releasing resources](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/releasing-resources.md)
>
> Close clients and sessions so the final report is sent.

# SDK Overview

> Every Moss SDK capability, with links to the detailed guide for each.

Moss ships official SDKs for seven platforms. They share one conceptual API (create or load an
index, then query) and one index format, so you can build in one and query from another.

> [card] [Python](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/api.md)
>
> Async Python SDK. `pip install moss`

> [card] [JavaScript](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/js/api.md)
>
> Node.js server-side SDK. `npm install @moss-js/moss`

> [card] [Swift (iOS)](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/swift/api.md)
>
> On-device iOS SDK via Swift Package Manager.

> [card] [Android](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/android/getting-started.md)
>
> On-device Android SDK, a Kotlin AAR.

> [card] [Elixir](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/elixir/api.md)
>
> Elixir SDK on Hex. `{:moss, "~> 1.0"}`

> [card] [Browser](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/browser/api.md)
>
> In-browser / WebAssembly SDK. `npm install @moss-dev/moss-web`

> [card] [C](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/c/getting-started.md)
>
> Native C library (libmoss).

> [!NOTE]
>
> Versions below 1.9.0 will stop loading models when the legacy download path is retired. Upgrade to 1.9.0+ before then.

## Capabilities

Everything the SDKs can do. Pick a language above for install and quickstart; follow a link
below for the details.

Links below go to the Python pages; each topic has a JavaScript equivalent under the JavaScript SDK.

| Capability | What it does | Learn more |
| - | - | - |
| Index management | Create, add, update, delete, get, and list indexes | [Indexing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/api.md#indexes) |
| Index from files | Build an index from PDF/DOCX with server-side parsing and OCR | [Index from files](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/files.md) |
| Load and query | Load an index into memory and run semantic search | [Load and query](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/api.md#load-and-query) |
| Hybrid search | Blend semantic and keyword scoring with `alpha` | [Hybrid search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/hybrid-search.md) |
| Metadata filtering | Narrow results with `$eq`, `$in`, `$near`, `$and`/`$or`, and more | [Metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md) |
| Custom embeddings | Bring your own vectors with `model_id="custom"` | [Custom embeddings](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/custom-embeddings.md) |
| Multi-index search | Query across several loaded indexes in one call, with the same `alpha` blend as a single-index query. Also in the JavaScript and Elixir SDKs | [Multi-index search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/multi-index-search.md) |
| Real-time sessions | Local-first indexing during a live interaction | [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md) |
| Cross-agent handoff | Resume a session across agents, channels, and devices | [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md) |
| Hydration and sync | Hydrate from the cloud, auto-refresh, and push updates | [Keeping indexes fresh](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/api.md#keeping-indexes-fresh) |
| Inference | Responses in the shape of OpenAI's Responses API, answered from your indexes. Every SDK has an inference client, and any OpenAI client works too, on a server or in a browser page. Direct page calls with the project key are for prototypes, local demos and internal tools; a public page calls through a route of yours, see [Keep the project key on your server](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/browser.md#keep-the-project-key-on-your-server) | [Python](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/python.md), [JavaScript](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/javascript.md), [Swift](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/swift.md), [Android](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/android.md), [Elixir](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/elixir.md), [Browser](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/browser.md), [C](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/c.md), [HTTP API](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/inference/responses.md) |

## Models

* `moss-minilm` (default) - fast, lightweight, good for edge and offline
* `moss-mediumlm` - higher accuracy with reasonable performance
* `moss-litelm` - the on-device default on iOS and Android
* `custom` - bring your own embedding vectors

## Samples

Runnable end-to-end examples live in the
[moss](https://github.com/usemoss/moss) repo, with parallel JavaScript and
Python projects you can adapt by swapping in your own data.

# Moss Python SDK overview

> Everything the Moss Python SDK can do, with a snippet for each operation.

The Moss Python SDK (`moss`) brings semantic search to Python. It wraps a high-performance
Rust core and exposes an async API. Documents are embedded and queried locally, with optional
cloud sync.

## Requirements

* Python 3.10 or higher

## Install

```bash theme={null}
pip install moss
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Versions below 1.9.0 will stop loading models when the legacy download path is retired. Upgrade to 1.9.0+ before then.

Get your project credentials from the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev).

## Two ways to search

* [`MossClient`](./classes/MossClient) - the entry point. Manage cloud indexes, load one into memory, and query it.
* [`SessionIndex`](./classes/SessionIndex) - a local, in-process index for real-time indexing during a live interaction; push to the cloud when done.

## Quick start

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import MossClient, DocumentInfo, QueryOptions

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)
    await client.create_index("faqs", [
        DocumentInfo(id="doc1", text="Track your order in your account.", metadata={"category": "shipping"}),
        DocumentInfo(id="doc2", text="30-day return policy for most items.", metadata={"category": "returns"}),
    ])
    await client.load_index("faqs")
    results = await client.query("faqs", "return a damaged product", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
    for doc in results.docs:
        print(doc.id, doc.score)

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Indexes

Create, inspect, and delete cloud indexes. Mutations run as async jobs and return a
`MutationResult` with a `job_id` and `doc_count`.

```python theme={null}
# Create (defaults to moss-minilm)
result = await client.create_index("faqs", documents)

# Inspect
info = await client.get_index("faqs")     # IndexInfo: name, doc_count, model.id, status
indexes = await client.list_indexes()      # list[IndexInfo]

# Delete
await client.delete_index("faqs")
```

## Index from files

Build an index straight from PDF and DOCX files - the server parses, chunks, and embeds
them. Up to 20 files per call.

```python theme={null}
from moss import ParseFileInput, ParseOptions

await client.create_index_from_files("contracts", [
    ParseFileInput(name="report.pdf", content_type="application/pdf", path="/docs/report.pdf"),
], parse_options=ParseOptions(ocr_mode="full_ocr"))
```

See [Index from files](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/files.md).

## Documents

Add, update, fetch, and remove documents on an existing index.

```python theme={null}
from moss import MutationOptions, GetDocumentsOptions

# Add or upsert
await client.add_docs("faqs", new_docs, MutationOptions(upsert=True))

# Fetch all, or by id
all_docs = await client.get_docs("faqs")
some = await client.get_docs("faqs", GetDocumentsOptions(doc_ids=["doc1", "doc2"]))

# Delete by id
await client.delete_docs("faqs", ["doc6", "doc7"])
```

## JSON, files and chunking

`create_index`, `add_docs` and `SessionIndex.add_docs` also take dicts, JSON array or JSON Lines
text, and `.json`, `.jsonl`, `.ndjson`, `.txt`, `.md` and `.markdown` files as
`pathlib.Path` objects. Text and markdown files are chunked into documents `{path}#{n}` with
metadata `parentId`. Tune that with `chunking=Chunking(...)`, or split text yourself with
`chunker=`. *(moss 1.18.0+)*

```python theme={null}
from pathlib import Path
from moss import Chunking

await client.create_index("faqs", Path("faqs.jsonl"))
await client.add_docs("faqs", [{"id": "doc9", "text": "30-day returns."}])
await client.create_index("handbook", Path("handbook.md"), chunking=Chunking(chunk_size=800))
```

`Chunking`, `DocsInput` and `Chunker` are exported from `moss`. See [`Chunking`](./interfaces/Chunking).

## Load and query

Load an index into memory, then query it in-process. Call `load_index` before querying.

```python theme={null}
await client.load_index("faqs")
results = await client.query("faqs", "return a damaged product", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
for doc in results.docs:
    print(doc.id, doc.score, doc.text)

await client.unload_index("faqs")   # free memory when done
```

## Hybrid search

Blend semantic and keyword scoring with `alpha` (1.0 = semantic, 0.0 = keyword; default 0.8).

```python theme={null}
await client.query("faqs", "return policy", QueryOptions(top_k=3, alpha=0.6))
```

See [Hybrid search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/hybrid-search.md).

## Metadata filtering

Narrow results by document metadata on a loaded index.

```python theme={null}
await client.query("products", "running shoes", QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={
    "$and": [
        {"field": "category", "condition": {"$eq": "shoes"}},
        {"field": "price",    "condition": {"$lt": "100"}},
    ],
}))
```

Operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$in`, `$nin`, `$near`, composed with
`$and` / `$or`. See [Metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md).

## Custom embeddings

Supply your own vectors with `model_id="custom"` (each document carries `embedding`, and
queries pass `embedding`).

```python theme={null}
await client.create_index("tickets", docs_with_embeddings, model_id="custom")
await client.load_index("tickets")
await client.query("tickets", "billing problem", QueryOptions(top_k=3, embedding=query_vector))
```

See [Custom embeddings](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/custom-embeddings.md).

## Multi-index search

Query several loaded indexes in one call; each result is tagged with its source `index_name`.

```python theme={null}
await client.load_indexes(["products", "reviews", "faqs"])
results = await client.query_multi_index(["products", "reviews", "faqs"], "battery life", QueryOptions(top_k=6))
for doc in results.docs:
    print(doc.index_name, doc.id, doc.score)
await client.unload_indexes(["products", "reviews", "faqs"])
```

See [Multi-index search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/multi-index-search.md).

## Sessions

Index and query locally in real time with a [`SessionIndex`](./classes/SessionIndex), then
push to the cloud. `session()` resumes an existing cloud index by name, or starts empty.

```python theme={null}
session = await client.session(index_name="call-123")
await session.add_docs([DocumentInfo(id="turn-1", text="Customer reported a duplicate charge.")])
hits = await session.query("billing issue", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
await session.push_index()
```

Save a session to disk and restore it in a later run with no index download.
*(moss 1.16.0+)*

```python theme={null}
await session.save_to_disk("/var/cache/my-app/moss")

# Later: skip the cloud load and restore the snapshot
session = await client.session(index_name="call-123", auto_load_on_init=False)
loaded = await session.load_from_disk("/var/cache/my-app/moss")
```

See [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md).

## Keeping indexes fresh

Auto-refresh a loaded index (poll the cloud and hot-swap newer versions in automatically),
and track async jobs.

```python theme={null}
await client.load_index("faqs", auto_refresh=True, polling_interval_in_seconds=300)
status = await client.get_job_status(result.job_id)
```

## Inference

Answer with facts from your indexes. A `MossInference` client takes the arguments of OpenAI's
`responses.create`, plus `indexes`, and returns responses with OpenAI's field names.

```python theme={null}
from moss import MossInference

llm = MossInference(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)
stream = await llm.responses.create(
    model="moss/fastlane-1",
    input="Do you ship to Canada?",
    indexes=["faqs"],
    stream=True,
)
async with stream:
    async for event in stream:
        if event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
            print(event.delta, end="")
```

See [Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/python.md).

## Errors

Every failure the native core reports raises [`MossError`](./interfaces/MossError), a
`RuntimeError` whose `code` is a stable string such as `"NOT_FOUND"` or `"NETWORK"`. Branch on
`code`, not on the message. [`InvalidArgumentError`](./interfaces/InvalidArgumentError) is the
`INVALID_ARGUMENT` subclass and is also a `ValueError`. `load_indexes` reports each failed
name's code in `failed_codes`. Checks the SDK makes before calling the core, such as a closed
client, raise plain Python exceptions with no `code`. *(moss 1.15.0+)*

```python theme={null}
from moss import MossError

try:
    results = await client.query("faqs", "refund policy")
except MossError as e:
    if e.code != "NOT_FOUND":
        raise
    await client.load_index("faqs")
    results = await client.query("faqs", "refund policy")
```

See [Error codes](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/errors.md#error-codes).

## Models

* `moss-minilm` (default) - fast, lightweight
* `moss-mediumlm` - higher accuracy
* `custom` - supply your own embedding vectors via `DocumentInfo.embedding`

## Guides

* [Index from files](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/files.md)
* [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md)
* [Hybrid search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/hybrid-search.md)
* [Metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md)
* [Custom embeddings](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/custom-embeddings.md)
* [Multi-index search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/multi-index-search.md)
* [Inference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/sdks/python.md)

## Reference

[MossClient](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/classes/MossClient.md) and [SessionIndex](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/classes/SessionIndex.md), plus all interfaces and types, are in the Reference section of the sidebar.

<!-- Page: Index from Files (Python SDK) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/files.md · local: pages/reference/python/files.md -->

# Index from Files (Python SDK)

> Create a Moss index from PDF and DOCX files in Python with server-side text extraction and configurable parsing.

`create_index_from_files` builds a new index directly from raw documents. You upload PDF and
DOCX files; the server parses them, splits them into chunks, generates embeddings, and builds
the index. The call returns when the index is ready to query.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Requires `moss` **1.7.3+**. Also available in JavaScript as
> [`createIndexFromFiles`](../js/files) (`@moss-js/moss` **1.8.0+**). `chunk_size` and `chunk_overlap` need **1.17.0+** (JavaScript **1.18.0+**).

```python theme={null}
from moss import MossClient, ParseFileInput, ParseOptions

client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

await client.create_index_from_files("contracts", [
    ParseFileInput(name="report.pdf", content_type="application/pdf", path="/docs/report.pdf"),
    ParseFileInput(
        name="manual.docx",
        content_type="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document",
        data=docx_bytes,  # raw bytes also work
    ),
], parse_options=ParseOptions(ocr_mode="full_ocr"))  # scanned documents with no text layer

# Load the new index, then query it in memory
await client.load_index("contracts")
results = await client.query("contracts", "termination clause")
```

## How it works

The call handles the full flow: it registers the files, uploads each one, and triggers
parsing, embedding, and the index build server-side. It blocks until the index is ready and
returns a [`MutationResult`](./interfaces/MutationResult). Jobs time out after 30 minutes.
There is no progress callback in Python.

## Files

Each entry is a [`ParseFileInput`](./interfaces/ParseFileInput):

| Field | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `name` | Yes | Identifier for the file. Names must be unique within the call - uploads are matched back to files by name. |
| `content_type` | Yes | `application/pdf` or `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` (DOCX). Not inferred from the file name; any other value is rejected before upload. |
| `path` | One of `path` / `data` | Filesystem path. |
| `data` | One of `path` / `data` | Raw file bytes (`bytes`). Takes precedence over `path` when both are set. |

Limits:

* 1 to 20 files per call. Each call creates a new index, and files cannot be appended to an
  existing index afterwards, so an index is built from at most 20 files.
* 50 MB per file, enforced server-side. The SDK does not pre-check size; an oversized file
  fails during the job.

## Options

* **model\_id** (`Optional[str]` = `None`) - defaults to `"moss-minilm"`; `"moss-mediumlm"`
  is also supported. `"custom"` is not supported - the server generates embeddings during
  parsing.
* **parse\_options** (Optional\[[`ParseOptions`](./interfaces/ParseOptions)] = `None`) -
  extraction controls, below.

### Parse options

All fields of [`ParseOptions`](./interfaces/ParseOptions) are optional; omitted fields use
the server defaults.

| Option | Values | What it does |
| - | - | - |
| `ocr_mode` | `"auto_ocr"` \| `"full_ocr"` | `full_ocr` forces OCR on every page, which is what scanned documents with no text layer need. `auto_ocr` runs OCR only where it looks necessary. |
| `use_high_resolution` | bool | Slower, higher-fidelity extraction. Useful for dense tables. |
| `segmentation_method` | `"smart_layout_detection"` \| `"page_by_page"` | How the document is segmented before extraction. |
| `merge_tables` | bool | Merge a table split across a page break into a single segment. |
| `chunk_size` | int (characters) | Maximum chunk length, 200-2000; default `1200`. Chunks end at `.`, `!` or `?` before a capital letter; a longer sentence is cut at spaces, or mid-word if it has none. The title prefix is not counted. *(moss 1.17.0+)* |
| `chunk_overlap` | int (characters) | Characters repeated from the end of one chunk at the start of the next, 0 to half of `chunk_size`; default `200`, or half of `chunk_size` when smaller. The overlap moves forward to a sentence start when one falls inside it, and is absent around long sentences. *(moss 1.17.0+)* |

The extraction options shape the text the parser extracts; chunking then runs over it as one stream per file.

## What gets indexed

Documents are split into chunks of up to `chunk_size` characters overlapping by up to `chunk_overlap`,
each prefixed with a title (the document's title or first heading, else the file name) that
is part of the hit text returned by `query`. Repeating page
headers, footers, page numbers, and images are excluded from the indexed text.
A scanned or
image-only document produces no readable text unless OCR runs - if a file fails with
"No readable text was found", retry with `parse_options=ParseOptions(ocr_mode="full_ocr")`.

## Querying a parse-built index

Load the index, then query it like any other index. Queries run in memory, and querying an
index that is not loaded raises `MossError` with code `NOT_FOUND`:

```python theme={null}
from moss import QueryOptions

await client.load_index("contracts")
results = await client.query("contracts", "termination clause", QueryOptions(top_k=5))
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If a text query on a parse-built index raises `InvalidArgumentError`, the index records no
> embedding model version. Keyword-only queries (`alpha=0`) and queries that pass their own
> embedding in `QueryOptions.embedding` still work.

## Errors

Passing `model_id="custom"` raises `ValueError` before anything is uploaded. Other failures
raise [`MossError`](./interfaces/MossError); `str(e)` is fixed text, `e.detail` starts with:

| `detail` starts with | Cause |
| - | - |
| `Validation error: files must not exceed 20` | More than 20 files in one call. |
| `Unsupported content type` | `content_type` is not PDF or DOCX. |
| `Validation error: Unsupported chunk_size` | `chunk_size` outside 200-2000. Rejected before upload, not clamped. |
| `Validation error: Unsupported chunk_overlap` | `chunk_overlap` negative or above half of `chunk_size` (600 when `chunk_size` is omitted). |
| `Model not allowed:` | The model is not enabled for your organization. |
| `Upload failed:` | A file could not be read or uploaded. |
| `Job failed:` | Parsing or the index build failed server-side. |
| `Job timed out after 1800 seconds` | The job exceeded the 30 minute polling ceiling. |

<!-- Page: Web Sources (Python SDK) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/web-sources.md · local: pages/reference/python/web-sources.md -->

# Web Sources (Python SDK)

> Create and resync website sources in the Moss Python SDK to keep searchable index content current.

A web source crawls a website into an index and keeps it up to date. The `MossClient` web
source methods are typed wrappers over the [`/v1/manage` web source
actions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/web-sources/createWebSource): each call goes to the Moss
cloud API with your project key, needs no index loaded locally, and works wherever the SDK
runs.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Requires `moss` **1.10.0+**. Also available in JavaScript as
> [`createWebSource`](../js/web-sources) and the other web source methods (`@moss-js/moss`
> **1.10.0+**). Crawling, manual re-sync, and scheduled refresh are plan gated; see
> [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/pricing.md).

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import JobStatus, ManageApiError, MossClient

client = MossClient(project_id, project_key)

async def wait_for_job(job_id: str) -> None:
    while True:
        job = await client.get_job_status(job_id)
        if job.status.value == JobStatus.COMPLETED:
            return
        if job.status.value == JobStatus.FAILED:
            raise RuntimeError(f"job {job_id} failed")
        await asyncio.sleep(5)

# Two sites, one index. The first call creates the index; the second adds to it.
docs = await client.create_web_source(
    "https://docs.yoursite.com", "support-kb", max_pages=500, max_depth=3, refresh_cadence="weekly"
)
blog = await client.create_web_source("https://blog.yoursite.com", "support-kb", max_pages=200)
await wait_for_job(docs.job_id)
await wait_for_job(blog.job_id)

await client.load_index("support-kb")
results = await client.query("support-kb", "how do I rotate an API key")
```

## Methods

All methods are `async` and the crawl settings are keyword-only.

| Method | Returns | What it does |
| - | - | - |
| `create_web_source(root_url, index_name, *, ...)` | `CreateWebSourceResult` | Registers the site on the index and starts a crawl. `job_id` polls the crawl. |
| `list_web_sources(index_name=None)` | `List[WebSource]` | Every source in the project, newest first, or only the sources on one index. |
| `get_web_source(source_id)` | `WebSource` | One source with its settings, schedule, and last-run stats. |
| `update_web_source(source_id, *, ...)` | `UpdateWebSourceResult` | Changes settings or cadence. With `resync=True` a crawl starts right away and `job_id` is set. |
| `resync_web_source(source_id)` | `ResyncWebSourceResult` | Re-crawls one source. `job_id` polls the crawl. |
| `delete_web_source(source_id)` | `DeleteWebSourceResult` | Removes the source and its pages. `purge_job_id` polls the removal. The index is kept. |

## Several sites on one index

* An index holds up to 20 web sources. Each root URL can be registered once per index; the
  URL with and without a trailing slash is the same source, and a repeat is refused with
  status 409.
* Each source's pages are tracked separately. A crawl or re-sync replaces only that source's
  pages, and `delete_web_source` removes only that source's pages. Other sources and
  documents added with `add_docs` are never touched.
* Crawls on the same index run one at a time. A crawl requested while another runs queues
  and starts on its own; you do not need to wait between `create_web_source` calls.
* Every source on an index uses the index's embedding model, fixed when the index is
  created.

## Create options

Keyword arguments of `create_web_source`, all optional:

| Argument | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `max_pages` | `500` | Page cap per crawl run, max `5000`. Your plan's crawl size caps it further. |
| `max_depth` | `3` | Link depth from `root_url`, max `10`. |
| `max_documents` | `50000` | Cap on indexed chunks. |
| `include_paths` | none | Only crawl matching path globs, e.g. `["/blog/*"]`. Up to 50. |
| `exclude_paths` | none | Skip matching path globs. Up to 50. |
| `respect_robots` | `True` | Honor robots.txt. |
| `parse_documents` | `True` | Parse linked PDF and DOCX files into the index (50 MB per file, 20 per run). |
| `refresh_cadence` | none | `"daily"` or `"weekly"` for scheduled re-crawls. Omit for a manual source. |
| `model_id` | `"moss-minilm"` | Or `"moss-mediumlm"`. Only used when the index is created. |

## Update options

Keyword arguments of `update_web_source`. Arguments you leave out stay unchanged; crawl
settings apply on the next crawl.

| Argument | Notes |
| - | - |
| `refresh_cadence` | `"daily"`, `"weekly"`, or `"manual"`. Changing it resets the schedule to now plus the interval. |
| `root_url` | Re-point the source. The next crawl indexes the new site and drops the old site's pages. |
| `include_paths`, `exclude_paths` | Path globs. Pass `[]` to clear. |
| `max_depth`, `max_pages` | New caps for future crawls. |
| `resync` | `True` starts a crawl after saving; the result carries `job_id`. |

Crawl settings cannot change while the source is crawling (status 409); the cadence can.
`max_documents`, `respect_robots`, and `parse_documents` are changed through the
[`updateWebSource` API action](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/api-reference/v1/web-sources/updateWebSource).

## The WebSource record

Every method except delete returns a frozen `WebSource` dataclass:

| Field | Notes |
| - | - |
| `id` | Source ID, used by the other methods. |
| `index_name`, `root_url` | The index and the registered URL (a bare origin gains a trailing slash). |
| `max_pages`, `max_documents`, `max_depth`, `include_paths`, `exclude_paths`, `respect_robots`, `parse_documents` | Crawl settings. |
| `refresh_cadence`, `next_refresh_at` | `"daily"`, `"weekly"`, or `"manual"`, and when the next scheduled run is due (`None` for manual). |
| `status` | `"crawling"` while a run is queued or active, `"idle"`, `"failed"`, or `"removing"` while a delete purges its pages. |
| `last_crawled_at`, `last_page_count`, `last_doc_count` | Stats from this source's last completed run. |
| `last_error_code` | Moss error code from the last failed run, or `None`. |

`CreateWebSourceResult` adds `job_id`. `UpdateWebSourceResult` adds `job_id` when `resync`
was `True`. `ResyncWebSourceResult` has `id`, `job_id`, and `status`. `DeleteWebSourceResult`
has `deleted`, `id`, and `purge_job_id`, which is `None` when there was nothing to purge, for
example when the index was already deleted.

## Polling jobs

Crawl and purge jobs are polled with `get_job_status(job_id)`, which returns a
[`JobStatusResponse`](./interfaces/JobStatusResponse). Its `status` is a
[`JobStatus`](./interfaces/JobStatus) object: compare `status.value` with the `JobStatus`
constants, as in the example above, rather than the object itself. `current_phase.value`
moves through `"queued"` (waiting for another crawl or build on the index), `"crawling"`,
`"parsing_documents"` when linked files were found, and `"building_index"`. A queued crawl
reports `status.value == JobStatus.BUILDING` with the phase `"queued"`.

## Errors

Every method raises `ManageApiError` with the HTTP `status` and the API's JSON error body in
the message, which includes the Moss error code.

| `status` | Error code | Cause |
| - | - | - |
| `400` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | A limit out of range, a non-public `root_url`, an unsupported `model_id`, or a 21st source on the index. |
| `403` | `PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_INCLUDED` | Scheduled refresh or manual re-sync is not on your plan. |
| `404` | `WEB_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | Unknown `source_id`. |
| `409` | `WEB_SOURCE_EXISTS` | The root URL is already registered on this index. |
| `409` | `BUILD_IN_PROGRESS` | Crawl settings changed, a re-sync requested, or a delete attempted while the source is crawling. |
| `429` | `USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | Concurrent job, crawled URL, index, or credit limits. |
| `503` | | Crawling or the plan check is temporarily unavailable. |

```python theme={null}
try:
    await client.create_web_source("https://docs.yoursite.com", "support-kb")
except ManageApiError as e:
    if e.status == 409:
        pass  # already registered on this index
    else:
        raise
```

## Environment

`MOSS_CLOUD_API_BASE_URL` overrides the API host used by the web source methods (default
`https://service.usemoss.dev`). It does not affect the client's other calls.

<!-- Page: Sessions (Python SDK) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md · local: pages/reference/python/sessions.md -->

# Sessions (Python SDK)

> Index and query locally in real time with a SessionIndex, then push to the cloud.

A session is a local, in-process index you read and write in real time, with no cloud round
trip on any operation. Sessions are how the Python SDK does indexing during a live
interaction: indexing transcript turns mid-call, building a per-user working set, or
accumulating context that is handed off between agents.

A session is a [`SessionIndex`](./classes/SessionIndex), created from
[`client.session()`](./classes/MossClient#session-index_name-model_id). For the full method
list, see the [SDK reference](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/api.md).

## Create or resume

`client.session(index_name=...)` returns a `SessionIndex`. If a cloud index with that name
already exists, it auto-loads into the session (no re-embedding); otherwise the session
starts empty. The workflow is identical in both cases, so you do not branch on whether the
index exists. Pass `auto_load_on_init=False` to skip that load and start empty, for example
to [restore the session from disk](#save-and-restore-on-disk).

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, QueryOptions

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    # Auto-loads from cloud if the index exists, starts fresh if not.
    session = await client.session(index_name="my-session-index")
    print(f"{session.doc_count} existing docs loaded")

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Mutate and query locally

`add_docs`, `delete_docs`, and `get_docs` run in-memory; `add_docs` embeds locally via the
Rust core with no network round trip. `query` also runs entirely in-memory (\~1-10 ms) and supports
the same metadata filter syntax as [`client.query()`](./classes/MossClient#query-name-query-options).

```python theme={null}
session = await client.session(index_name="call-123")

# Add or update docs - appended to whatever was loaded.
added, updated = await session.add_docs([
    DocumentInfo(id="turn-1", text="Customer reported a duplicate charge on their March invoice."),
    DocumentInfo(id="turn-2", text="Agent confirmed the refund would arrive in 3-5 business days."),
])
print(f"{added} added, {updated} updated (total: {session.doc_count})")

# Query locally.
results = await session.query("refund timeline", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
for doc in results.docs:
    print(f"{doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")

# Fetch and delete by id, all in-memory.
some = await session.get_docs()
await session.delete_docs(["turn-1"])
```

## Persist to the cloud

`push_index()` uploads the session's documents to the cloud under the session's name,
creating or replacing that index. For a built-in model the service re-embeds the text with
that model, so the pushed index answers text queries like one built with `create_index`. A
custom-model session keeps its own embeddings.

```python theme={null}
result = await session.push_index()
print(f"Pushed {result.doc_count} docs (job {result.job_id}) status={result.status}")
```

## Extend an existing index

Because `session()` resumes by name, the same code extends an index across runs. Resume,
append new documents, then push back to overwrite the cloud copy with the combined set.

```python theme={null}
session = await client.session(index_name="my-session-index")  # loads prior docs

await session.add_docs([
    DocumentInfo(id="follow-up-1", text="Customer called back to confirm the refund was received."),
    DocumentInfo(id="follow-up-2", text="Refund of $49.99 appeared on the statement within 3 days."),
])

results = await session.query("refund outcome and customer satisfaction", QueryOptions(top_k=3))
await session.push_index()   # creates or overwrites the cloud index
```

## Save and restore on disk

[`save_to_disk(cache_path)`](./classes/SessionIndex#save_to_disk-cache_path) writes the
session under `<cache_path>/<name>/`. A later session with the same name restores it with
[`load_from_disk(cache_path)`](./classes/SessionIndex#load_from_disk-cache_path-rebuild_legacy),
which returns the number of documents loaded. Open that session with
`auto_load_on_init=False`, so it skips the cloud load and the restore downloads no index.
*(moss 1.16.0+)*

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, MossError

CACHE_DIR = "/var/cache/my-app/moss"

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    # Skip the cloud load, then restore the last saved snapshot.
    session = await client.session(index_name="notes", auto_load_on_init=False)
    try:
        loaded = await session.load_from_disk(CACHE_DIR)
    except MossError as e:
        if e.code != "DESERIALIZATION":
            raise
        loaded = 0  # no snapshot yet, so the session starts empty
    print(f"{loaded} docs restored, model {session.model_id}")

    await session.add_docs([
        DocumentInfo(id="note-1", text="Customer prefers a call back on Friday."),
    ])

    # Save for the next run.
    await session.save_to_disk(CACHE_DIR)

asyncio.run(main())
```

* The snapshot replaces the session's documents and model, so `session.model_id` reports
  the snapshot's model after a load. After a custom-model snapshot loads, `add_docs` and
  `query` need embeddings.
* A missing or damaged snapshot raises `MossError` with code `DESERIALIZATION` and leaves the
  session as it was. A failed or interrupted save leaves the last saved snapshot loadable.
* A snapshot that an older core saved for a built-in model has no model artifact identity.
  By default `load_from_disk` rebuilds it for a session opened with the same model: it
  re-embeds the stored documents and saves the snapshot back in the same call, which needs
  the cloud for the model. If the model cannot be loaded, it raises `MossError` with code
  `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` and changes nothing. Pass `rebuild_legacy=False` to load such a snapshot
  as a custom-model session.
* A relative `cache_path` resolves against the current working directory, and `~` is not
  expanded.
* `cache_path` is optional. Without one, snapshots go in `sessions/<project id>/` under the
  client's `cache_path`, else under the `MOSS_SESSION_CACHE_PATH` environment variable, which
  only session snapshots read, else under `moss` in the default cache directory:
  `~/.cache/moss` on macOS and Linux, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\moss` on Windows. *(moss 1.19.0+)*

## Live-call context: short-term plus long-term

A session is short-term context - the working set for the current interaction. A persistent
cloud index loaded with [`load_index()`](./classes/MossClient#load_index-name-auto_refresh-polling_interval_in_seconds)
is long-term context - durable knowledge shared across interactions. A typical live call
loads a cloud FAQ index for long-term context and opens a session for short-term context,
then queries both for each turn.

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, QueryOptions

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    # Long-term context: a persistent cloud index, loaded for in-process queries.
    await client.load_index("support-faqs")

    # Short-term context: a session for this specific call.
    session = await client.session(index_name="call-abc")

    # As each turn arrives, index it locally (~1-5 ms).
    await session.add_docs([
        DocumentInfo(id="turn-1", text="Customer was billed twice for the same renewal."),
    ])

    # Query both for context on the current turn.
    user_turn = "why was I charged twice"
    recent = await session.query(user_turn, QueryOptions(top_k=3))          # this call
    knowledge = await client.query("support-faqs", user_turn, QueryOptions(top_k=3))  # all-time

    context = list(recent.docs) + list(knowledge.docs)
    for doc in context:
        print(f"{doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")

    # At call end, persist the session for future retrieval.
    await session.push_index()
    await client.unload_index("support-faqs")

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Behavior notes

* The session's embedding model is set by `model_id` on `session()` (default `"moss-minilm"`;
  also `"moss-mediumlm"` or `"custom"`). When resuming an existing cloud index, omit
  `model_id` to adopt the stored model - passing a different one raises a `ValueError`. All
  participants resuming the same index must use the same model.
* `session.model_id` is the model the session uses, or `"custom"`. Loading a cloud index or
  a disk snapshot moves the session to the loaded model. *(moss 1.16.0+)*
* With `model_id="custom"`, each document must carry its own `.embedding` and every query
  must pass `QueryOptions.embedding`. See [Custom embeddings](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/custom-embeddings.md).
* Project credentials are validated when the session is opened; `session()` raises if they
  are invalid.
* `close()` sends the final usage report and frees the session's memory, and
  `async with await client.session(...) as session:` calls it for you. `client.close()`
  also closes every session the client opened. Requires `moss` >= **1.15.0**. See
  [Releasing resources](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/releasing-resources.md).

<!-- Page: Hybrid search (Python SDK) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/hybrid-search.md · local: pages/reference/python/hybrid-search.md -->

# Hybrid search (Python SDK)

> Configure hybrid semantic and keyword search with the alpha parameter in the Moss Python SDK.

Semantic (vector) search captures meaning; keyword (BM25) search captures exact terms.
Hybrid search blends both with one parameter, `alpha`, set on
[`QueryOptions`](./interfaces/QueryOptions). As with all queries, load the index first with
[`load_index()`](./classes/MossClient#load_index-name-auto_refresh-polling_interval_in_seconds)
(or open a [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md)).

## The `alpha` parameter

| `alpha` | Behavior |
| - | - |
| `1.0` | Pure semantic (embeddings only) |
| `0.0` | Pure keyword (BM25 only) |
| between | Blends the two; default is semantic-heavy at `0.8` |

## Example

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import MossClient, QueryOptions

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)
    await client.load_index("faqs")   # required before querying

    # Blend semantic and keyword scoring (60/40).
    hybrid = await client.query("faqs", "return policy", QueryOptions(top_k=3, alpha=0.6))

    # Pure keyword.
    keyword_only = await client.query("faqs", "return policy", QueryOptions(top_k=3, alpha=0.0))

    # Pure semantic (the default leans here at 0.8).
    semantic_only = await client.query("faqs", "return policy", QueryOptions(top_k=3, alpha=1.0))

    for doc in hybrid.docs:
        print(f"{doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

`alpha` also applies inside a [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md) query and composes with
[metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md):

```python theme={null}
session = await client.session(index_name="call-123")
await session.query("billing dispute", QueryOptions(top_k=3, alpha=0.6))
```

## Choosing alpha

* Lower `alpha` (toward keyword) when queries contain exact identifiers, SKUs, names, or jargon.
* Higher `alpha` (toward semantic) when queries are natural-language paraphrases.
* Tune per index and per intent (returns, billing, onboarding, and so on).

## Behavior notes

* If you omit `alpha`, it defaults to `0.8`.
* `alpha` works the same way for [multi-index search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/multi-index-search.md).

## Related

> [card] [Metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md)
>
> Constrain results by document metadata.

> [card] [Custom embeddings](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/custom-embeddings.md)
>
> Bring your own vectors.

<!-- Page: Metadata filtering (Python SDK) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md · local: pages/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md -->

# Metadata filtering (Python SDK)

> Narrow query results to documents whose metadata matches a filter.

Attach metadata to documents at index time, then constrain queries to the documents whose
metadata matches a filter passed as [`QueryOptions.filter`](./interfaces/QueryOptions).
Filtering is evaluated on the locally loaded index, so call
[`load_index()`](./classes/MossClient#load_index-name-auto_refresh-polling_interval_in_seconds)
(or open a [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md)) before querying with a filter.

## Operators

| Operator | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `$eq`, `$ne` | equals / not equals |
| `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte` | greater than, greater than or equal to, less than, less than or equal to. See [how ranges compare](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/metadata-filtering.md#how-ranges-compare) |
| `$in`, `$nin` | value in / not in a list |
| `$near` | within a haversine distance of a point: `"lat,lng,radiusMeters"` |

Compose multiple conditions with `$and` / `$or` (nestable). A single condition can be passed
on its own without a wrapper.

Metadata values are strings. Filter values can be `str`, `int` or `float`; a `datetime`
raises `TypeError`.

Dicts and JSON passed to `create_index` or `add_docs` may also hold number and boolean metadata
values. They are stored as strings: `30` becomes `"30"`, and a boolean becomes `"true"` or
`"false"`. Filter booleans with those strings, such as `{"$eq": "true"}`, not with Python
`True`. *(moss 1.18.0+)*

## On a loaded index

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, QueryOptions

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    docs = [
        DocumentInfo(id="doc1", text="Running shoes with breathable mesh for daily training.",
                     metadata={"category": "shoes", "price": "79", "city": "new-york",
                               "location": "40.7580,-73.9855"}),
        DocumentInfo(id="doc2", text="Trail running shoes built for rocky terrain.",
                     metadata={"category": "shoes", "price": "149", "city": "seattle",
                               "location": "47.6062,-122.3321"}),
        DocumentInfo(id="doc3", text="Lightweight city backpack with laptop compartment.",
                     metadata={"category": "bags", "price": "95", "city": "new-york",
                               "location": "40.7505,-73.9934"}),
    ]

    index = f"catalog-{datetime.now():%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}"
    await client.create_index(index, docs)
    await client.load_index(index)   # required before filtering

    # $eq - a single condition needs no wrapper.
    await client.query(index, "running gear",
        QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={"field": "category", "condition": {"$eq": "shoes"}}))

    # $and - shoes under $100.
    await client.query(index, "running shoes",
        QueryOptions(top_k=5, alpha=0.6, filter={"$and": [
            {"field": "category", "condition": {"$eq": "shoes"}},
            {"field": "price",    "condition": {"$lt": "100"}},
        ]}))

    # $in - city in a set.
    await client.query(index, "city essentials",
        QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={"field": "city", "condition": {"$in": ["new-york"]}}))

    # $near - within 5km of Times Square.
    await client.query(index, "city products",
        QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={"field": "location",
                                      "condition": {"$near": "40.7580,-73.9855,5000"}}))

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Inside a session

A [session](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md) query takes the same filter syntax, evaluated in-memory against the
local session index. The example below indexes a call transcript and applies a range of
operators.

```python theme={null}
session = await client.session(index_name="call-123")
await session.add_docs([
    DocumentInfo(id="t1", text="Customer opened the call about an incorrect charge.",
                 metadata={"speaker": "agent", "topic": "billing", "priority": "3"}),
    DocumentInfo(id="t2", text="I need a full refund for the duplicate charge of $49.99.",
                 metadata={"speaker": "customer", "topic": "refund", "priority": "5"}),
    DocumentInfo(id="t3", text="The refund will be processed within 3 to 5 business days.",
                 metadata={"speaker": "agent", "topic": "refund", "priority": "4"}),
])

# $eq - customer turns only.
await session.query("what did the customer say",
    QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={"field": "speaker", "condition": {"$eq": "customer"}}))

# $ne - exclude agent turns.
await session.query("what was discussed",
    QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={"field": "speaker", "condition": {"$ne": "agent"}}))

# $gt - priority > 3.
await session.query("urgent issues",
    QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={"field": "priority", "condition": {"$gt": "3"}}))

# $or - refund or upgrade topics.
await session.query("account changes",
    QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter={"$or": [
        {"field": "topic", "condition": {"$eq": "refund"}},
        {"field": "topic", "condition": {"$eq": "upgrade"}},
    ]}))
```

## Date ranges

Store dates as Unix epoch seconds in a decimal string and filter with integers, so both
sides compare as numbers. [Filter by date](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/integrate/metadata-filtering.md#filter-by-date)
explains the encoding and the pitfalls of ISO 8601 strings.

```python theme={null}
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from moss import GetDocumentsOptions

created = datetime(2026, 1, 10, 9, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
timestamp_str = str(int(created.timestamp()))
await session.add_docs(
    [
        DocumentInfo(
            id="t4",
            text="Customer confirmed the refund arrived.",
            metadata={"created_at": timestamp_str},
        ),
    ]
)

january = {
    "$and": [
        # 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-01-31T23:59:59Z
        {"field": "created_at", "condition": {"$gte": 1767225600}},
        {"field": "created_at", "condition": {"$lte": 1769903999}},
    ]
}
await session.query("refund", QueryOptions(top_k=5, filter=january))

# Every match, oldest first, with no ranking (sessions only).
await session.get_docs(GetDocumentsOptions(filter=january, sort_by="created_at"))
```

## Related

>
> Blend semantic and keyword scoring.

> [card] [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md)
>

<!-- Page: Exact / Graph Retrieval (Python SDK) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/graph-retrieval.md · local: pages/reference/python/graph-retrieval.md -->

# Exact / Graph Retrieval (Python SDK)

> Deterministic fetch by id or metadata, sorting, and parent grouping on a session.

Alongside semantic [`query`](./api), a [`SessionIndex`](./classes/SessionIndex)
supports **deterministic retrieval** — exact lookups that run with *no embedding
and no similarity ranking*. Use it when you know precisely which documents you
want: fetch by id, filter by metadata, and group chunks back into their parent
unit. All of it runs locally on the session.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Requires `moss` **1.6.0+** (which pulls `inferedge-moss-core` `0.19.0`). This is
> the Python counterpart to the [Swift exact/graph retrieval](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/swift/graph-retrieval.md)
> surface.

In the examples below, `session` is a [`SessionIndex`](./classes/SessionIndex)
opened with `session = await client.session(index_name, model_id=...)`. The
deterministic fetches are configured through
[`GetDocumentsOptions`](./interfaces/GetDocumentsOptions) passed to
`session.get_docs`; parent grouping is also available on semantic
`session.query` via [`QueryOptions.group_by`](./interfaces/QueryOptions).

## Fetch by id (exact, ordered)

Returns documents in the **exact order requested**; missing ids are skipped.

```python theme={null}
from moss import GetDocumentsOptions

docs = await session.get_docs(GetDocumentsOptions(doc_ids=["doc_42", "doc_17", "doc_88"]))
# -> [doc_42, doc_17, doc_88], minus any id that doesn't exist
```

## Fetch by metadata (filter + sort)

Pass a `filter` — the same dict shape used for [metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md)
on queries — to fetch every matching document, with no query vector and no
ranking. `sort_by` orders by a metadata field (numeric-aware); `ascending`
defaults to `True`.

```python theme={null}
# Every published doc, newest first.
published = await session.get_docs(GetDocumentsOptions(
    filter={"field": "status", "condition": {"$eq": "published"}},
    sort_by="updated_at",
    ascending=False,
))

# Compose with $and / $or, numeric-aware comparisons, $in, $near — same as queries.
shoes = await session.get_docs(GetDocumentsOptions(
    filter={"$and": [
        {"field": "category", "condition": {"$eq": "shoes"}},
        {"field": "price", "condition": {"$lt": "100"}},
    ]},
    sort_by="price",
))
```

## Group chunks into their parent record

When a logical record (a long document, an article, a transcript) is stored as
several sibling chunks that share a parent id,
[`ParentGrouping`](./interfaces/ParentGrouping) collapses them into one result —
sibling text assembled in `order_field` order (numeric-aware), the best score
kept.

```python theme={null}
from moss import GetDocumentsOptions, ParentGrouping

articles = await session.get_docs(GetDocumentsOptions(
    filter={"field": "kind", "condition": {"$eq": "chunk"}},
    group_by=ParentGrouping("article_id", "chunk_index"),
))
# One document per article_id; .text is the chunks joined in chunk_index order.
```

Grouping also works on semantic `query` via
[`QueryOptions.group_by`](./interfaces/QueryOptions), which collapses sibling
hits into one result per record:

```python theme={null}
from moss import QueryOptions, ParentGrouping

result = await session.query("how vector search works", QueryOptions(
    top_k=5,
    group_by=ParentGrouping("article_id", "chunk_index"),
))
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> For **complete** records, prefer `get_docs(..., group_by=...)` — it groups over
> the full matching set. On the semantic `query` path, grouping over-fetches
> candidates and returns `top_k` records, but a record whose siblings fall outside
> the fetched window may still be partially assembled; raise `top_k` for wider
> coverage.

## Mixing exact and semantic

There's no blended call — run the two and combine. A common pattern: semantic
`query` to rank candidates, then `get_docs(doc_ids=...)` to pull the exact,
fully-populated records (with [payloads](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/structured-payload.md)) for the winners.

```python theme={null}
ranked = await session.query("waterproof hiking boots", QueryOptions(top_k=10))
ids = [d.id for d in ranked.docs]
full = await session.get_docs(GetDocumentsOptions(doc_ids=ids))  # exact order
```

## Related

> [card] [Structured payload](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/structured-payload.md)
>
> Carry the full verbatim record alongside the embedded text.

> [card] [Metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md)
>
> The filter dict shape, shared with queries.

<!-- Page: Custom embeddings (Python SDK) · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/custom-embeddings.md · local: pages/reference/python/custom-embeddings.md -->

# Custom embeddings (Python SDK)

> Use caller-provided document and query embeddings with cloud indexes and sessions in the Moss Python SDK.

Moss embeds text on-device with built-in models (`moss-minilm`, `moss-mediumlm`). If you
already generate embeddings elsewhere - a proprietary model, a hosted embedding API, or a
shared pipeline across services - use `model_id="custom"` to supply your own vectors. Moss
indexes and searches them; it does not load a local model. This works for both cloud indexes
and [sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md).

## How it works

* At index time, every document must carry its own `embedding`. With `model_id="custom"`,
  Moss does not embed for you. (If you omit `model_id` and every document has an `embedding`,
  Moss infers `"custom"` automatically; mixed documents are rejected.)
* At query time, you must pass the query vector via
  [`QueryOptions.embedding`](./interfaces/QueryOptions), because there is no local model to
  embed the query text.
* All vectors must share the same dimensionality.

## On a cloud index

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient, QueryOptions

def embed(text: str) -> list[float]:
    """Your embedding function - any model, as long as dimensions are consistent."""
    ...

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    # Index with precomputed vectors. model_id="custom" means Moss does not embed.
    docs = [
        DocumentInfo(id="1", text="Customer asked about billing", embedding=embed("Customer asked about billing")),
        DocumentInfo(id="2", text="Refund requested for duplicate charge", embedding=embed("Refund requested for duplicate charge")),
    ]
    await client.create_index("tickets", docs, model_id="custom")
    await client.load_index("tickets")   # required before querying

    # Query with your own query vector (required for custom embeddings).
    q = embed("billing problem")
    results = await client.query("tickets", "billing problem", QueryOptions(top_k=3, embedding=q))
    for doc in results.docs:
        print(f"{doc.id} score={doc.score:.3f} {doc.text}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

## In a session

Sessions support custom embeddings too: open the session with `model_id="custom"`, set
`.embedding` on every document you add, and pass `QueryOptions.embedding` on every query.

```python theme={null}
session = await client.session(index_name="conv-123", model_id="custom")
await session.add_docs([DocumentInfo(id="1", text="Customer asked about billing", embedding=embed("Customer asked about billing"))])
results = await session.query("billing problem", QueryOptions(top_k=3, embedding=embed("billing problem")))
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> With `model_id="custom"`, adding a document without `.embedding`, or querying without
> `QueryOptions.embedding`, raises a `ValueError`.

## Related

> [card] [Hybrid search](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/hybrid-search.md)
>
> Blend semantic and keyword scoring.

> [card] [Sessions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/sessions.md)
>
> Use custom vectors in a live local index.

<!-- Page: Structured payload · https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/structured-payload.md · local: pages/reference/python/structured-payload.md -->

# Structured payload

> Attach an opaque structured record to a document, stored and returned verbatim.

Each document can carry an optional `payload` — an opaque string (typically JSON) that Moss
stores and returns **unchanged**. It is never embedded or searched; it's the place for the
full structured record behind the embeddable `text` (the source row, a nested object,
anything you can serialize). Use `metadata` for the flat fields you filter on, and `payload`
for the complete record you want back verbatim.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Requires `moss` **1.5.0+** (which pulls `inferedge-moss-core` `0.18.0`). Older indexes built
> without a payload return `payload = None`; no migration is needed.

## How it works

* Set `payload` (a `str`) on a [`DocumentInfo`](./interfaces/DocumentInfo) when you build or
  add documents. Moss carries it through the upload/build pipeline and persists it alongside
  `text` and `metadata`.
* It comes back on [`get_docs()`](./classes/MossClient#get_docs-name-options) and on query
  results ([`QueryResultDocumentInfo.payload`](./interfaces/QueryResultDocumentInfo)).
* Moss treats it as an opaque string — it does not parse or validate it. Serialize/deserialize it
  yourself (e.g. `json.dumps` / `json.loads`).

## On a cloud index

```python theme={null}
import asyncio
import json
from moss import DocumentInfo, MossClient

async def main():
    client = MossClient(MOSS_PROJECT_ID, MOSS_PROJECT_KEY)

    # The full structured record travels in `payload`; `text` is what gets embedded.
    docs = [
        DocumentInfo(
            id="ticket-42",
            text="Customer asked about a duplicate billing charge.",          # embedded + searched
            metadata={"status": "open", "priority": "high"},                  # filterable
            payload=json.dumps({                                              # verbatim record
                "customer": {"id": "c_1", "tier": "pro"},
                "amount": 19.0,
                "tags": ["billing", "refund"],
            }),
        ),
    ]
    await client.create_index("tickets", docs, model_id="moss-minilm")

    # Read the documents back — payload returns exactly as stored.
    fetched = await client.get_docs("tickets")
    record = json.loads(fetched[0].payload)
    print(record["customer"]["tier"])   # -> "pro"

    # Payload is also present on query hits.
    await client.load_index("tickets")
    results = await client.query("tickets", "billing problem")
    top = results.docs[0]
    if top.payload:
        print(json.loads(top.payload)["tags"])   # -> ["billing", "refund"]

asyncio.run(main())
```

You can set `payload` the same way on [`add_docs()`](./classes/MossClient#add_docs-name-docs-options)
to append documents to an existing index.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `payload` is independent of `metadata`. Keep the fields you filter or sort on in `metadata`
> (string key/values); use `payload` for the larger or nested record you only need to retrieve.

## Related

> [card] [Metadata filtering](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/metadata-filtering.md)
>
> Filter results by the flat fields you store in `metadata`.

> [card] [DocumentInfo](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/reference/python/interfaces/DocumentInfo.md)
>
> The document shape, including `payload`.
